items.body:
## Overview

Implements adaptive mtp with a new option `--spec-type draft-mtp-adaptive`

Suggested configuration to use is: `--spec-type draft-mtp-adaptive --spec-draft-n-max 12`

The algorithm is a counting based state machine with a climb counter and a weighted drop-pressure accumulator. The depth climbs one step after a number consecutive verifies that accepted every drafted token; any miss adds (N - acceptance) to the drop pressure and the depth drops one step once it exceeds a certain amount. High depths fall quickly (a total miss adds N), low depths hold, and at the floor no pressure accumulates at all.  The specific climb difficulty and drop pressure values were empirically determined over a wide range of tests.

`--spec-draft-n-max` bounds the upper adaptive range and both the floor and the cold-start depth default to 3.  The default floor of 3 may be adjusted  with `--spec-draft-n-min-adpative`, although in testing 3 seems to be the best value to choose here.

As higher depths are reached the barrier to climb higher is reduced.  This allows for predictive runs to quickly ascend after they've "proven" themselves.

## Testing and Performance Results

Model: Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 on 2x Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, ROCm).
Configs: plain `draft-mtp` with `--spec-draft-n-max 2` and `3`, and `draft-mtp-adaptive`
with `--spec-draft-n-max 12` (controller starts at the configured `--spec-draft-n-min-adaptive`
floor of 2 or 3 and adjusts on its own). Temperature 0.6, top-k 20, top-p 0.95, min-p 0.001,
8 threads, ctx 8192, 2 seeds per cell.

Tasks (realistic output lengths):
- prose / hard prose: "write a 1000-word essay ...", capped at 1600 tokens (the model
  generated the full 1600 in every run)
- coding: a mid-file C++ benchmark program (merge sort vs heap sort vs std::sort) to
  complete, ~750-800 tokens of generated continuation



### Throughput

| spec config | prompt | tokens/s (mean) | tokens/s (range) | draft accept | mean draft len | depth reached |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fixed depth 2 | coding | 67.2 | 67.2-67.3 | 92.2% | 2.0 | - |
| fixed depth 3 | coding | 78.8 | 78.5-79.0 | 86.8% | 3.0 | - |
| adaptive (n_max 12, floor 2) | coding | **86.4** | 86.2-86.5 | 58.4% | 8.0 | 2 -> 10..11 |
| adaptive (n_max 12, floor 3) | coding | 85.3 | 83.7-86.9 | 59.3% | 7.5 | 3 -> 9..12 |
| fixed depth 2 | prose | 53.3 | 51.3-55.3 | 62.1% | 2.0 | - |
| fixed depth 3 | prose | **56.4** | 52.5-60.3 | 52.2% | 3.0 | - |
| adaptive (n_max 12, floor 2) | prose | 54.4 | 50.4-58.3 | 54.8% | 2.8 | 2 -> 3..4 |
| adaptive (n_max 12, floor 3) | prose | 54.8 | 51.2-58.5 | 51.4% | 3.2 | 3 -> 4..5 |
| fixed depth 2 | hard prose | 51.2 | 51.1-51.2 | 57.8% | 2.0 | - |
| fixed depth 3 | hard prose | **52.6** | 52.6-52.6 | 46.7% | 3.0 | - |
| adaptive (n_max 12, floor 2) | hard prose | 51.0 | 50.8-51.1 | 51.8% | 2.6 | 2 -> 3 |
| adaptive (n_max 12, floor 3) | hard prose | 51.3 | 51.1-51.4 | 46.7% | 3.1 | 3 -> 4 |

Console logs for the above runs 
[prfinal-console-all.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31147070/prfinal-console-all.txt)

### Demonstration of content replay speedups

It's difficult to fully capture and show the moments where the model is recalling content from memory, or regenerating code where predictions really spike.  

The following shows the console log from the coding output from a long Web coding session prompt.  When the Qwen3.8-27B model is recalling code generated from its thought process, we can see it spiking well above 100 t/s.  This demonstrates the capability of the adaptive MTP to take full advantage of such opportunities.   This system typically sustains around 30-35t/s for non-MTP generation, so the following hopefully demonstrates the capacity for amazing speed gains.

### Name and Version

llama-server --version

version: 10194 (e1a1abb78)
built with GNU 11.5.0 for Linux x86_64

git commit:
e1a1abb78746c025f5e9039f590e37ccdb758ae7

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 5950X
RAM: 128 GB DDR4-3200
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 Founders Edition, 24 GB VRAM
NVIDIA driver: 550.163.01
CUDA: 12.4
Compute capability: 8.9

### Models

Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
Quantization: UD-Q4_K_XL

GGUF metadata:
general.architecture = qwen35
qwen35.block_count = 65
qwen35.context_length = 262144
qwen35.embedding_length = 5120
qwen35.feed_forward_length = 17408
qwen35.attention.head_count = 24
qwen35.attention.head_count_kv = 4
qwen35.nextn_predict_layers = 1

Multimodal projector:
mmproj-BF16.gguf

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I reproduced a native MTP VRAM allocation problem on a clean llama.cpp b10194 build.

Hardware:
- RTX 4090 24 GB
- Ryzen 9 5950X
- 128 GB RAM
- CUDA 12.4
- Linux

Model:
Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf

Configuration:
- context: 196608
- KV cache: q4_0 / q4_0
- parallel: 1
- native `draft-mtp`
- `--spec-draft-n-max 2`
- all model/MTP layers on GPU

With clean b10194, the target context loads, but creation of the native MTP draft context fails because it tries to reserve an additional CUDA compute buffer.

Baseline A0:

`n_ubatch = 512`

The MTP context attempts:

`allocating 1040.28 MiB on device 0`

and fails with:

`cudaMalloc failed: out of memory`
`failed to allocate compute pp buffers`
`failed to create MTP context`

I then made one isolated change: cap only the MTP compute micro-batch from 512 to 32 while keeping `n_batch` unchanged.

A1:

`n_batch=2048 n_ubatch=512->32`

This reduces the requested MTP compute allocation to:

`785.27 MiB`

but it still fails with CUDA OOM.

I then tested a proof-of-concept where the target and MTP contexts keep independent backend schedulers, but share the backing ggml gallocr / CUDA compute arena.

I initially tried sharing the entire scheduler, but that is not valid and caused a backend identity assertion. The working implementation shares only the backing allocator while keeping both schedulers independent.

With the shared-gallocr implementation:

- model loads successfully
- native MTP remains on GPU
- context remains 196608
- KV remains q4_0
- llama-server process VRAM after generation: 22038 MiB
- generation: 61.80 tokens/s
- draft tokens generated: 152
- draft tokens accepted: 96
- draft acceptance: 63.16%
- mean draft length: 2.26
- graphs reused: 1

The proof-of-concept does not share scheduler state or backend scheduling decisions between the target and MTP contexts. Each context retains its own scheduler; only the backing graph allocator / compute workspace is shared.

The relevant runtime messages are:

`Q38F_SHARED_GALLOC: MTP eligible; target/MTP schedulers stay independent`

`sched_reserve: Q38F_SHARED_GALLOC sharing target compute arena`

followed by:

`model loaded`

`listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080`

This suggests that for sequential target/MTP execution (`--parallel 1`), reserving independent backing compute arenas is unnecessarily expensive. The schedulers can remain independent while sharing the backing graph allocator / compute workspace.

I am presenting the shared-gallocr implementation as a proof of the allocation issue, not as a claim that this is necessarily the final upstream design.

I created a standalone proof-of-concept patch against clean b10194. It applies cleanly to a second detached b10194 worktree using `git apply --check`.

Reproduction command:

    build/bin/llama-server \
      -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
      --mmproj mmproj-BF16.gguf \
      --no-mmproj-offload \
      -ngl 999 \
      -c 196608 \
      --cache-type-k q4_0 \
      --cache-type-v q4_0 \
      --flash-attn on \
      --parallel 1 \
      --spec-type draft-mtp \
      --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
      --spec-draft-type-k q4_0 \
      --spec-draft-type-v q4_0 \
      --spec-draft-ngl all \
      --metrics

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected.

The issue was reproduced on a clean b10194 checkout:

e1a1abb78746c025f5e9039f590e37ccdb758ae7

I am not claiming that this commit introduced the behavior.

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Clean b10194 - baseline MTP OOM</summary>

```console
common_speculative_init_result: creating MTP draft context against the target model
ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating 1040.28 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
ggml_gallocr_reserve_n_impl: failed to allocate CUDA0 buffer of size 1090814080
graph_reserve: failed to allocate compute buffers
llama_init_from_model: failed to initialize the context: failed to allocate compute pp buffers
common_speculative_init_result: failed to create MTP context
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>MTP n_ubatch=32 - still OOM</summary>

```console
common_speculative_init_result: CLEAN_MTP_UBATCH_CAP n_batch=2048 n_ubatch=512->32
common_speculative_init_result: creating MTP draft context against the target model
ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating 785.27 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
ggml_gallocr_reserve_n_impl: failed to allocate CUDA0 buffer of size 823411840
graph_reserve: failed to allocate compute buffers
common_speculative_init_result: failed to create MTP context
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Shared gallocr POC - working</summary>

```console
common_speculative_init_result: CLEAN_MTP_UBATCH_CAP n_batch=2048 n_ubatch=512->32
Q38F_SHARED_GALLOC: MTP eligible; target/MTP schedulers stay independent
sched_reserve: Q38F_SHARED_GALLOC sharing target compute arena

llama_server: model loaded
llama_server: listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080

prompt eval time = 489.92 ms / 62 tokens (126.55 tokens/s)
eval time = 2783.30 ms / 172 tokens (61.80 tokens/s)
graphs reused = 1
draft acceptance = 0.63158 (96 accepted / 152 generated), mean len = 2.26

llama-server VRAM after generation:
22038 MiB
```

### Name and Version

`llama-server` / `llama-bench`, commit `666f889` (build 304), built with ROCm 6.3.1 on Fedora 44

### Operating systems

Linux (Fedora 44, kernel 7.1.8)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

HIP backend (GGML_HIP)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

**Short version:** ROCm 7.x (7.1.1 on Fedora 44) segfaults in `libamd_comgr` when compiling kernels for RDNA2 (gfx1030). AMD's ROCm 7.2 release notes drop RDNA2 entirely. However, **ROCm 6.3.1 installed side-by-side works perfectly** on the same system — restoring full MTP throughput (~46 t/s on a 27B model) without any OS downgrade. This is a reproducible recipe for other RDNA2 (RX 6000 series) users.

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT (gfx1030, RDNA2, Navi21) |
| CPU | Intel i9-12900K |
| OS | Fedora 44 (kernel 7.1.8-200.fc44) |
| System ROCm | 7.1.1 (Fedora package) — **broken on gfx1030** |
| Side-by-side ROCm | 6.3.1 (extracted from Fedora 42 archive) — **works** |
| llama.cpp | `666f889` (build 304) |

### The problem: ROCm 7.x comgr segfault on gfx1030

With system ROCm 7.1.1, any HIP build of llama.cpp crashes during model load:

```
ggml_cuda_init: found 1 ROCm devices (Total VRAM: 16368 MiB):
  Device 0: AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT, gfx1030 (0x1030), VMM: no, Wave Size: 32, VRAM: 16368 MiB
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

dmesg pinpoints it:

```
segfault ... in libamd_comgr.so.3.0
```

`libamd_comgr` is AMD's code-object compiler. It crashes deterministically while generating device code for gfx1030 under ROCm 7.1. There is no newer comgr in Fedora's repos, AMD's official ROCm 7.2 release notes do not list any RDNA2 GPU, and AMD's own prebuilt llama.cpp artifacts only target gfx110X/115X/120X. **AMD has effectively abandoned RDNA2 in the 7.x line with no fix available.**

### The fix: side-by-side ROCm 6.3.1 (no OS downgrade)

ROCm 6.3.1 (the last version with solid gfx1030 support) can be installed alongside 7.x without touching the system packages:

1. **Download the F42 ROCm 6.3.1 RPMs** (Fedora archives them via `dnf --releasever=42`):
   ```bash
   sudo dnf --releasever=42 --disablerepo="*" --enablerepo=fedora,updates download \
     --destdir=. rocm-hip-6.3.1-4.fc42 rocm-hip-devel-6.3.1-4.fc42 \
     rocm-comgr-18-37.rocm6.3.1.fc42 rocm-comgr-devel-18-37.rocm6.3.1.fc42 \
     rocm-llvm-18-37.rocm6.3.1.fc42 rocm-llvm-devel-18-37.rocm6.3.1.fc42 \
     rocm-llvm-libs-18-37.rocm6.3.1.fc42 rocm-device-libs-18-37.rocm6.3.1.fc42 \
     rocm-core-6.3.1-2.fc42 rocm-core-devel-6.3.1-2.fc42 rocminfo-6.3.0-2.fc42 \
     hipblas-6.3.0-4.fc42 hipblas-devel-6.3.0-4.fc42 rocblas-6.3.0-4.fc42 \
     rocblas-devel-6.3.0-4.fc42 hipblaslt-6.3.1-4.fc42 hipblaslt-devel-6.3.1-4.fc42 \
     rocm-llvm-filesystem-18-37.rocm6.3.1.fc42 rocm-runtime-6.3.1-4.fc42 \
     rocm-runtime-devel-6.3.1-4.fc42 hipcc-18-37.rocm6.3.1.fc42
   ```

2. **Extract them side-by-side (no install):**
   ```bash
   sudo mkdir -p /opt/rocm-6.3
   cd <rpm dir> && for f in *.x86_64.rpm; do
     sudo rpm2cpio "$f" | sudo cpio -idm --no-absolute-filenames -D /opt/rocm-6.3
   done
   ```
   (Extract only the `x86_64` RPMs last — the i686 variants can clobber symlinks.)

3. **The HIP compiler:** Fedora's `rocm-llvm` package does not ship a standalone `clang` binary; use the one from the *system* ROCm 7.1 install — it is era-appropriate (clang 20.0.0.rocm) and works fine:
   ```bash
   export HIP_CLANG_PATH=/usr/lib64/rocm/llvm/bin
   ```

4. **Additive versioned symlinks** so llama.cpp's CMake finds the 6.3 libs at the F42-style paths (the system 7.1 libs use different version numbers, so this is additive and safe):
   ```bash
   sudo ln -sf /opt/rocm-6.3/usr/lib64/libhipblas.so.2.3 /usr/lib64/libhipblas.so.2.3
   sudo ln -sf /opt/rocm-6.3/usr/lib64/librocblas.so.4.3 /usr/lib64/librocblas.so.4.3
   ```

5. **Configure and build:**
   ```bash
   export ROCM_PATH=/opt/rocm-6.3/usr
   export HIP_PATH=/opt/rocm-6.3/usr
   export PATH=/opt/rocm-6.3/usr/bin:$PATH
   cmake -S . -B build-hip63 -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1030 \
         -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLLAMA_CURL=ON \
         -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/rocm-6.3/usr \
         -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=/usr/lib64/rocm/llvm/bin/clang
   cmake --build build-hip63 -j24
   ```

6. **Runtime env vars** (needed for rocblas TensileLibrary and the 6.3 libs):
   ```bash
   export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/rocm-6.3/usr/lib64
   export ROCBLAS_TENSILE_LIBPATH=/opt/rocm-6.3/usr/lib64/rocblas/library
   ```

### Results

| Config | t/s (MTP, 27B IQ4_XS) |
|---|---|
| ROCm 7.1.1 (system) | segfault — unusable |
| ROCm 6.3.1 side-by-side | **~46 t/s** (sustained 1500-token gen: 39-47 t/s) |
| Original F42 + ROCm 6.3.1 baseline (reference) | 46.8 t/s |

Stable across a reboot (systemd unit auto-starts with env vars), sustained load (6 sequential queries, 1500-token generation), temps 44-54 C, zero GPU faults.

### Notes / gotchas

- **VRAM is the real ceiling at 16 GB**: 27B IQ4_XS (14.6 GB) + 16K KV + MTP draft + vision projector sits at ~99.9% VRAM. It works, but the margin is thin; dropping vision or context size gives headroom. Watch for `Failed to pin framebuffer` in dmesg as the early symptom.
- The `--rocm-device-lib-path=/opt/rocm-6.3/usr/lib64/rocm/llvm/lib/clang/18/amdgcn/bitcode` flag is needed if compiling HIP directly (hipcc) with clang 20; llama.cpp's CMake handles it via `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`.
- Benign warning on load: `device 'ROCm0' does not have support for op TOP_K needed for sampler 'top-k'` — doesn't affect output quality/throughput in our tests.

### Request

1. Re-confirm RDNA2 (gfx1030) support status in ROCm 7.x — if it's deprecated, a documented statement would save users a lot of debugging.
2. Consider documenting the side-by-side ROCm install path as a known workaround for gfx1030 in the HIP build docs.

### Name and Version

### Description

I'm observing a reproducible VRAM memory leak when running DeepSeek V4 Flash GGUF with DSpark speculative decoding enabled. After each PP+TG (prefill + generate) cycle, VRAM usage increases by approximately **10 MB**, and this accumulation continues until the process eventually runs out of memory (OOM).

This issue does **not** occur with:
- Step 3.7 + DSpark
- Qwen3.8-27B + DSpark

Both of the above maintain stable VRAM usage across multiple cycles.

### Environment
- Model: DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731 version) GGUF + DSpark
- Framework: llama.cpp
- Issue: VRAM leak, ~10 MB per PP+TG cycle

### Suspected Root Cause

I suspect this is a **Draft KV Cache leak** specific to the DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 model when used with DSpark. Specifically:

1. **KV cache positions** are written during every draft step but are **never compacted or properly reclaimed**, leading to continuous VRAM growth[reference:0]. A similar issue has been reported in related forks where "positions are written every tree step but never compacted," causing OOM under sustained traffic[reference:1].

2. **DSpark draft KV-cache group poisoning**: The DSpark draft model's KV cache is flagged as an "eagle group" (same as EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP/DFlash)[reference:2]. The multi-group cache-hit lookup requires **every** KV-cache group to report a nonzero hit for cache reuse to succeed — any single group reporting zero short-circuits the entire request's lookup[reference:3].

3. **Sparse and discontinuous draft KV**: DSpark's draft-layer KV is recomputed from the target model's real hidden state every decode step, meaning it has **no cross-request reuse value**[reference:4]. Its stored blocks are sparse and discontinuous (e.g., `[MISS, MISS, HIT, MISS, MISS]`)[reference:5], never satisfying the consecutive-hit window required for cache lookup[reference:6].

4. **"One-vote veto" effect**: This permanently poisons the AND-combination lookup for the entire request[reference:7], even though the model's real KV-cache groups (SWA, compressed C4A/C128A, indexer) independently have a working hit rate around 89%[reference:8]. As a result, the prefix caching mechanism is effectively disabled — every new request cannot reuse historical caches and must recompute and write new KV cache entries, causing VRAM to grow until exhaustion.

A similar fix has been proposed in vLLM where DSpark draft KV-cache groups are excluded from the cache-hit lookup poisoning mechanism[reference:9]. The same root cause likely applies to llama.cpp.

### Why Step 3.7 and Qwen3.8-27B Are Not Affected

These models likely have different DSpark implementations or KV cache structures that do **not** trigger this cache lookup conflict, allowing normal cache reuse and stable VRAM usage.

### Suggested Fix Direction

- Exclude DSpark draft KV-cache groups from the prefix caching lookup's "all-groups-must-hit" requirement, similar to the approach taken in vLLM PR #47891[reference:10].
- Alternatively, ensure DSpark draft KV cache positions are properly compacted or reclaimed after each generation cycle, as addressed in PR #23461 for draft/MTP resources.

### Additional Context

There have been related reports of DeepSeek V4 KV cache not being reclaimed on slot release, and DSpark-specific KV cache issues with offloading connectors[reference:13]. This may share a root cause with the hybrid-attention KV handling.

Please let me know if additional logs or reproduction steps would be helpful.

Thanks!

## Overview

I found an issue with quants, that they become very slow on prefill. Later I googled the exact issue. Found out that q_8 is working perfectly fine, but it did not compress enough memory for single gpu to use newest qwen 3.8 model. Tested each quant individually to get results, which were unsatisfactory:

All "after" numbers measured at the same ~9000 token prompt for a fair comparison. Before the fix the small quants collapse and time out at long prompts, so those are at shorter prompts:

| KV | before | after (~9000 tok prompt) |
|----|--------|--------------------------|
| q4_0 | 74 t/s | 1182 t/s |
| q4_1 | ~157 | 1175 |
| q5_0 | slow / timeout | 1167 |
| q5_1 | 125 | 1164 |
| q8_0 | 1159 (already fast) | 1159 |

At equal prompt length all quant KV types now run within ~2% of each other, so the fix makes them all as fast as q8_0.

Than tried reverse engineer to find the problem with opus 4.8. Because it is working on q_8 i decided that the fix will be easy, as AI can find patterns and apply similar patterns for smaller quants. q4_0 was successfull from the start, later I ran into issues with q4_1, q5_0, q5_1. It took several hours to recompile them (they also need GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON to be enabled), but the issue was fixed. After re-testing at the same prompt length all quants run at about the same speed. Still though I think there is room for improvement, but for maximum memory squeeze and performance q4_0 looks like the sweet spot for now. For a little bit better quality use q8_0, or q5_1 which sits between q4_0 and q8_0 in quality.

## Additional information

Fixes #27109. Tested on 2x RTX 3090 with Qwen 3.8 27B, outputs are numerically correct.

llama.cpp prebuild for rtx 3090 lower Quants fast prefill fix (if you don't want to compile): https://github.com/Cybertiron/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b27109-quant-kv-fix

This fix was prompted by testing with DFlash, where performance with Q4 was slower than with Q8 and FP16. Upon investigating the cause, it became apparent that the reconstruction of the Q4\_K weights—which was repeated in the destination columns in SYCL—could be optimized. This led me to examine how it was done in CUDA, where I observed a structural difference, including the use of two rows per block, which provided the clue to conduct an experimental verification.

### SYCL MTP on Intel Arc: correct output but no speed gain over baseline

**Build:** b9292 (master, oneAPI 2025.3.3)
**GPU:** Intel Arc Pro B70 (32656 MiB)
**Model:** Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-uncensored-heretic-Native-MTP-Preserved-Q4_K_M.gguf (MoE, 256 experts, 8 active)

#### Summary

After the recent merges (#23174 GDN K>1, #23142 MoE prefill, #23287 backend sampling), SYCL MTP produces **100% correct output** with **perfect draft acceptance**. This is a major milestone — earlier builds produced garbled text.

However, MTP consistently underperforms the non-MTP baseline:

| Config | Tok/s | Draft Accept | Output |
|--------|-------|-------------|--------|
| No MTP | **73.3** | — | ✅ Clean |
| MTP (draft-mtp, n_max=2) | **57.8** | 26/26 (100%) | ✅ Clean |
| MTP (draft-mtp, n_max=3) | ~48 | ~80% | ✅ Clean |

MTP is **~21% slower** than generating without speculation, despite 100% draft accuracy. This is the opposite of the expected result (typically 1.5-2x speedup on CUDA).

#### What was fixed (since b9159)

- 🟢 **GDN K>1** (#23174 karavayev) — eliminated garbled output entirely
- 🟢 **MoE prefill** (#23142 sanmai) — improved prefill, reduced generation overhead
- 🟢 **Backend sampling** (#23287) — D2H optimization, top-10 logits only
- 🟢 **VRAM leak** (#23461) — MTP resources freed on idle slots

#### What remains

The MTP head forward pass adds significant launch overhead on SYCL. Each MTP step requires:
- 1 main model decode (40 layers, ~8 experts each)
- 1 MTP head decode (1 layer, same expert count)
- 1 verification pass (batched main model decode)

On SYCL/Intel Arc, the per-kernel dispatch cost is 100-500µs vs ~5µs on CUDA. The 100% draft acceptance means the draft tokens are perfect — the bottleneck is purely kernel dispatch overhead, not compute.

#### Comparison with Vulkan

The same b9187 code built with `-DGGML_VULKAN=ON` achieves 53 tok/s with MTP — similar throughput but Vulkan has lower dispatch overhead per kernel.

#### Launch command for reproduction

```bash
source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh --force && export GGML_SYCL_F16=1 && \
  ~/llama.cpp/build-sycl-mtp-b9292/bin/llama-server \
  --jinja --chat-template-file ~/models/chat_template-v18.jinja \
  -m ~/models/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-uncensored-heretic-Native-MTP-Preserved-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2 --spec-draft-n-min 1 \
  -t 24 -ngl 99 -ub 512 -b 4096
```

#### Prior related issues

- #23149 (eval bug, resolved by PR merges)
- #23155 (original bug report, closed as duplicate)
- #23142 (MoE prefill, merged)
- #23174 (GDN K>1, merged)

#### Note

This is not a regression — the output quality and correctness fixes are invaluable. This report is to track that MTP generation speed on SYCL+MoE architectures still needs Intel kernel-level optimization (likely kernel fusion or SYCL graph support for the MTP head pipeline).

## Summary
On the Vulkan backend, Qwen3.5-27B (architecture qwen35, hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full-attention layers) generates garbage / truncated output when the batch size is set to 512. The same model and configuration generate correct, coherent text at batch sizes 1024 and 4096.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11 (build 26200)
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (24 GB), AMD proprietary driver
- Backend: Vulkan
- Software: koboldcpp 1.119 (nocuda build, Vulkan backend) which bundles the llama.cpp Vulkan backend. The underlying kernel issue appears to be in ggml-vulkan.

## Model
- Architecture: qwen35 (Gated DeltaNet / linear-attention hybrid, full_attention_interval = 4, 3x DeltaNet + 1x full-attention per group, ssm state_size 128)
- GGUFs tested: Q4_K_M and Q6_K_M quantizations of Qwen3.5-27B, including a variant carrying the built-in MTP/NextN head
- Context: reproduced at both 32768 and 262144

## Repro steps
1. Load the model with the Vulkan backend.
2. Set batch size to 512 (llama.cpp: -b 512; koboldcpp: batchsize=512), ubatch 512.
3. Send a simple generation request (e.g. 'Write a short poem about the ocean.').
4. Observe output: random token fragments / garbage, or generation stops after 1-2 tokens (e.g. 'The.') with an early EOS.

With batch size 1024 or 4096 the same request produces normal coherent output.

## Notes
- MMQ disabled; Flash Attention on/off both reproduce the issue.
- KV cache f16 and q8_0 both reproduce the issue.
- MTP drafting on/off both reproduce the issue.
- The symptom pattern points at the Gated Delta Net kernel path selection: at small batch the autoregressive (non-chunked) path corrupts the logits, while at larger batch the chunked/fused path works correctly.
- Related: #20610 (Qwen3.5-27B garbage on Vulkan), #21888, #24812, #20515.

## Expected behavior
Output quality should be independent of batch size.
items.title: [Vulkan] Qwen3.5-27B (qwen35 hybrid DeltaNet) garbage output at batch size 512; OK at 1024/4096

items.body:
## Disclosure

I used AI assistance (Claude) for the investigation, benchmarking and drafting of this PR, including this description and the commit messages. I have reviewed and validated everything myself; all measurements below were run on my own hardware and are reproducible. Flagging this explicitly per CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Summary

`ggml_vk_should_use_mmvq()` returns early with *"MMVQ is generally good for batches"* for any `n > 1`. A speculative-decode step evaluates `n = 1 + n_draft` tokens, so it takes that path and enables MMVQ — bypassing the per-vendor small-`k` heuristics below it.

Those heuristics predate speculative decoding and were only ever reachable at `n == 1`. This PR raises the cutoff so decode-like `n` reaches them too. **No vendor threshold is changed** — they simply now apply at the small `n` a speculative step actually uses.

Enabling MMVQ there costs twice:

1. The Q8_1 quantization of the activations does not amortize at such small `n`.
2. It **perturbs the logits**, so the draft and the target disagree on tokens they should agree on — lowering **draft acceptance**.

The second effect is the less obvious one: MMVQ was not merely slower in the speculative path, it was degrading speculation quality.

## Commits

- `vulkan: don't use MMVQ for k-quants at small k on AMD` — AMD-specific tuning: for k-quants the Q8_1 quantization does not pay for itself at small `k`; DMMV is faster.
- `vulkan: treat a speculative-decode step as decode, not as a batch` — vendor-agnostic; raises the `n > 1` cutoff to `MMVQ_MAX_DECODE_LIKE_N`.

## Testing

AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 "Strix Halo" (gfx1151, 40 CU, RADV/Mesa), 128 GB unified memory.
Model: 35B-A3B MoE, Q6_K attention + Q4_K FFN. MTP self-speculation (`--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2`), ~33k context, 2 runs each, against master `7f575c39d`.

| | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TG, speculative | 75.2 t/s | **84.9 t/s** (+12.9%) |
| draft acceptance | 72–75% | **83–85%** |
| TG, non-speculative | 72.9 t/s | 73.9 t/s |
| PP (prefill), pp4096 | 679.4 t/s | 677.5 t/s (unchanged) |

Prefill is unaffected because `n` there is far larger — with a 2048 ubatch the per-expert token counts are ~64+, well above the cutoff, so batched MMVQ is retained.

An op-level trace of the MMVQ decisions during a speculative step on master shows the mechanism directly:

```
984x  n=3 k=2048 m=512  q4_K -> MMVQ     (expert up/gate)
492x  n=3 k=512  m=2048 q4_K -> MMVQ     (expert down)
220x  n=1 ...          q4_K -> dmmv      (plain decode, correctly bypassed)
```

## Caveats

- **I could only test gfx1151.** The second commit now applies to all vendors per review feedback, but I have no NVIDIA or Intel hardware to validate against. Numbers from someone with a dGPU would be very welcome — particularly whether MMVQ at `n = 2..8` is a win on those backends, since if so the cutoff may need to stay vendor-conditional.
- The first commit changes AMD behaviour at `n == 1` and therefore also affects **discrete** RDNA cards, which I likewise could not test. It is kept as a separate commit so it can be dropped independently.
- `MMVQ_MAX_DECODE_LIKE_N = 8` is a bound chosen to cover common draft widths. Happy to derive it from the actual draft width instead if you'd prefer something less arbitrary.

## Name and Version

```
$ ./llama-server --version
version: 0.1.0-dev (build 10178, commit e9e3fdd15)
built with GNU 15.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

## Operating systems

- Linux (kernel 7.0.0-29-generic)

## Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

- libllama (core library)
- llama-server

## Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-IQ4_NL.gguf --mmproj mmproj-BF16.gguf -a qwen3.8-27b \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -ngl 99 -c 130000 \
  --cache-type-k q4_1 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --flash-attn on -b 2048 -ub 512 -np 1 --threads-batch 12 \
  --temp 0.6 --min-p 0.05 --repeat-penalty 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 \
  --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4 --mlock --metrics --cache-ram 2048
```

## Problem description & steps to reproduce

Switching the K cache from `q8_0` to `q4_1` collapses prompt processing (prefill) speed by ~20x on a **qwen35 hybrid architecture** model (attention + recurrent memory layers, 65 blocks, 17 attention layers, GQA 4x256). Generation speed is unaffected.

Measured on an RTX 3090 (compute capability 8.6), driver 580.173.02, CUDA 13.0, full GPU offload, `--flash-attn on`, `cache_prompt=false`:

| Config | Prefill (4-10K prompt) | Generation |
|:------:|:----------------------:|:----------:|
| q8_0 / q8_0 | 991-1276 t/s | ~60 t/s |
| K=q4_1, V=q8_0 | 34-106 t/s | ~60 t/s |

At 65K+ prompt lengths prefill is slow enough that requests hit the 600s timeout (a 90K prompt takes ~44 min at ~34 t/s).

**Important:** the MMQ shared-memory guard from #26141 (`caa596ab3`) is NOT the trigger here — it passes on this system. Measured: `cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin` returns **101376 B (99 KiB)** on the RTX 3090, so `smpbo < 48 * 1024` is false and MMQ stays enabled. Issue #26285 reports a similar symptom from an older build; on the current build the guard does not cause the fallback.

A 4-bit **V** cache showed the same collapse earlier (31 Jul, older build): PP ~195 t/s with `V=q4_0` vs ~1174 t/s after returning V to q8_0. So the slow path appears to be the CUDA flash-attention / quantized-KV dequant kernel selection for 4-bit KV on this hybrid architecture, independent of the shared-memory guard.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Start `llama-server` with `--cache-type-k q4_1 --cache-type-v q8_0` (+ `--flash-attn on`, full offload) on a qwen35 hybrid model.
2. Send a ~8K token prompt with `cache_prompt=false`.
3. Observe prefill at ~40-100 t/s instead of ~1000+ t/s.
4. Switch to `q8_0/q8_0`, restart, same prompt -> ~1000+ t/s.

## First Bad Commit

Not bisected. Reproduces on `e9e3fdd15` (14 Aug 2026 upstream + cherry-picked PR #25592). The same 4-bit KV prefill collapse was observed on 31 Jul with 4-bit V on an older build.

## Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>

```console
I slot print_timing: id  0 | task 1152 | prompt processing, n_tokens =   6144, progress = 0.07, t =  57.95 s / 106.03 tokens per second
I slot print_timing: id  0 | task 1152 | prompt processing, n_tokens =   8192, progress = 0.09, t = 103.49 s /  79.16 tokens per second
I slot print_timing: id  0 | task 1152 | prompt processing, n_tokens =  10240, progress = 0.12, t = 165.77 s /  61.77 tokens per second
I slot print_timing: id  0 | task 1152 | prompt processing, n_tokens =  16384, progress = 0.19, t = 481.66 s /  34.02 tokens per second
```

With `q8_0/q8_0` the same server logs ~1174-1276 t/s at these context sizes.

</details>

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 3645 (6c8dcaa7ae)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Commit tested: `6c8dcaa7ae41fa9f4aa2b3b68ee82cb8b2a03632` (master, `sycl: parallelize the non-contiguous concat kernel (#25852)`)
CUDA build: `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`, `GGML_CUDA=ON`, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89`, built with GNU 13.3.0.

### Operating systems

- Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel `7.0.0-28-generic`)

### GGML backends

- CUDA

### Hardware

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (24 GiB), driver `595.84`, CUDA `13.2`.

### Models

`unsloth/Qwen3.5-0.8B-MTP-GGUF` at `Q4_K_XL` (the `Qwen3.5-0.8B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf` file). This is the Qwen3.5 "unified decoder" (hybrid full-attention / linear-attention / gated delta net) architecture with a built-in **MTP/NextN** head (`qwen35.nextn_predict_layers`, one nextn block at `blk.24`).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` crashes with a hard CUDA error (`cublasSgemm_v2` → `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` → `GGML_ABORT`) when run with `--spec-type draft-mtp` under parallel load with KV-cache saturation. The crash is a **GPU-API abort, not a graceful "context size exceeded" return**, so it is a bug rather than an expected failure mode of running out of context.

This has been reproducible for a long time ("ever since MTP code merged"); the same crash class is reported in #20049 and #23803, and in Indras-Mirror/llama.cpp-turboq-mtp#17. The maintainers' earlier explanation ("total parallel tokens exceeded total KV slots") describes the *trigger* (the log is full of context-exceeded/retry events) but not the *mechanism*: a context-full condition must return `decode() == 1` gracefully, never reach `cublasSgemm`.

**Stable, fast reproduction** (~20–25 min, no benchmark harness needed). Two independent server configs both crash; both crash on the *same* op:

Server A (smaller context):
```shell
llama-server -m Qwen3.5-0.8B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --temp 0 \
  -c 1024 -np 4 --kv-unified --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18081 --no-webui
```
Server B (larger context):
```shell
llama-server -m Qwen3.5-0.8B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --temp 0 \
  -c 8192 -np 4 --kv-unified --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18080 --no-webui
```

Stress client: many parallel `/completion` requests with mixed prompt lengths / `n_predict`, designed to keep the KV cache permanently saturated so the server is constantly in the `failed to find free space in the KV cache, retrying with smaller batch size` / `Context size has been exceeded` regime (the exact regime shown in the attached log). A minimal Python soak that reproduces it:

```python
import concurrent.futures, json, random, urllib.request
HOST = "http://127.0.0.1:18081"; CONC = 10
WORDS = "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog".split(); TEXT = " ".join(WORDS)
def mk(n): return " ".join([TEXT]*(max(1, int(n*4.2/len(TEXT)))))
def one(_):
    p = {"prompt": mk(random.choice([150,250,350,500,650,850])),
         "n_predict": random.choice([16,32,64,128,256,512]), "temperature": 0}
    req = urllib.request.Request(HOST+"/completion", data=json.dumps(p).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type":"application/json"})
    try: urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600).read()
    except Exception: pass
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(CONC) as ex:
    futs = [ex.submit(one, i) for i in range(CONC)]
    while True:
        done, _ = concurrent.futures.wait(futs, return_when=concurrent.futures.FIRST_COMPLETED)
        for f in done:
            f.result(); futs.remove(f); futs.append(ex.submit(one, 0))
```

Both servers crash after ~20–25 min with the identical signature. The original (real-world) report was under `hb run -d terminal-bench -a mini-swe-agent` against the same server, where it took much longer (many thousands of tasks); the soak above just makes the same KV-saturation regime much denser.

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. Long-standing — the reporter states the crash has occurred "ever since the MTP code was merged", and the same crash class is described in #20049 / #23803 / Indras-Mirror/llama.cpp-turboq-mtp#17.

### Relevant log output

Every crash is preceded by the same pattern: one or more `Context size has been exceeded` events, slots released, then 4 fresh slots launched, then the crash in the first decode:

```console
E srv    send_error: task id = 46435, error: Context size has been exceeded.
I slot      release: id  1 | task 46435 | stop processing: n_tokens = 1293, truncated = 0
E srv    send_error: task id = 46443, error: Context size has been exceeded.
I slot      release: id  2 | task 46443 | stop processing: n_tokens = 2584, truncated = 0
E srv  update_slots: decode() failed: Context size has been exceeded.
I slot get_availabl: id  0 | task -1 | selected slot by LRU, t_last = 536191175449
I slot launch_slot_: id  0 | task 46553 | processing task, is_child = 0
... 4 slots launched ...
ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:106: CUDA error
E CUDA error: an unsupported value or parameter was passed to the function
E   current device: 0, in function ggml_cuda_mul_mat_cublas_impl at ggml-cuda.cu:1541
E   cublasSgemm_v2(ctx.cublas_handle(), CUBLAS_OP_T, CUBLAS_OP_N, ne01, ne11, ne10, (const float*)alpha, (const float*)src0_ptr, s01, (const float*)src1_ptr, s11, (const float*)beta, (float*)dst_ptr, ne0)
```

### Captured failing GEMM (via a local diagnostic patch, `LLAMA_DEBUG_GEMM=1`)

I added a one-line diagnostic at the exact crash site (`ggml-cuda.cu:1541`, F32 `cublasSgemm` branch) that dumps the failing call's parameters on `cublasSgemm_v2 != CUBLAS_STATUS_SUCCESS`. Both independent reproductions failed on the **identical** matmul, with **all cuBLAS constraints satisfied**:

```
GEMM-FAIL: status=7 src0='blk.0.ssm_alpha.weight'(0) ne00=1024 ne01=16 nb00=4 nb01=4096
           src1='attn_norm-0'(0) ne10=1024 ne11=16 nb10=4 nb11=4096
           dst='node_43' ne0=16 | s01=1024 s11=1024 ne0=16
           align0=0 align1=0 alignD=0 src0_ptr

# `tool_choice: "required"` is accepted but not enforced on templates with `supports_preserve_reasoning: true`

### Name and Version

```
build_info: b330-84e908c62
```
Built locally for CUDA 13.0, `-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121 -DCMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS="-O2"`.

### Operating systems

Linux (aarch64, NVIDIA GB10 / sm_121)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

`llama-server`, and the chat/grammar layer under `common/` (`chat-auto-parser-generator.cpp`).

### Command line

```
llama-server -m qwen36-NVFP4-MTP-HQ.gguf --host 0.0.0.0 --port 11435 \
  -c 131072 --jinja -ngl 999 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --spec-type draft-mtp
```

### Problem description

`llama-server` accepts `"tool_choice": "required"` on `/v1/chat/completions` without error or
warning, and then does not enforce it, on models whose chat template llama.cpp classifies with
`supports_preserve_reasoning: true`.

Instead of being constrained to emit a tool call, the model generates freely until `max_tokens`
is exhausted. The request returns `finish_reason: "length"` with `predicted_n` equal to the full
budget and no `tool_calls`. In the runs I inspected the tail of the output had degenerated into a
repeating emoji sequence, which is consistent with generation being unconstrained rather than
grammar-limited.

The failure is **silent and expensive**: a caller that relies on `required` for structured output
receives ordinary prose, no error, and pays the maximum token cost of the request every time.

Two servers on the same host, same binary, same build string, both `--jinja`, differ only in the
model/template:

| | fast lane | smart lane |
|---|---|---|
| model | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (NVFP4, MTP) | Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct (Q4_K_M) |
| `supports_tool_calls` | true | true |
| `supports_parallel_tool_calls` | true | true |
| `supports_object_arguments` | true | true |
| **`supports_preserve_reasoning`** | **true** | **false** |
| `tool_choice: "required"` | **ignored** | honoured |

`supports_preserve_reasoning` is the only differing capability in `/props → chat_template_caps`.

**On reproducing this without my exact file:** the GGUF above is a local conversion and is not
something you can download, so please do not treat the filename as the repro target. The trigger
appears to be the *chat template* — specifically whichever templates llama.cpp classifies
`supports_preserve_reasoning: true`, i.e. a `<think>`-style reasoning template. Any model whose
`/props → chat_template_caps` reports that flag together with `supports_tool_calls: true` should
show it. `repro.sh` prints both flags up front so it is obvious at a glance whether a given server
is a candidate. I am happy to attach the exact template text if that helps.

### What is NOT the cause (ruled out by measurement)

- **The model.** An identical hand-written GBNF grammar posted to `/completion` forces a perfect
  tool call on both servers, from a prompt with no intent to call anything. Section B of the
  reproducer is this control.
- **Grammar sampling generally.** `root ::= "BANANA"` is honoured on the affected server.
- **Speculative decoding.** The control above succeeds with `--spec-type draft-mtp` active.
- **Reasoning parsing.** Sending `"reasoning_format": "none"` does not change the behaviour.
- **Token budget.** Identical failure at `max_tokens` 500 / 1500 / 3000 / 5000 — all fully
  consumed, `reasoning_content` exactly 801 chars each time.
- **The tool-call syntax.** Both templates emit `<tool_call>…</tool_call>` with `<|im_start|>`.

### Why this looks like a defect rather than unsupported behaviour

`common/chat-auto-parser-generator.cpp` appears to intend enforcement on this path:

```cpp
// ~line 84
bool include_grammar = has_response_format || (has_tools &&
        ((inputs.tool_choice == COMMON_CHAT_TOOL_CHOICE_AUTO && !trigger_marker.empty()) ||
          inputs.tool_choice == COMMON_CHAT_TOOL_CHOICE_REQUIRED));

// ~line 89 — REQUIRED yields a NON-lazy (eager) grammar
data.grammar_lazy = !has_response_format && inputs.tool_choice == COMMON_CHAT_TOOL_CHOICE_AUTO;

// ~line 369 and ~line 500 — for REQUIRED the tool calls are NOT made optional
if (!require_calls) { tool_calls = p.optional(tool_calls); }
```

So a grammar is built, marked eager, and tool calls are non-optional — yet generation is
evidently unconstrained. I have not isolated the specific line where enforcement is lost; that
likely needs a debug build dumping the emitted GBNF for the two templates.

### Steps to Reproduce

Full script at the bottom of this issue. `./repro.sh <host:port>` exits **1** when the bug reproduces and **0**
when `required` is honoured — it was verified to discriminate between the two servers above.

```bash
curl -s http://HOST:PORT/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model":"local",
  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello, how are you today?"}],
  "tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_disk_free",
    "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"host":{"type":"string"}},"required":["host"]}}}],
  "tool_choice":"required","max_tokens":2000,"temperature":0}'
```

Expected: a `tool_calls` response. Actual on an affected template: `finish_reason: "length"`,
`predicted_n` == `max_tokens`, no `tool_calls`.

### Relevant log output

```
finish_reason : length
predicted_n   : 2000
tool_calls    : NONE
content tail  : '🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️…'

# control, same server, hand-written grammar via /completion:
'<tool_call>{"name": "get_disk_free", "arguments": {"host": "beta"}}</tool_call>'
```


### Possibly related open issues

- **#26781** — *"enable_thinking forced true in jinja/caps.cpp capability probe leaks into
  non-DeepSeek templates"*. Same model family (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B), same subsystem, and a very
  similar end state: budget consumed inside `reasoning_content`, no `tool_calls`, a silent dead
  end for an API consumer. **Differences:** that report needs ~38-41 turns of accumulated co

items.body:
### Problem

For recurrent and hybrid models the server keeps up to `--ctx-checkpoints` (default 32) context checkpoints per slot, and each one serializes the full recurrent state as fp32 into host RAM (`server_prompt::checkpoints`). On Qwen3.8-27B (arch `qwen35`, 65 blocks, SSM state size 128 across 16 groups, inner size 6144) one checkpoint's recurrent plane is 149.6 MiB, so a single slot at the default limit holds about 4.7 GiB, and that scales linearly with slots.

I could not find any upstream attempt to compress this. The checkpoint-related work I found is all functional — SWA generalization (#16382), speculative checkpointing (#19493, #22227), slot persistence (#20819), restore fixes (#22384) — and 4b836fd points the other way, warning about nondeterminism when a quantized V cache meets speculative checkpoints. Before opening a PR I'd like to know whether the storage side is something you'd entertain at all.

### What I've been running

A codec at the state serialization boundary, off by default:

```
--rs-checkpoint-codec N    # 0 = fp32 (default), 1 = RHT-INT16, 2 = RHT-INT8
```

Each row is rotated by a random Hadamard transform (sign vector derived from a fixed seed, so it is reproducible and carries no side data), then stored as int16 or int8 with a per-row scale. Only the write path is affected. The read path detects a magic header, so checkpoints written with and without the flag load interchangeably. Non-finite values or degenerate scales fall back to fp32 for that block, and a metadata mismatch is fail-closed. Restored state runs in fp32; nothing in the live compute path changes.

It hooks the recurrent memory's state io, so it applies to recurrent and hybrid memory generally, though I have only tested the two models below.

Setup for everything that follows: Qwen3.8-27B (`qwen35`, 65 blocks, one MTP layer) on 4 GPUs and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (`qwen35moe`) on 2, both Q8_0 GGUF with `-sm tensor` and MTP speculation on, server at ece963f41. The weight quant is incidental to these numbers, since the recurrent state is fp32 either way. It has been running on all three instances in production here.

### Measurements

Roundtrip, forced continuation of 48 tokens:

| model | codec | checkpoint | mean rel. L2 | worst | token flips |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 27B | fp32 | 149.63 MiB | — | — | 0/48 |
| 27B | RHT-INT16 | 74.82 MiB (2.00x) | 0.0049% | 0.0067% | 0/48 |
| 27B | RHT-INT8 | 37.41 MiB (4.00x) | 1.27% | 1.74% | 0/48 |
| 35B | RHT-INT16 | 31.41 MiB (2.00x) | 0.0037% | 0.0050% | 0/48 |
| 35B | RHT-INT8 | 15.70 MiB (4.00x) | 0.96% | 1.28% | 1/48 |

Server-level A/B on two identical instances, greedy sampling, every continuation going through a real restore:

| | 27B RHT-INT16 | 35B RHT-INT16 | 35B RHT-INT8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| token flips vs fp32 | 0/360 (0.0%) | 65/349 (18.6%) | 234/338 (69.2%) |
| divergence/rewind test | 5/5 identical | 5/5 correct, 4/5 differ textually | — |

fp32 against fp32 on the same pair is 0/72, so the baseline really is deterministic. Across 42 restores there were no decode errors. Restore costs about 0.35 s for a 120–160 MiB checkpoint, and model load time is unchanged.

### The caveat

Weight and KV quantization error is per-token and self-limiting. Checkpoint error is not: the restored state is the starting point for everything decoded after it, so the error feeds the entire continuation. That is what the two models above show — same codec, same L2, 0% versus 18.6% token divergence. Sensitivity is model-dependent and cannot be read off the L2 figure, which is why I want this opt-in and off by default, with the caveat stated in the flag help, in the same spirit as the 4b836fd warning.

INT8 fails my own gate on the 35B (69%) and I would keep it non-default, but I'd rather include the measurement than hide it.

On "why not just f16": at the same 2 bytes per element, int16 with a per-row scale after the rotation spends its whole mantissa on the row's actual dynamic range, while f16 gives up bits to an exponent the data doesn't need. If a plain f16 path would be the more welcome version, that is a much smaller change and I'd rather learn it now than after a PR. For what it's worth, the same codec ships as the default state codec in oMLX (an unrelated MLX-based project I also work on) at 1.93x and 0.0025% mean relative L2, which lines up with the numbers here.

### Questions

1. Is a lossy, default-off storage codec for checkpoints something you would consider?
2. Scope. There is a second piece I have running. The draft context's KV and speculative state go into the same checkpoint at whatever `--spec-draft-type-k/-v` is set to, F16 by default, and unlike the recurrent plane that part grows with position: 84.7 MiB of a 234 MiB 27B checkpoint at 21.5k tokens, about 4.1 KiB per token, so it dominates at long context. Storing it as q8_0 while the live draft cache stays f16, plus skipping the per-cycle draft snapshot, takes the 35B checkpoint down a further 48.9%. One PR or two?
3. Naming. I use `--rs-checkpoint-codec` locally, but `--checkpoint-codec` seems closer to the existing flags. Preference?

The branch is 18 files modified for about 220 insertions, plus a new codec source pair and two tests (a unit test and a roundtrip harness). I'll rebase onto master and re-run the gates before sending anything.

### Name and Version

version: 0.1.0-dev (build 10428, commit 885c5bbe8)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64

b10428 Windows x64 (CUDA 13)

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

1 RTX 5070TI + 1 RTX3060TI

### Models

Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL
https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF/tree/main

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

While decoding tokens, generation suddenly freezes and GPU utilization jumps from around 85 % while generating to 100% in the frozen state. The server doesn't report an error and doesn't recover. System is stable and responsive. Restarting llama-server solves the problem, till next lockup.

The problem does seem to only occur with using --split-mode tensor and --spec-type draft-mtp together. Sometimes it occurs after 7 tokens, sometimes after 40,000 tokens and sometimes never. The higher the --spec-draft-n-max value, the sooner the lockup happens. Everything over --spec-draft-n-max 2 seems to lead to a pretty much instant lockup.

Without --spec-type draft-mtp enabled, --split-mode tensor seems stable.

With --split-mode layer the problem doesn't occur at all, not even at dysfunctional --spec-draft-n-max 5.

Here my config. Tried removing ngram-mod and ngram-map-k4v as well but this had no influence. Neither did reducing --ctx-size for more VRAM headroom. I had a feeling though, that modifying --batch-size and --ubatch-size had an influence on when the problem occurs but that very well could have been a random fluke.

--spec-type draft-mtp,ngram-mod,ngram-map-k4v
--spec-draft-n-max 2
--spec-draft-n-min 0
--spec-draft-p-min 0.0
--spec-ngram-mod-n-match 36
--spec-ngram-mod-n-min 48
--spec-ngram-mod-n-max 64
--spec-ngram-map-k4v-size-n 12 
--spec-ngram-map-k4v-size-m 48
--spec-ngram-map-k4v-min-hits 1
--parallel 1
--main-gpu 0
--ctx-size 65336
--batch-size 1024

--cache-type-k q8_0
--cache-type-v q8_0
--kv-unified
--split-mode tensor
--tensor-split 2.05,0.95
--cache-reuse 256
--cache-ram 32768
--checkpoint-min-step 512
--ctx-checkpoints 8

Unidentified, but the problem ranges at least from b10428 to b10436

items.body:
## Overview

Fixes a regression after #24233, which restored HIP integrated GPU detection. On my AMD APU, this also made the ROCm host-buffer path available for HIP integrated GPUs. With that path enabled, prompt input appears corrupted: chat templates and system prompts can be ignored, and generated output becomes garbage.

This change keeps integrated GPU detection/reporting intact, but disables direct ROCm_Host compute on HIP integrated GPUs. The fix does not disable host-buffer exposure entirely, pinned buffers remain available to preserve functionality, while only the problematic direct compute path is blocked.

## Additional information

Tested locally on gfx1151 / RDNA3.5 APU with ROCm 7.14. The corrupted input/output issue is fixed with this patch.
The issue appeared in external harnesses like Pi and OpenCode. It can also be reproduced in the built-in web UI with a sufficiently large combined first input. For example, gemma-4-26B-A4B with 4676 tokens of context or more outputs `<unused49>` indefinitely. Other models can be way more resilient and their output starts by saying 'Based on the text provided, which appears to be a corrupted or "hallucinated" version of a Wikipedia article'.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - I used AI assistance to review and patch the relevant code. I tested and reviewed the final change myself.

items.body:
## Bug: AMD GPU token substitution corruption on Qwen3.6-27B (both Vulkan and ROCm)

### Summary

All models produce consistent character substitution errors in generated text on AMD GPU backends (Vulkan and ROCm). The CPU backend produces correct output. Cloud vLLM with the same model also produces correct output. The corruption is deterministic, reproducible, and not model-specific.

**Version:** b10298 (commit 15586e2d7)

### Symptom

URLs and long token sequences get corrupted with character substitutions. Examples from Qwen3.6-27B:

| Input | GPU output |
|-------|-----------|
| `awesome-zsh-plugins` | `awesome-zh-plugins` |
| `awesome-zsh-plugins` | `awesome-zshell-plugins` |
| `awesome-zsh-plugins` | `awesome-ssh-plugins` |
| `froggeric` | `frogger` |
| `helix-assist` | `helix-Assist` |

Short strings like `zsh-plugins` reproduce correctly in isolation. The corruption only appears in longer sequences, suggesting precision accumulation in attention over longer contexts.

### Reproduction

1. Start llama-server with any GGUF model on AMD GPU (Vulkan or ROCm backend)
2. Send a chat completion asking to repeat a URL:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "code",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "You are a precise assistant. Repeat exactly."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "Repeat this URL exactly:\nhttps://github.com/unixorn/awesome-zsh-plugins/blob/main/README.md"}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 100,
    "temperature": 0.0
  }'
```

3. Observe corrupted URL in the response
4. Run the same request on CPU backend (`--n-gpu-layers 0`) and observe correct output

### Environment

- **GPU 0:** AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (Navi 31, RDNA3, discrete)
- **GPU 1:** AMD Ryzen 9 9950X integrated GPU (RAPHAEL_MENDOCINO)
- **Vulkan driver:** Mesa RADV 26.1.6, Vulkan API 1.4.354
- **ROCm:** latest (via `ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-rocm`)
- **Kernel:** 6.17.9
- **llama.cpp version:** b10298 (commit 15586e2d7)
- **Containers:** `ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-vulkan` and `ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-rocm`

### Exclusion testing

Every variable tested produces identical corruption on GPU. Only the CPU backend is correct.

| Variable | Values tested | Result |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| Model quants | Q4_K_XL, Q4_K_M, UD-Q4_K_XL, UD-Q5_K_XL | All corrupted |
| GPU backend | Vulkan (RADV), ROCm (HIP) | Both corrupted |
| KV cache type | q8_0, f16 | Both corrupted |
| GPU count | Both GPUs, single GPU (`GGML_VULKAN_DEVICE=0`) | Both corrupted |
| Speculative decoding | On (draft-mtp), off | Both corrupted |
| Thinking/reasoning | Enabled, disabled | Both corrupted |
| Chat template | Custom template, raw completion | Both corrupted |
| Temperature | 0.0 (greedy) | Still corrupted |
| **CPU backend** | `--n-gpu-layers 0` | **Correct** |

Forcing a single GPU via `GGML_VULKAN_DEVICE=0` rules out multi-GPU issues like #26197.

### Not model-specific: Gemma 4 also corrupts

Tested Gemma 4 31B (`gemma-4-31B-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf`) on the same Vulkan backend. It also corrupts URLs, but with a different pattern — inserting spaces instead of substituting characters:

| Input | Gemma 4 output |
|-------|---------------|
| `awesome-zsh-plugins` | `awesome zsh-plugins` |
| `helix-assist` | `helix assist` |
| `froggeric` | `froggereric` |
| `Qwen-Fixed-Chat-Templates` | `Qwen-Fixed-Chat- Templates` |

The corruption pattern differs by model (Qwen3.6 substitutes characters, Gemma 4 inserts spaces) but both produce incorrect output on AMD GPU.

### Not a model issue: cloud vLLM is correct

The same Qwen3.6-27B model running on cloud vLLM (different quant, different inference engine) reproduces all test URLs perfectly. This confirms the corruption is specific to llama.cpp on AMD GPU.

### Conclusion

This is a general AMD GPU compute issue in llama.cpp, not model-specific, not quant-specific, not backend-specific. It affects all models on the RX 7900 XTX. Both GPU backends (Vulkan and ROCm) produce identical corruption patterns, suggesting a shared AMD code path issue.

Potentially related issues:
- #26197 (multiple AMD GPUs lead to gibberish output) — ruled out by single-GPU test
- #20029 (Vulkan garbage output on AMD)
- #25612 (split-mode garbled output)
items.title: AMD GPU token substitution corruption on Qwen3.6-27B (both Vulkan and ROCm)

### Name and Version

Built from `505b1ed1` (2026-07-15). The relevant code is **unchanged in current master** (`86d86ed`, 2026-07-17): the assert at `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp:4282` and `ggml_repack_get_optimal_repack_type()` are as described below.

### Operating systems

macOS (Apple Silicon, arm64 / NEON)

### GGML backends

CPU (Metal build, but run with `-ngl 0`)

### Hardware

Apple Silicon, 128 GB unified memory

### Models

`bullerwins/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-GGUF` — `DeepSeek-V4-Flash.Q8_0.gguf` (arch `deepseek4`; attention in Q8_0, routed experts in MXFP4).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

On **Apple Silicon (arm64/NEON), CPU only (`-ngl 0`)**, `deepseek4` (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) produces **garbled output** — an endless run of `=` — instead of text. This is **not** the CUDA/ROCm expert issue in #25582 / #25436, and not fixed by the rejected assert change in #25412. It is the **CPU online-repack path silently corrupting `blk.N.attn_output_a` / `blk.N.attn_output_b`** (the MLA low-rank output projection).

```
./llama-cli -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash.Q8_0.gguf -ngl 0 -cnv -st -p "What is the capital of France? Answer briefly."
# -> [Start thinking] ==================================================  (garbage)
```

**Bisection** (each variant is a one-line change to `ggml_repack_get_optimal_repack_type()` returning `nullptr` for the named tensors, then a full rebuild + rerun):

| repack disabled for… | output |
|---|---|
| nothing (stock) | garbled (also hits the `:4282` assert on the 3D expert stacks) |
| 3D tensors only (`ggml_n_dims != 2`) | **still garbled** |
| the DSA `indexer` tensors | still garbled |
| `attn_kv` | still garbled |
| `attn_q_a` / `attn_q_b` | still garbled |
| **`attn_output_a` / `attn_output_b`** | **correct** ("Paris") |
| everything | correct |

So the culprit is exactly `attn_output_a/_b` — 86 of 494 tensors. Excluding *only* those from repack yields coherent output.

**Controls (both pass with fully stock repack on the same machine):**
- `gemma4-31b` Q4_K_M (dense) — correct.
- `Agents-A1` Q8_0 (`qwen35moe`, 256 routed experts) — correct.

So this is **`deepseek4`-specific**, not a general MoE or 3D-tensor repack problem — a 256-expert MoE and a dense model both repack fine.

### Root cause (analysis)

`ggml_repack_get_optimal_repack_type()` selects a repack `tensor_traits` purely by tensor **type** (q4_0/q4_K/q5_K/q6_K/q2_K/q8_0/iq4_nl/mxfp4) and `ne[1] % 8`; it **never checks `ggml_n_dims`** and does not exclude the MLA output-projection tensors. `extra_buffer_type::supports_op` *claims* `MUL_MAT_ID` for 3D `src0` (`repack.cpp:4795`), but the compute path `forward_mul_mat` asserts 2D (`repack.cpp:4282`). For `attn_output_a/_b` specifically, repacking reorders the weight in memory and the result read back is wrong — silently, when the assert is avoided.

Note: changing the assert to `>= 2` (as in the rejected #25412) is not a fix — it turns the crash into silent garbage, which is what the "3D tensors only" row above shows.

I'm happy to test a proper patch. The mechanism for why `attn_output_a/_b` in particular is affected (while `attn_q_a/_b`, same type, is not) I have not pinned down — likely how those tensors are consumed in the `deepseek4` MLA graph after repack reorders them.

### Relevant log output

```
/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp:4282: GGML_ASSERT(ggml_n_dims(op->src[0]) == 2) failed
  ...forward_mul_mat_id... (stock repack, before any workaround)
```

## Summary

Under parallel mixed load (`-np 4 --kv-unified`), `llama-server` on an **integrated HIP GPU** (Strix Halo / gfx1151, 128 GB UMA) returns **complete responses that verbatim belong to a different, earlier request**. A large-prompt request receives, as its entire response, the literal answer text of a short request from an earlier round. We also observed a **chimeric** response fusing tokens of two different requests' expected outputs.

**Bisected to a single commit: c7d87229 "ggml-cuda : restore prop.integrated on HIP builds" (#24233).**

| build | result (validated responses, nonce-checked) |
|---|---|
| 505b1ed1 (parent window start) | clean — 0 violations / 168 |
| 5839ba35 (= parent of c7d87229) | clean — 0 / 36 |
| **c7d87229** | **cross-request replays: 3 hard / 36** |
| e8f19cc0 (window end) | cross-request replays: 7 hard + 1 chimera / 96 |

The same harness against **CPU builds** of both window endpoints shows no build-dependent difference (model-compliance noise only) — consistent with the culprit being the HIP integrated-memory path. This presumably explains why it went unnoticed: discrete GPUs are unaffected; it needs an **integrated** AMD GPU (`prop.integrated == 1`), multiple slots and concurrent mixed traffic.

## Environment

- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo), gfx1151, 128 GB unified memory, ROCm 7.14, Ubuntu 24.04
- Build: `cmake -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang++` (Release)
- Server: `llama-server -m <model> -ngl 999 -c 65536 -np 4 --kv-unified --jinja --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'`
- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE (Q4-class quant). First hit this in production behind LocalAI (same symptom after its vendored-llama.cpp bump crossed this commit); reproducing on vanilla `llama-server` rules the wrapper out.

## Reproduction

Load pattern per round (~30 s, script below): (B) short "repeat exactly this code: <nonce>" request → (C) large-prompt (~10k tokens) request whose system prompt requires echoing a per-request nonce in the first line → (D) burst of 4 concurrent short nonce requests (2 streamed / 2 plain). Every response is validated to contain its **own** nonce and no nonce of an **earlier** request.

On affected builds the round-N large-prompt request receives a literal foreign nonce as its complete response, typically from a round-(N−1) burst request. Verbatim from run logs at e8f19cc0:

```
R4/C got='pd-20260722-115649-3-d1'      (expected: reply echoing pc-...-4-c + a summary)
R5/C got='pd-20260722-115649-4-d2'
R6/C got='pd-20260722-115649-1-d1'
R7/C got='pd-20260722-115649-6-d1'
R8/C got='pd-20260722-115649-7-d1'
R3/C got='<!-- run:pc-20260722-115649-2-d0 -->'   <-- chimera: pc-...-2 stem fused with a -d0 burst suffix
```

In production we additionally observed: a poisoned slot re-serving its stored answer to unrelated requests **20+ minutes later** (the victim's `usage` then reports the foreign request's token counts), and occasional degeneration into repeated single characters (`/////...`).

<details><summary>repro-crossover.py (needs httpx)</summary>

```python

items.body:
### Name and Version

```
$ llama-cli --version
version: 9721 (dfsg)
built with gcc for x86_64-linux-gnu
```

(Ubuntu 26.10 `llama.cpp 9721+dfsg-1ubuntu1` package, `libggml0-backend-hip 0.15.2-1` from the `ppa:bullwinkle-team/rocm-with-generics` PPA, ROCm 7.2.4.)

I have also confirmed the underlying pattern still exists on `master` (`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvq.cu` — host `get_device_table_id(int cc)` at ~line 89 and device `get_device_table_id()` at ~line 73 use two different lookups). See "Why #24129 doesn't fully close this" below.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 w/ Radeon 860M (gfx1152, RDNA3.5, Strix Halo family iGPU), integrated 16 GiB VRAM (UMA).

### Models

`unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF:Q4_0` (any Q4_0/Q4_1/Q5_0/Q5_1/Q8_0/Q6_K/IQ4_NL model that dispatches through the MMVQ `n=1` path reproduces).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

MMVQ produces `NaN` outputs for `ncols_dst == 1` (batch=1 decode) whenever the loaded HIP code object was compiled for `--offload-arch=gfx11-generic` and the runtime device is RDNA3.5 (gfx1150/gfx1152/gfx1153 without native code in the fatbin). Symptom in `llama-cli` is coherent-looking prompt processing followed by tokens rendered as `?????...` at plausible generation rates. HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.0.0 (native gfx1100) or =11.5.1 (native gfx1151) both hide the bug — they steer HIP to a native code object instead of `gfx11-generic`.

**Minimal repro** (fatbin without a gfx1152 native code object; equivalent to the current Debian/Ubuntu `ggml` build):

```
lxc launch --ephemeral --profile rocm-gpu ubuntu-daily:stonking generics-repro
lxc exec generics-repro -- sudo add-apt-repository ppa:bullwinkle-team/rocm-with-generics -y
lxc exec generics-repro -- sudo apt install -y llama.cpp libggml0-backend-hip

# NaN outputs from MMVQ (all n=1 cases fail):
lxc exec generics-repro -- /usr/libexec/x86_64-linux-gnu/ggml/test-backend-ops test -b ROCm0 -o MUL_MAT -p 'type_a=q4_0'
# ...
# [MUL_MAT] NaN at index 0 (ROCm0=nan CPU=4.080024)   MUL_MAT(type_a=q4_0,type_b=f32,m=16,n=1,k=256,...): FAIL
# every n=1 case fails; every n>=2 case passes

# Garbage tokens from llama-cli:
lxc exec generics-repro -- bash -c "echo 'What is 2+2?' | llama-cli -hf unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF:Q4_0 --predict 15 --single-turn"
# > What is 2+2?
# | ???????????????
```

`AMD_LOG_LEVEL=3` on the failing run shows the runtime resolving to the generic code object:

```
Using generic code object for device: amdgcn-amd-amdhsa--gfx1152 co: amdgcn-amd-amdhsa--gfx11-generic
```

### Root cause

`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvq.cu` has two `get_device_table_id()`s and they disagree on `gfx11-generic` + RDNA3.5:

- **Device** (`__device__`, ~line 73), compile-time preprocessor: for `gfx11-generic`, `__GFX11__` is set (so `RDNA3` is defined) but none of `__gfx1150/51/52/53__` are set (so `RDNA3_5` stays undefined) → `RDNA3_0` is defined → returns `MMVQ_PARAMETERS_RDNA3_0`. For Q4_0/Q4_1/Q5_0/Q5_1/Q8_0/IQ4_NL at `ncols_dst == 1`, `calc_nwarps(...)` returns 8 (2 for Q6_K). The kernel is emitted with `__launch_bounds__(8*warp_size, 1)` and sizes `__shared__ float tmp_shared[nwarps-1][...][warp_size]` for an 8-way inter-warp reduction.
- **Host** (`__host__`, ~line 89), runtime `cc`: on gfx1152 `cc = GGML_CUDA_CC_OFFSET_AMD + 0x1152`, so `GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_RDNA3_5(cc)` is true → returns `MMVQ_PARAMETERS_RDNA2` → `calc_nwarps(...)` returns 1 → launches `block_dims = (warp_size, 1, 1)`.

Only warp 0 executes, so the `if (threadIdx.y > 0) tmp_shared[threadIdx.y-1][...] = ...` writes never happen. The reduction loop `for (int l = 0; l < nwarps-1; ++l) tmp[j][i] += tmp_shared[l][...];` runs with `nwarps == 8` (compile-time), reading uninitialized LDS for `l = 0..6` → NaN, then propagates through the rest of the graph and shows up as `?????` at the sampler.

Confirmed by the test-backend-ops bisection: every `MUL_MAT(type_a=q4_0, n=1, ...)` case fails with `NaN at index 0`; every `n>=2` case passes. That's exactly the `if (ncols_dst == 1)` boundary in `calc_nwarps` where the RDNA3_0 branch would return 8 vs. falling through to 1.

Trivial FP32 kernels compiled the same way (`--offload-arch=gfx11-generic`) and run on the same gfx1152 produce correct results, so this is not a general clang miscompile of the generic target — it's specifically a host/device disagreement on the MMVQ tuning table.

### Why PR #24129 doesn't fully close this

[#24129](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24129) (merged) added `__gfx1152__` / `__gfx1153__` to the `RDNA3_5` macro in `hip.h`. That is the right fix for the case where the fatbin **does** ship a native gfx1152 code object — the runtime loads native gfx1152, the device compile sees `__gfx1152__` → `RDNA3_5` → returns `MMVQ_PARAMETERS_RDNA2`, matches the host. Great.

But if a build has `--offload-arch=gfx11-generic` in its target list without a native gfx1152, the runtime falls through to the generic code object, and `__gfx11_generic__` (which *is* set for the generic target — confirmed with `hipcc --offload-arch=gfx11-generic -E -dM`) is not part of the `RDNA3_5` macro. So on that same hardware the mismatch is unchanged. This is the situation in the Debian/Ubuntu `ggml` build (whose target list, via `rocm-target-arch` from `pkg-rocm-tools`, currently emits `gfx11-generic gfx1100 gfx1101 gfx1151 …` without gfx1152/1153) and, from what I can tell, in the TheRock build path that [#25436](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/25436) (DeepSeek V4 garbled on Strix Halo, still open) and possibly [#24962](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/24962) are hitting.

More generally, the host/device pattern is inherently fragile: any future target/generic pair where the two lookups disagree will silently reintroduce this. The specific instance was fixed but the root shape wasn't.

### Proposed fix

Derive `nwarps` from the compiled kernel instead of recomputing it on the host: refactor `calc_launch_params` to be templat

items.body:
## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

This PR adds support for MTP (Multi Token Prediction) heads. I tested this on Qwen3.6 27B and Qwen3.6 35BA3B but in principle it should work for any MTP model. I've posted the detailed results below, but typically I see a steady-state acceptance of around 75% with 3 draft tokens, which is more than >2x speed-up over baseline. The design decisions I took to get to this stage are as follows:

- The MTP model is a separate model which loads from the same GGUF, the idea is that MTP should automatically start and we shouldn't need to distribute the MTP gguf separately but also it has it's own context/kv-cache etc. 
- I saw a problem in #18039 where the hidden features weren't propagated correctly across multiple ubatches, so this PR adds a separate "hook" for the MTP to consume after each `ubatch`
- The MTP speculative class is fairly trivial (although it does depend on #22400, but could work without it)

> [!TIP]
> MTP is compatible with Vision input and Tensor/Pipeline Parallelism

> [!NOTE]
> Prompt processing (PP) speed typically takes a negative hit when MTP is enabled mainly due to Device-To-Host (D2H) embedding transfers. It's something to be optimized in the future.

> [!NOTE]
> Parallel decoding with MTP is supported, but not fully optimized yet.

## Performance
 
A simple bench for testing various prompts is here: https://gist.github.com/am17an/228edfb84ed082aa88e3865d6fa27090. Posting the results below:

<details>

<summary> Performance on DGX Spark :thread: </summary> 
 
## No MTP (baseline)

`./llama-server  -m ../qwen3.6-q8_0.gguf  -np 1 --chat-template-kwargs "{\"preserve_thinking\": true}"`

``` 
  code_python        pred= 192 draft=   0 acc=   0 rate=n/a tok/s=7.0
  code_cpp           pred= 192 draft=   0 acc=   0 rate=n/a tok/s=7.3
  explain_concept    pred= 192 draft=   0 acc=   0 rate=n/a tok/s=7.3
  summarize          pred=  53 draft=   0 acc=   0 rate=n/a tok/s=7.1

items.body: ### Why this exists On AMD, image generation came out visibly wrong at 1024×1024 and larger: a ghosted, doubled subject that got worse as the resolution grew. Smaller resolutions were clean, and the same job ran clean on CPU and on NVIDIA, so it was specific to AMD and only showed above a certain resolution. The flash-attention kernel was quietly ignoring the precision the model asked for and running in half precision instead. That is usually harmless, but at large resolutions the rounding piles up until it shows in the image. Worse, it fails silently: no error, just a wrong, ghosted picture. ### What it does When the model asks for fp32 precision, the kernel now uses it, instead of quietly running in half precision. Where fp32 will not fit, it falls back to the existing path, so those cases stay unchanged. This only affects AMD/HIP. NVIDIA never uses this kernel, so CUDA builds are untouched. ### Why it's the right fix Before this, there was no way to get a correct image out of an affected AMD GPU. The kernel did not fall back to anything; it just silently produced a garbled result. The only way to a correct image was to give up on the GPU and run on the CPU, which is far slower. So this is not a slower-path tradeoff: it makes the AMD GPU usable for these images, where before it was quietly broken. Builds with rocWMMA enabled already had a correct GPU path; this fix is for the AMD setups that do not. ### How I found it I reproduced it with Chroma (a non-GQA model, head size 128) in stable-diffusion.cpp on an RDNA4 GPU (a Radeon AI PRO R9700), built without rocWMMA flash-attention. Comparing the same generation on the CPU and on the GPU step by step, everything matched until the attention step (the `FLASH_ATTN_EXT` op), which was the one place the GPU result diverged. It also does not show up in `test-backend-ops`, because that test's synthetic inputs are too uniform to trigger the rounding. It surfaced alongside a separate bug on the same path, an incorrect mask shape in masked flash attention, which I fixed upstream in [leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp#1625](https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp/pull/1625) (merged). Those two changes are independent; together they make Chroma's masked flash attention correct on HIP. ### Validation The clearest way to see the bug is to render the same prompt and seed on several backends and compare. The correct backends agree on one image; the unpatched AMD tile kernel is the lone outlier, and the fix brings it back into agreement. Chroma1-HD, 1280², 20 steps, euler, flash attention on, fixed seed: - **NVIDIA (A100)**, **AMD with matrix cores** (rocWMMA), and **AMD with the fix** (fp32 tile) all produce the same image. - **AMD without the fix** (fp16 tile) produces a different, ghosted, wrong image. That is the point: the unpatched AMD result is not "just a different valid render." Three correct paths converge on one image: a different vendor (NVIDIA) and two different AMD kernels, the matrix-core rocWMMA path and the fp32 tile fix. Only the unpatched fp16 tile diverges. With the fix, that path rejoins them. At higher resolution the unpatched path degrades further, to a fully black image at 2048, while the others stay correct. Environment: - NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB: driver 580.159.04, CUDA 13.0 - AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201): ROCm 7.2.4, amdgpu 6.16.13 `test-backend-ops` is unchanged; head sizes 512 and 576 fall back to fp16. ### Reproduction Reproduced via stable-diffusion.cpp (commit `4e85e07`), which vendors this ggml kernel. Build `sd-cli` for AMD (HIP): ``` cmake -B build -DSD_HIPBLAS=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1201 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build -j --target sd-cli ``` The wrong result is this build as-is (the unpatched fp16 tile path); the correct result is the same build with this PR's ggml patch applied. For the NVIDIA reference, configure with `-DSD_CUDA=ON` instead. Render (identical command on every backend, only the build differs): ``` ./sd-cli -M img_gen \ --diffusion-model Chroma1-HD.safetensors \ --t5xxl t5xxl_fp16.safetensors \ --vae ae.safetensors \ -p "a photograph of a dog on the beach, photorealistic, hyperrealistic, highly detailed, sharp focus, natural lighting, DSLR" \ --cfg-scale 4.0 --guidance 3.5 --sampling-method euler --steps 20 \ -W 1280 -H 1280 --seed 42 --rng cuda --chroma-enable-t5-mask --diffusion-fa \ -o out.png ``` ### Performance note This is the tile flash-attention kernel, the path used whenever the matrix-core path (rocWMMA flash-attention) is not in use. That path is opt-in, a build flag that is off by default, so a default HIP build runs the tile kernel on any AMD GPU, with or without matrix cores. The tile kernel has no hardware-accelerated fp32. On RDNA the fast fp16 path uses a packed dot instruction that fp32 cannot use, and fp32 storage roughly doubles the shared memory the kernel needs, which lowers occupancy. So running this kernel in fp32 is inherently slower than fp16. It is still far faster than the only correct option this path had before, which was to fall back to the CPU. That slowdown is not a reason to leave it broken. The kernel is an active code path, and this is current hardware, not a legacy quirk: it was caught on an RDNA4 Radeon AI PRO R9700. Any build without rocWMMA flash-attention lands here, and the hardware affected worst is anything with no matrix cores at all, such as the RDNA2 generation, which cannot use rocWMMA and so has the tile kernel as its only attention path, with no faster option to switch to. All of them silently produce a ghosted image. GPUs that do have the matrix-core path keep using it and are unaffected. For everyone on the fallback, a small and correct slowdown is far better than a fast and wrong result.
