- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.

- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.

## Research Stage
- [x] Background Research
- [x] Hypothesis Formed
- [x] Strategy / Implementation Forming
- [x] Analysis of results
- [ ] Debrief / Documentation

## Previous existing literature and research

The bellow is a result of trying to reduce my decode bottleneck and profiling it, noticing that a large piece of it is coming from the draft itself.

For large-vocabulary models, the draft model's LM-head projection (`hidden -> vocab_size`) is a significant fraction of per-step draft cost in speculative decoding, independent of the draft transformer's own size. **FR-Spec** (Zhao, Pan, Han et al., ACL 2025, arXiv:2502.14856) addresses this directly: restrict the draft's candidate search to a frequency-ranked subset of the vocabulary (e.g. top 32,768 of a 100k+ vocab), cutting LM-head compute by ~75% while the target model still verifies over the *full* vocabulary, so the output distribution is provably unchanged (lossless, same guarantee as standard speculative sampling).

SGLang already ships this for EAGLE-style drafters via `--speculative-token-map`: a `hot_token_id` tensor gathers the draft's `lm_head` rows down to the hot set at load time, and after the draft's topk sampling, predicted indices are remapped back to real vocab IDs (`topk_index = hot_token_id[topk_index]`) before being used downstream ([`eagle_worker_v2.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py), lines ~336-338 and ~594-595 as of this writing).

llama.cpp's own EAGLE-3 implementation ([`src/models/eagle3.cpp`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/src/models/eagle3.cpp)) already has the equivalent machinery for a *different reason* — handling a draft model whose native vocabulary is smaller than the target's. It carries a `d2t` ("draft-to-target") tensor, auto-sized from the GGUF (`d2t_meta->ne[0]`), and after the draft head's matmul it scatters the compressed logits into a full-vocab tensor (filled `-inf` elsewhere) via `ggml_set_rows`, so every downstream consumer (sampler, verify path) only ever sees full-vocab-shaped, correctly-indexed logits.

The native MTP path (`--spec-type draft-mtp`, landed in #22673) has no equivalent — every MTP-capable architecture I checked (`qwen35.cpp`, `qwen35moe.cpp`, `step35.cpp`, `glm4-moe.cpp`, `bailingmoe2.cpp`) hardcodes the MTP head's output tensor (`nextn.shared_head_head`, or `model.output` when that's absent) to the trunk's full `n_vocab`.

## Hypothesis

`d2t` is architecture-agnostic infrastructure, not EAGLE-3-specific. If a standalone MTP-only draft GGUF ships a `d2t` tensor, the same trim-at-load + scatter-after-matmul pattern EAGLE-3 already uses should let native MTP drafters use a frequency-ranked vocab subset too — with the same lossless guarantee (target still verifies full vocab) and the same kind of LM-head-cost reduction FR-Spec reports.

## Strategy / Implementation

Implemented and tested for `qwen35.cpp` (covers Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6 dense MTP). Branch: https://github.com/avifenesh/llama.cpp/tree/frspec-mtp-vocab-trim (commit `047bfa508`).

The change is ~30 lines, gated so it's a no-op for every existing GGUF:
- In `load_arch_tensors`: if the draft is MTP-only (`mtp_only`) and a `d2t` tensor is present in the GGUF, size `output.weight` from `d2t->ne[0]` instead of `n_vocab`, and load `d2t` via the same `LLM_TENSOR_D2T` tensor name EAGLE-3 already uses.
- In the MTP head's graph build (after `build_lora_mm(head_w, ...)`): if `model.d2t` is set, scatter the compressed logits back to full-vocab shape with `ggml_set_rows`, identical to the existing code in `eagle3.cpp`.
- No changes needed in `common/speculative.cpp` — the scatter happens inside the compute graph, so the draft sampling loop never has to be aware the head was trimmed (verified empirically: the EAGLE-3 draft loop already has zero `d2t`-aware code, for the same reason).

A draft GGUF with a trimmed `output.weight` + a `d2t` tensor was produced offline with `gguf-py` (gather the `output.weight` rows by a frequency-ranked token-ID list, store that list as `d2t`). No `convert_hf_to_gguf.py` producer path exists yet — this issue is about the consumer/loader side and whether the approach is worth pursuing before building that out.

The frequency map itself was built from two sources for reproducibility:
1. A 1GB, 50/50 code-prose corpus from public HF datasets (`codeparrot/codeparrot-clean-valid`, `codeparrot/github-jupyter-code-to-text`, `Salesforce/wikitext` wikitext-103, `allenai/c4` en, `HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu`), tokenized with the target model's own tokenizer, top-32768 by raw frequency.
2. A code-only corpus from my own agent/coding-session logs (not reproducible by others, included only as a private-workload data point, not part of the proposal).

## Analysis

Hardware: Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 trunk + Q6_K MTP draft GGUF (`--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3`), single RTX 5090 Laptop, 128k ctx, K=q8_0/V=q5_1 cache.

**Kernel-level (Nsight Systems, isolated decode window, same prompt before/after):**
| | baseline (full 248,320-vocab head) | trimmed (32,768 hot vocab) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mul_mat_vec_q` (Q6_K, draft LM-head, batch=1) | 407.1 ms / 655 calls | 61.6 ms / 675 calls | **-84.9%** |
| avg latency per call | 621 µs | 91 µs | -85.3% |

That matches FR-Spec's reported ~75% LM-head-compute reduction (32768/248320 ≈ 7.6x fewer rows; measured ≈6.6x time reduction — close given other fixed per-call overhead).

**End-to-end decode throughput**, wide bench (6 code + 4 prose prompts, temp=0, `n-max=3`):
| draft / vocab map | code mean tok/s | prose mean tok/s | overall mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (no trim) | 88.4 | 77.2 | 83.9 |
| trimmed, public 50/50 corpus | 89.6 | 78.3 | 85.1 |
| trimmed, private code-heavy corpus | 93.4 | 76.1 | 86.5 |

The public, reproducible 50/50 map improves *both* code and prose over baseline. A code-weighted map trades some prose acceptance for a bigger code win — expected, sin

## Overview

`llama-imatrix` only runs forward passes through the trunk, so MTP draft head tensors (`blk.<n_layer>.nextn.eh_proj` etc., added by #22673) never receive activations and have no imatrix data. Low-bit i-quants for those tensors then fail at quantize-time:

  llama_model_quantize: failed to quantize: Missing importance matrix for
  tensor blk.40.nextn.eh_proj.weight in a very low-bit quantization

This adds an opt-in `--mtp` flag to `llama-imatrix`. When set and the loaded model has MTP/NextN layers, a second `llama_context` is created with `ctx_type = LLAMA_CONTEXT_TYPE_MTP`. After each trunk sub-batch decode, the trunk's pre-norm hidden states are paired with the next-token ids and decoded through the MTP context, mirroring how `common_speculative_state_draft_mtp::process()` invokes the head during real spec decoding. MTP-layer tensors then land in the same imatrix collector via the existing eval callback.

Default behavior unchanged. No-op (with warning) for models without MTP layers. Currently restricted to `n_seq == 1` to keep MTP-row-to- output-row mapping unambiguous; warns and disables itself otherwise.

Adds a small public accessor `llama_model_n_nextn(model)` so callers outside `src/` can probe MTP presence without pulling in `llama_hparams`.

## Requirements

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

The `llama-server` fails to reuse the KV cache for subsequent requests in the same chat session. On the second request to the same slot, it forces a full prompt re-processing, logging: `forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data (likely due to SWA or hybrid/recurrent memory)`. As a result, the model "forgets" the conversation history.

This occurs on different models (Qwen 3.5 MoE, Gemma 4 MoE), different llama.cpp versions (b8025, b8769), and even with minimal context (e.g., 45 tokens). The issue is reproducible with direct `curl` requests, ruling out client-side problems.

**Steps to reproduce:**

items.body:
### Name and Version

$ llama-cli --version
version: 9924 (90e0f5cfc)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64


### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

GPU: 5x NVIDIA CUDA (2x RTX 3090, RTX 5060 Ti, 2x RTX 4060 Ti), 96 GiB total VRAM
CPU: Intel Core i5-13600K (14 cores / 20 threads)
RAM: 128 GB DDR4-3200
OS: Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04)

### Models

DeepSeek-V4-Flash (DSV4-Flash), GGUF, MXFP4 quant, 5 shards.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

During an agentic coding session, after several turns, I get a crash with a false "Context size has been exceeded" at ~1250 tokens against a 16k context. It's SWA find_slot exhaustion of the 768-cell window, not a real context limit, with 0 CUDA errors (no OOM/abort).

Also, before the crash, throughout the session every divergent turn stalls. Every divergent turn re-prefills thousands of tokens from a checkpoint boundary instead of just the delta, so the agent sits on "Working" with nothing streaming. The same churn eventually crashes.

Both fall out of the same no-partial-rollback limitation; one proper seq_rm of the diverged suffix fixes both.

The window full so no slot even at ~1250 tokens, not a real ctx limit, 0 CUDA errors proves it's not a GPU fault.

The root cause:

DSV4-Flash raw attention is a 128-token sliding window on a 768-cell SWA KV cache, the only cache find_slot runs on. find_slot reuses an occupied cell only if SWA-masked. Also the same sequence causal reuse path is commented out (src/llama-kv-cache.cpp ~1043-1047) on the invariant "purge futures beforehand."

Normal models satisfy that with seq_rm(seq_id, n_past, -1) before re-decoding a divergent suffix. DSV4 can't do a partial seq_rm (src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp ~1153). The compressor ring state can't roll back mid-block. So the server rewinds via a checkpoint-restore that repopulates the SWA window without purging futures.

The crash: re decode refills positions inside the full 768-cell window and find_slot can neither reuse the occupied same-seq cells nor reclaim the live top ~128 window cells resulting in a false "context exceeded."

The stall: The same no partial rollback. Every divergent turn re prefills from a checkpoint boundary, no delta path.

The defect is in shared KV / server code not a CUDA kernel. Having no CUDA errors backs this so it's expected across backends.

A monotonic growing prompt never jams and the band probe reached 119,788 tokens clean. The crash needs reuse that re-fills occupied cells, not raw depth.

Reproduce with:

churn.py:
```python
import urllib.request, urllib.error, json, random, time
URL="http://127.0.0.1:10099/v1/completions"
random.seed(11)
def sent(i): return f"Paragraph {i}: quick brown fox {i} leaps over lazy dog {i}, counting {i} apples, {i} pears, {i} plums in crate {i} now. "
def comp(prompt,n=8):
    data=json.dumps({"prompt":prompt,"max_tokens":n,"cache_prompt":True,"temperature":0.6}).encode()
    req=urllib.request.Request(URL,data=data,headers={"Content-Type":"application/json"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req,timeout=600) as r: return r.status, r.read().decode()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: return e.code, e.read().decode()
    except Exception as e: return -1, str(e)
MAXLINES=340; lines=[]; peak=0; t0=time.time()
for it in range(1200):
    if len(lines)>=MAXLINES:
        lines=lines[:random.randint(30, 90)]          # DEEP rewind from high depth -> strands high-pos cells
    elif lines and random.random()<0.6:
        lines[-1]=("d",it)                             # shallow divergence -> checkpoint rewind
    lines.append(("a",it))
    prompt="".join(sent(hash(x)%99999) for x in lines)
    st,body=comp(prompt)
    if st==-1: print(f"[NETERR] it={it} {body[:150]}",flush=True); continue
    if st>=500 or "exceed" in body.lower():
        print(f"[JAM] it={it} elapsed={time.time()-t0:.0f}s lines={len(lines)} peak_ptok={peak} status={st} body={body[:200]}",flush=True); break
    try:
        u=json.loads(body).get("usage",{}); pt=u.get("prompt_tokens",0); peak=max(peak,pt)
        if it%10==0: print(f"it={it} t={time.time()-t0:.0f}s lines={len(lines)} ptok={pt} peak={peak}",flush=True)
    except Exception as e: print(f"[PARSE] it={it} {body[:100]}",flush=True)
else: print(f"[NOJAM] done 1200 iters peak_ptok={peak}",flush=True)
print("FIN",flush=True)
```

```bash
# 1. isolated debug server: small ctx, KV-cache debug on (substitute your own DSV4-Flash GGUF path)
CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4 GGML_CUDA_NO_PINNED=1 LLAMA_KV_CACHE_DEBUG=2 ./llama-server --port 10099 --host 127.0.0.1 --flash-attn on --jinja --parallel 1 --model <DSV4-Flash GGUF, shard 1 of 5> --ctx-size 16384 --ubatch-size 512 --fit on --fit-ctx 16384 --fit-target 1024,1024,2048,2048,2048 --no-mmap --temp 0.6 --top-p 0.95 -lv 5
# wait for {"status":"ok"} on /health

# 2. drive the churn (grows depth, then deep-rewinds into the checkpoint-restore path)
python3 churn.py     # seed=11, targets :10099/v1/completions
```

**Fix branch**

EDIT: I did another rebase and rework. The current branch is https://github.com/TacoTakumi/llama.cpp/tree/dsv4-rs-rollback

A fix branch is up at https://github.com/TacoTakumi/llama.cpp/tree/dsv4-swa-churn-fix
A proper seq_rm of the diverged suffix so only the delta re-prefills, which removes both symptoms. This builds on @danielhanchen's own DeepSeek-V4 Checkpointing fix (PR #25402) and is forked from commit 15f732183. A PR may follow depending on maintainer interest.

**AI assistance**

I'm a 30+ year experience software developer and sysadmin. Claude Fable xhigh meaningfully assisted the root cause analysis, the reproduction, and iterating the fix, under my direction. I reviewed every line, understand it, and can explain any part.

**Not a duplicate**

This is not a duplicate of any of these issues:
- #25320 (issue) general 3x slow prompt processing, not DSV4, no crash
- #25416 (PR) checkpoint timing / tool role, different scope
- #254

items.body:
### Summary

`--spec-type draft-dflash` works well at low concurrency, but under concurrent slots the **draft model's predictions get corrupted**, draft acceptance collapses, and throughput goes into reverse (slower than no speculation). We traced this on an AMD gfx1151 APU across two ROCm versions and pinned down that the corruption **scales with the number of concurrently-drafting sequences, not with batch token count, server slot count, or draft length alone**:

| server `-np` | active requests | `--spec-draft-n-max` | noise-block batch | per-slot draft acceptance | aggregate throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 4 | 15 | 64 tok | **0.51 – 0.66** (healthy) | healthy |
| **16** | **4** | 15 | 64 tok | **0.51 – 0.66** (bit-identical to the row above, same seed) | healthy |
| 8 | 8 | 15 | 128 tok | 0.11 – 0.46 (degraded) | degraded |
| 16 | 16 | 7 | 128 tok | 0.22 – 0.74 (bimodal) | bad |
| 16 | 16 | 15 | 256 tok | **0.06 – 0.49** (bimodal; sustained load collapses to **0.0018**) | ~17–21 tok/s vs **37 tok/s** no-spec baseline |
| 16 | 16 | **1** | 32 tok | **0.83 – 0.92** | **~80 tok/s (2.2× the no-spec baseline)** |

Key observations that localize the defect:

1. **Per-slot corruption is established during prefill and persists for the request's lifetime.** 16 *identical* requests (same prompt, seed, temperature) produce an ~8× spread in acceptance across slots, visible from the very first speculative tick. The draft model's top-1 confidence is bimodal per slot: median 0.25 on "broken" slots vs 0.92–0.98 on "healthy" ones.
2. **It is not the server's slot configuration** — a `-np 16` server with only 4 in-flight requests produces bit-identical results to a `-np 4` server.
3. **It is not the drafter's intrinsic quality** — with `--spec-draft-n-max 1` the same 16-way load accepts 83–92 % of drafts and beats the no-spec baseline by 2.2×.
4. **It is not a ROCm-version regression** — identical pathology on ROCm 7.2.1 and 7.14.0 (we cannot test CUDA here; see "ask" at the end).

### Git commit

- Verified at `0b1bad14ff204627636aeb1de22ddcd5acb859d4` (2026-08-11).
- **Still reproduces on current master `0177dcc7300bad8914bb838baabce87899812491` (2026-08-15, freshly built)**: 16 identical concurrent requests → the same bimodal per-slot acceptance (0.05–0.50, broken slots waste 500–977 drafts per 160-token request); the 4-concurrent control on the same server recovers (0.19–0.61). The numbers below are from the pinned build.

Build: `-DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DROCM_PATH=…` (Release, GCC 13.3, `GGML_HIP_GRAPHS=ON` default).

Hardware/runtime: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S iGPU (gfx1151, 96 GB unified), kernel 6.17, ROCm 7.14.0 (side-by-side 7.2.1 with identical results).

Models: Muse-Glimmer-30B target (Q4_K "kquant" GGUF, ~17 GB, all layers on GPU) + the matching DFlash draft GGUF (`general.architecture = dflash`, 5 layers, `block_size=16`, 5 extracted target layers). Any supported dense target + DFlash pair should reproduce the concurrency dependence.

### Command line

```bash
llama-server -m muse-glimmer-30B-kquant-17gb.gguf -ngl 999 \
  -np 16 -c 131072 --jinja \
  -md dflash-kquant.gguf -ngld 99 \
  --spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 15 \
  --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 64 --seed 42 \
  --port 8080 > server.log 2>&1
```

Reproduce (the server log is the instrument — `/metrics` spec counters stay 0 on these builds):

```bash
# 16 identical concurrent streaming requests
seq 16 | xargs -P16 -I{} curl -sN http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Explain in detail why the sky is blue."}],
       "max_tokens":160,"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95,"top_k":64,"seed":42}' >/dev/null

grep 'draft acceptance' server.log
```

Controls (each on a fresh server):

- `-P4` instead of `-P16` (same `-np 16` server) → acceptance recovers to ~0.5–0.66.
- `--spec-draft-n-max 1` with `-P16` → acceptance 0.83–0.92, ~2.2× no-spec throughput.
- `-np 4` server, `-P4` → bit-identical to the `-np 16`/`-P4` run (same seed).

### Problem description & logs

Expected: draft acceptance roughly constant w.r.t. concurrency (speculative decoding is lossless; batching drafts from many sequences should not change per-sequence predictions), and DFlash at `-np 16` to at least not be slower than no speculation.

Actual (16 identical concurrent requests, fresh server, `0b1bad1`):

```
slot print_timing: id  1 | draft acceptance = 0.05333 (    4 accepted /    75 generated), mean len =  1.80
slot print_timing: id  7 | draft acceptance = 0.25424 (   45 accepted /   177 generated), mean len =  3.50
slot print_timing: id 10 | draft acceptance = 0.49074 (   53 accepted /   108 generated), mean len =  6.89
slot print_timing: id 12 | draft acceptance = 0.19048 (   44 accepted /   231 generated), mean len =  3.44
slot print_timing: id  0 | draft acceptance = 0.07289 (   32 accepted /   439 generated), mean len =  2.03
...
spec statistics: draft-dflash: #calls(b,g,a) = 16 31 294, #gen tokens = 3758, #acc tokens = 509,
                #mean acc len = 2.73, dur(b,g,a) = 0.020, 4133.404, 0.072 ms
```

Under sustained long-generation load this collapses completely — a 16×512, 5-rep run on ROCm 7.2.1 was aborted after 5 h 16 min with **3,270,000 drafted / 6,060 accepted (0.18 %)**.

Secondary symptoms at `-np 16` (measured on the same runs):

- Prompt processing with DFlash injection runs at ~57 ms/token (~17.5 tok/s) vs ~23 ms/token (~43 tok/s) without DFlash at the same `-np` — the per-sequence sequential `llama_encode` + inject `llama_decode` in `process()` is paid once per sequence per batch.
- Steady-state speculative tick is 1.15–1.5 s; `draft()` alone averages 133 ms per call (256-token noise block); per-token time grows ~3× over a 320-token request (207 → 570 ms/token), i.e. it decays as generations lengthen.
- The HIP backend logs `CUDA graph warmup reset` 1–2× per tick (54–194 per run) as batch composition chang

### Name and Version

version: 9668 (32120c10e)
built with MSVC 19.44.35225.0 for x64

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

Ryzen 7950X  &  NVIDIA RTX 3090 

### Models

huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-GGUF/Qwen3.6-27B-IQ4_NL.gguf

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Problem description

The model loads and runs normally after server startup. However, if the model remains idle long enough to be unloaded from VRAM (or otherwise released by the server's idle memory management), subsequent requests cause a CUDA failure during the first inference after the model is reloaded.

The error occurs consistently after the idle → unload (sleeping mode) → reload cycle and does not occur immediately after startup.

The failure happens during the forward pass with the following error:

```
ggml_cuda_compute_forward: MUL_MAT failed
CUDA error: invalid argument
```

The model can be loaded successfully, all initialization steps complete normally, and the crash only appears when processing the first request after the model has been unloaded and reloaded.


## Steps to reproduce
The full settings will be listed here:
<details>
<summary>Settings</summary>

```console
[*]
models-max = 1
sleep-idle-seconds = 120

ctx-size = 72000

ngl = -1

threads = 12
threads-batch = 12

mmap = true
flash-attn = auto

cache-type-k = q8_0
cache-type-v = q8_0

[Qwen27B/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP]
m = ./...
mmproj = ./...

spec-type = ngram-mod,draft-mtp

spec-ngram-mod-n-match = 24
spec-ngram-mod-n-min = 16
spec-ngram-mod-n-max = 48

spec-draft-n-max = 3

temperature=1.0
top-p=0.95
top-k=20
min-p=0.0
presence-penalty=0.0
repeat-penalty=1.0
```

</details>

Then here is the steps: 

- Set `sleep-idle-seconds` for models, where the model I used is Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-IQ4_NL.
- Load the model successfully and verify that inference works normally. (Triggering this issue may require a longer context). 
- Leave the server idle long enough for the model to be unloaded from VRAM (or enter sleeping state).
- Send a new inference request.
- Observe that the model reloads successfully.
- During the first generation request after reload, CUDA will fail.

## Additional problem in older version

In versions earlier than b9557 ( the version I used is b9555 ), the issue does not result in an immediate error. Instead, after exiting sleep mode and reloading the model, inference performance drops significantly, suggesting that the model may not be fully loaded onto the GPU or that some computations are no longer being executed on the GPU as expected. The corresponding logs are also included in the Log Output section below.


### First Bad Commit

items.body:
For models that share tensors with another model through ctx_other (e.g. Gemma4Assistant, Eagle3, DFlash, DSpark), add the other model's device backends to the context scheduler so that pre-allocated shared tensors (tok_embd, output) can be scheduled. Fixes an abort when the speculative draft model uses a device list that does not cover the GPU holding the target model's output projection.

Assisted-by: opencode

## Overview

## Bug (observed behavior)
- Abort during llama_context construction: "pre-allocated tensor (output.weight) in a buffer (CUDA10) that cannot run the operation (NONE)"
- Location: ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp (line ~898/930 depending on version), called from llama_context::sched_reserve -> graph_reserve -> resolve_fused_ops
- Trigger: speculative decoding with ctx_other (draft-dspark / draft-dflash / draft-mtp), draft model on its own device via --device-draft/--spec-draft-device, target model on other GPU(s)
- Root cause : the draft context scheduler only had backends for the draft's own devices; shared pre-allocated tensors (tok_embd/output.weight, taken from the target model via ctx_other in src/models/dflash.cpp) live in buffers on the target's devices; scheduler found no backend for those buffers and aborted

## Reproduction (your setup)
- llama-server in router mode, model preset:
  - device = CUDA3,CUDA4,CUDA5,CUDA7,CUDA8,CUDA9,CUDA10 (--split-mode layer)
  - spec-type = draft-dspark, spec-draft-n-max = 8
  - spec-draft-device = CUDA0
  - model-draft = dspark/dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf
- Before fix: GGML_ABORT, spec model failed to load
- After fix: draft context logs "adding backend for device CUDA3..CUDA10: shared tensors with the other model (e.g. tok_embd, output)", speculative implementation 'draft-dspark' initializes (n_max=8, block_size=5), server healthy
- Verified with CI-built image version 10282 (34ec9c9bb) on 15-GPU host (RTX 3080/4080/4090/3090), CUDA 12, 16x 3090-class workload


## Additional information

## Related issues
- #26475 - "using -devd CUDA0 on draft-dspark causes model to crash": same abort message (output.weight, CUDA8), same stack, draft-dspark + tensor split. Directly matches. (open)
- #24492 - Gemma 4 31B MTP, Vulkan: "pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l58) ... cannot run the operation (NONE)" - same abort class, ctx_other/KV sharing; mechanism may differ (Vulkan backend support), unknown whether fixed
- #24366 - Gemma MTP, tensor split, buffer "Meta()": same abort class; unknown whether fixed
- #26339 - "Dspark model fails to load with -sm tensor on MI50": possible same class; unknown
 
## Requirements

items.body:
## Overview The Q4_K/Q5_K scale unpack branches on a runtime value to pick between two layouts. nvcc can't fold that, so it predicates it and then repeats the whole thing for every column of the ncols_dst loop instead of doing it once. Swapping the branch for a mask select fixes it: predicated instructions at ncols_dst=8 go from 226 to 34, and the Q4_K kernel at 16 columns from 2256 to 1648. None of the other quant types have this problem, they already unpack unconditionally (Q3_K does the same 6-bit layout with plain shifts). We see perf gains from batch size >=4 on RTX 5090 and >=5 on RTX 4090 (more details in the Performance drop down), however we do not see a gain with DGX Spark, and in fact a small regression at batch sizes 4-6, which is why the change is gated off there. The most probable reason for this can be that the memory bandwidth on DGX Spark is much lower than that of RTX 4090 or 5090, and this means even with this optimization there is no effective time to save, since in the original code the unpack was already running while the kernel waits on the weight loads and so was not adding to the total time.
Performance

## Benchmarks (RTX 5090, sm_120, CUDA 12.9, driver 620.23) Both builds are from the same commit; the only difference is this patch. Batch size below refers to `ne11`, the number of columns the matmul receives in a single forward pass. It can arise in three ways, which are indistinguishable to the kernel: N concurrent requests against a server started with `-np N`, a draft block of `n_max + 1` tokens on a single slot, or `llama-bench -p N` directly. Two rows per model. `decode` is `llama-bench -p N -n 0 -embd 1 -r 40`, a single forward pass of N tokens with nothing generated, which is the decode step at batch N. `end to end` is llama-server tokens/sec, which also includes prefill, sampling and the draft model, and is therefore always lower. `*` marks a quant type this patch does not modify. ### 1. vs batch size Llama-3.1-8B, no draft model; only `-np` changes. The llama-server figures are total tokens over wall time at 256 tokens per request, temperature 0, across 3 runs alternating between the two builds. The request count is always a multiple of the batch size so that the final wave is not partially filled. | quant | metric | batch 1 | batch 2 | batch 4 | batch 8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Q4_K_M** | decode | **-0.3%** | **+1.6%** | **+8.9%** | **+14.7%** | | | end to end | +0.4% | +1.1% | +7.4% | +10.8% | | **Q5_K_M** | decode | **+0.4%** | **+2.0%** | **+6.6%** | **+14.2%** | | | end to end | -0.1% | +1.5% | +5.5% | +11.4% | | **Q6_K** * | decode | **-1.2%** | **-1.1%** | **-0.8%** | **-0.9%** | | | end to end | -0.1% | +0.2% | +0.3% | +0.2% | There is no effect at batch 1, which is expected: the unpack can only be amortised once there is more than one column to share it across. ### 2. Other models Batch pinned at 4, no draft model. | model | metric | Q4_K_M | Q5_K_M | Q6_K * | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Llama-3.1-8B** | decode | **+8.9%** | **+6.6%** | **-0.8%** | | | end to end | +7.4% | +5.5% | +0.3% | | **gemma-4-12B** | decode | **+8.2%** | **+6.3%** | **+0.0%** | | | end to end | +6.8% | +6.0% | +0.1% | | **Qwen3.6-27B** | decode | **+6.2%** | **+5.1%** | **+0.3%** | | | end to end | +8.0% | +4.2% | +0.5% | ### 3. Batch from a draft block instead of concurrent requests `--spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 3` on a single slot, so the target verifies 4 tokens in one pass: batch 4 obtained from a draft block rather than from concurrency. The decode rows repeat table 2 because it is the same file at the same batch; the kernel is indifferent to the source of the batch. | model | metric | Q4_K_M | Q5_K_M | Q6_K * | |---|---|---|---|---| | **gemma-4-12B-it** | decode | **+8.2%** | **+6.3%** | **+0.0%** | | | end to end | +6.3% | +6.2% | -0.7% | | **Qwen3.6-27B** | decode | **+6.2%** | **+5.1%** | **+0.3%** | | | end to end | +6.3% | +5.5% | +0.1% | ### 4. Decode over the whole batch range The same llama-bench run on `--pure` single-type models, so that every quantized `mul_mat` is the type in question. The Q4_K_M / Q5_K_M files above are mixed, with output and some attention tensors in Q6_K, which is why they report lower gains. | type | batch 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Q4_K** | +1.0% | +3.6% | +6.7% | +13.6% | +17.0% | +19.0% | +17.5% | +17.4% | | **Q5_K** | -0.6% | +2.0% | +1.7% | +9.3% | +10.3% | +16.8% | +15.9% | +17.2% | | **Q6_K** * | +0.3% | +0.4% | -1.0% | -0.5% | -0.8% | -0.4% | -1.6% | -0.6% | | **Q8_0** * | +1.1% | +0.3% | +1.0% | +1.3% | +1.0% | +1.8% | +1.9% | +1.7% | ## Benchmarks (RTX 4090, sm_89, CUDA 12.9, driver 591.86) Both builds are from the same commit; the only difference is this patch. Conventions are as above: `decode` is `llama-bench -p N -n 0 -embd 1 -r 40`, `end to end` is llama-server tokens/sec at 256 tokens per request, temperature 0. `*` marks a quant type this patch does not modify. Clocks were pinned, no interactive session was present on the machine, and the base build was run at both ends of every pass so that the noise floor is measured rather than assumed. Batch size throughout refers to `ne11`, the number of columns the matmul receives in a single forward pass. It can arise in three ways, which are indistinguishable to the kernel: N concurrent requests against a server started with `-np N`, a draft block of `n_max + 1` tokens on a single slot, or `llama-bench -p N` directly. Tables 1, 2 and 4 use the first and third; table 3 uses the second. ### 1. vs batch size Llama-3.1-8B, no draft model. Decode rows use `-p N`; end-to-end rows use `-np N` with the request count kept a multiple of N so that all slots remain occupied. | quant | metric | batch 1 | batch 2 | batch 4 | batch 8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Q4_K_M** | decode | **+0.0%** |

items.body:
## Summary
We maintain a Rust llama.cpp host (in-process via the llama-cpp-rs bindings — no llama-server subprocess). We cannot use any of llama.cpp's speculative-decoding machinery (including the new DeepSeek V4 DSpark path from #25784) because it lives entirely in the `common/` layer, which is tied to llama-server's main loop.

## The gap
As of `596a579` (and latest master), the core `llama.h` API exposes no speculative params:
- `llama_model_params` has no `draft_model` / spec fields.
- `llama_context_params` has no spec fields.
- There is no `llama_speculative_*` init function in the public API.

DSpark (and MTP) support is implemented in `common/speculative.cpp` / the server layer only. A library consumer that links llama.cpp and drives `llama_decode` directly cannot:
- load a draft model alongside the target, or
- enable `--spec-type draft-dspark` style speculation, or
- benefit from DSpark's Markov/confidence-head draft at all.

## Ask
A minimal core-API speculative surface for in-process hosts, e.g.:
- `llama_model_params.draft_model` (+ spec type / draft-n-max) re-added, OR
- a `llama_speculative_*` API that manages draft+target contexts and exposes a `llama_decode_speculative`-style call.

We (and likely other language bindings that bypass llama-server) would be happy to test, provide repro cases, or contribute to a design/implementation. We already drive the bundled llama.cpp in production for DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (284B/13B MoE, `deepseek4` arch) and are currently forced to use our own draft→verify loop, which cannot use DSpark's confidence head.

## Context
- omm-ci (Rust server) tracks this as P1c; DSpark draft pairing via a custom greedy loop works but can't use the confidence head: https://github.com/thermodynamic-retard/omm-ci
- DSpark reference: #25784, #25167

Thanks for considering — happy to help move it forward.

## Overview

CUDA also fuses SOFTPLUS; tests already cover SILU/SIGMOID/SOFTPLUS.

## Additional information

version: 7464 (0a0bba05e)
built with Clang 20.0.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
./llama-server -m /home/user/Models/lmstudio-community/gpt-oss-120b-GGUF/gpt-oss-120b-MXFP4-00001-of-00002.gguf \
    -t 4 \
    -c 131072 \
    -n 8192 \
    --parallel 10 \
    --cont-batching \
    --jinja \
    --reasoning-format deepseek \
    --chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort": "low", "reasoning_format": "auto"}' \
    --n-gpu-layers 999 \
    --swa-full \
    --flash-attn on \
    -b 2048 \
    -ub 2048 \
    --no-mmap \
    --cache-type-k q8_0 \
    --cache-type-v q8_0 \
    --cache-ram 0 \
    --cache-reuse 256 \
    --defrag-thold 0.1 \
    --temp 1.0 \
    --top-p 1.0 \
    --top-k 0 \
    --min-p 0 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8888 \
    --api-key "okokok"
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Summary

The UMA (Unified Memory Architecture) detection introduced in PR #17368 incorrectly identifies AMD APUs (such as Strix Halo) as UMA systems and limits the available GPU memory to system RAM's `MemAvailable`, ignoring the much larger TTM (Translation Table Manager) memory allocation that AMD APUs can utilize.

## Environment

- **Hardware**: AMD Strix Halo APU (gfx1151)
- **GPU Memory**: 96GB TTM allocation via kernel boot parameters
- **System RAM**: 32GB
- **OS**: Ubuntu Linux with kernel 6.14.0
- **ROCm Version**: 7.9.0
- **llama.cpp Version**: Latest master (commit 0a0bba05e)

### Kernel Boot Parameters
```
amdgpu.gttsize=98304 ttm.pages_limit=25000000 ttm.page_pool_size=12000000
```

## Problem Description

After PR #17368 (DGX Spark: UMA support), the `ggml_backend_cuda_device_get_memory()` function checks `prop.integrated > 0` to detect UMA systems. When detected as UMA, it reads available memory from `/proc/meminfo` instead of using `cudaMemGetInfo()`.

**The issue**: AMD APUs report `integrated = true`, but they can utilize significantly more memory than system RAM through TTM. In my case:
- System RAM available: ~27GB
- Actual GPU memory available via TTM: **96GB**

This causes the new `llama_params_fit` auto-fitting logic to incorrectly calculate that there isn't enough memory, resulting in:
1. Context size being reduced from 131072 to 4096
2. Model layers being offloaded to CPU unnecessarily
3. Significant performance degradation

## Logs

### Before patch (incorrect behavior):
```
llama_params_fit_impl: projected to use 64909 MiB of device memory vs. 98304 MiB of free device memory
llama_params_fit_impl: cannot fulfill margin of 1024 MiB, need to reduce device memory by 37767 MiB
llama_params_fit_impl: context size reduced from 131072 to 4096
llama_params_fit_impl: ROCm0 (AMD Radeon Graphics): 36 layers (21 overflowing), 27049 MiB used
```

### After patch (correct behavior):
```
llama_params_fit_impl: projected to use 64909 MiB of device memory vs. 98304 MiB of free device memory
llama_params_fit_impl: will leave 33092 >= 1024 MiB of free device memory, no changes needed
```

## Root Cause

In `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu`, the `ggml_backend_cuda_device_get_memory()` function:

```cpp
#if defined(__linux__)
    cudaDeviceProp prop;
    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&prop, ctx->device));

    bool uma_env = getenv("GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY") != nullptr;
    bool is_uma = prop.integrated > 0 || uma_env;  // <-- AMD APUs hit this

    if (is_uma) {
        // Uses /proc/meminfo which returns ~27GB instead of 96GB TTM
        if (ggml_backend_cuda_get_available_uma_memory(&available_memory_kb, &free_swap_kb) && available_memory_kb > 0) {
            *free = (size_t)available_memory_kb * 1024;
        }
    }
#endif
```

## Proposed Fix

Skip the UMA memory detection for ROCm/HIP builds, as AMD APUs with TTM can report accurate memory via `hipMemGetInfo()`:

```diff
-#if defined(__linux__)
+#if defined(__linux__) && !defined(GGML_USE_HIP)
     // Check if this is a UMA (Unified Memory Architecture) system
+    // Note: Skip this for ROCm/HIP - AMD APUs with large TTM allocations (e.g., Strix Halo)
+    // report integrated=true but can use much more memory via TTM than system RAM
     cudaDeviceProp prop;
     CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&prop, ctx->device));
     ...
-#endif // defined(__linux__)
+#endif // defined(__linux__) && !defined(GGML_USE_HIP)
```

## Alternative Solutions

1. **Environment variable override**: Add an env var like `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_UMA_DETECTION` to skip UMA detection
2. **TTM-aware detection for AMD**: Check `/sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_vram_total` or similar for AMD GPUs
3. **Compare reported vs actual**: If `cudaMemGetInfo` returns significantly more than `MemAvailable`, prefer `cudaMemGetInfo`

## Verification

With the proposed patch applied:
- `amd-smi` shows 65GB+ GPU memory usage (correct)
- Model loads with full 128K context
- All 36 layers stay on GPU
- No unnecessary CPU offloading

## Related

- PR #17368: DGX Spark: UMA support
- PR #17537: cuda: fix UMA detection on discrete GPUs

## System Information

```
$ amd-smi
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| AMD-SMI 26.1.0      ROCm version: 7.9.0                                      |
|-------------------------------------+----------------------------------------|
| 0000:c5:00.0    AMD Radeon Graphics |                          65XXX/98304 MB |
+-------------------------------------+----------------------------------------+

$ amd-ttm
Current TTM pages limit: 25000000 pages (95.37 GB)
Total system memory: 30.99 GB

$ cat /proc/cmdline
... amdgpu.gttsize=98304 ttm.pages_limit=25000000 ...
```


### First Bad Commit

_No response_

any quantization. Just depends, whether rpc is used

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

### Summary

A ROCm RPC worker on AMD gfx1151 aborts in `GGML_OP_TOP_K` while processing a sufficiently long DeepSeek V4 Flash prompt.

Short requests work correctly.

A long request consistently reaches exactly 4096 processed prompt tokens and then causes the remote ROCm RPC worker to abort with:

```text
ggml_cuda_compute_forward: TOP_K failed
ROCm error: invalid configuration argument
```

The client then reports:

```text
Remote RPC server crashed or returned malformed response
recv failed (bytes_recv=0, size_to_recv=8)
```

This is reproducible on both:

```text
TheRock / ROCm 7.13.0
TheRock / ROCm 7.14.0
```

using the same llama.cpp commit:

```text
3653e6d6d
```

Replacing only the remote ROCm RPC worker with a Vulkan/RADV RPC worker on the exact same Radeon 8060S / gfx1151 hardware makes the same setup stable.

Vulkan is significantly slower, but it does not crash.

### Difference from #24177

This appears related to #24177 because both failures involve the AMD `TOP_K` path and an RPC worker abort.

However, this case is different:

- `--no-spec-draft-backend-sampling` is already enabled.
- The failure occurs during prompt prefill, not draft-token backend sampling.
- Short prompts work.
- Long prompts reproducibly fail after 4096 processed prompt tokens.
- Reducing `--ubatch-size` from 256 to 128 does not change the failure point.
- Switching only the RPC worker backend from ROCm to Vulkan avoids the crash.

Therefore, the `--no-spec-draft-backend-sampling` workaround from #24177 does not avoid this failure.

### Server command

```bash
/usr/local/bin/llama-server \
  --model /opt/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/UD-IQ3_XXS/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00004.gguf \
  --alias deepseek-v4-flash-q3-xxs \
  --gpu-layers all \
  --fit off \
  --load-mode none \
  --ctx-size 1048576 \
  --parallel 4 \
  --jinja \
  --rpc 10.44.0.2:50053 \
  --split-mode layer \
  --tensor-split 1,1 \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 \
  --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --no-spec-draft-backend-sampling \
  --spec-draft-type-v q8_0 \
  --temp 1.0 \
  --top-p 0.95 \
  --min-p 0.0 \
  --top-k 0 \
  --spec-type draft-dspark \
  --model-draft /opt/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/UD-IQ3_XXS/dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf \
  --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
  --batch-size 1024 \
  --ubatch-size 128 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --flash-attn on \
  --port 5800
```

Remote worker:

```bash
ggml-rpc-server \
```

items.body:
## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

this adds several fixes for rpc and rocm related GPU paths additional tuning and fixes crashes, prefill issues and general compatibility. Fixes #26746

### Included changes relative to upstream

#### HIP, RPC and long-context routing

- Enables hipCUB for HIP top-k and argsort, including the distributed RPC execution
  path, so these operations remain GPU-capable on ROCm.
- Adds a gfx1151-local Lightning Indexer top-k specialization for 512, 1024 and 2048
  candidates up to 8192 score entries, avoiding the expensive generic device-wide sort
  during DeepSeek-V4 long-context prefill.
- Keeps the Lightning Indexer key cache in F16 when a quantized KV cache is selected,
  where required by the DeepSeek path.
- Resolves fused operations per layer and device instead of disabling an entire graph
  on a single ROCm/RPC backend mismatch; the default fallback remains unfused GPU work,
  not CPU work.
- Fixes the HIP MMVF dispatch for MoE LoRA `MUL_MAT_ID` tensors. Rank-1 LoRA-B
  expert matrices now use the existing general GPU fallback instead of entering an
  MMVF kernel which requires an even K dimension; this prevents RPC worker crashes
  with valid DeepSeek-V4 expert LoRA adapters.

#### Strix Halo compute tuning

- Adds RDNA3.5/gfx1151 kernel and launch tuning for MMQ, MMVQ, Q8 MoE and expert MMQ.
- Caches MMVQ Q8_1 activations and partitions MMQ waves across rows and columns.
- Adds AMD WMMA Lightning Indexer support and tuned tiled Flash Attention, including a
  fix for NaNs in the compacted-tile mask path.
- Tunes Gated Delta Net and adds quantized-KV Flash Attention support for Strix Halo.
- Extends the gfx1151 MMVQ selection to the relevant Q4/Q5/Q6/Q8 and MXFP4 decode
  types, including the Q6_K VDR=2 decode kernel.
- Keeps HIP integrated-GPU host-buffer handling safe.

#### DeepSeek-V4 and speculative decoding

- Makes the grouped output-projection input contiguous for small multi-token
  DeepSeek-V4 speculative batches.
- Uses matching MMVQ and Flash-Attention kernel configurations for decode and small
  speculative/MTP verification batches, preventing numerical divergence between the
  logits used for acceptance checks.
- Keeps fused DeepSeek-V4 HC and Gated Delta Net operations on devices that support
  them while safely falling back only for mismatching layers.

#### Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 and hybrid SSM models

- Fuses SSM gate/beta projections, the SSM convolution-output L2 norm, and the SSM
  pre-scan chain (convolution, L2 norm, gate/beta).
- Folds SSM convolution-input concatenation into QKV MMVQ and fuses paired MMVQ
  matmuls that share an activation.
- Caches graph-local Q8_1 matmul inputs, folds Q8_1 quantization into RMS norm and
  gating-MUL, and fuses a matmul-plus-add-through-view sequence.
- Folds MoE top-k weights into the down projection and fuses the shared-expert output
  chain.
- Fuses IMRoPE and set-rows for BF16 KV cache use, and aligns the attention-gate
  tensor-parallel split with attention-Q.

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

tested on a halo strix cluster setup (RPC, rocm 7.14).

## Requirements

rocm 7.14, hipcub-dev (build requirements)
ROCm/HIP with hipCUB, HIP/ROCm >= 6.1.
Build for gfx1151 (-DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151).

- AI usage disclosure: <!-- mention: YES / NO - if yes, describe how AI was used --> YES

OpenAI Codex GPT 5.6 Terra for tracing affected crash paths. Adding GPU fallback, instead of adding CPU fallback.

### Sources and provenance

- [@ggml-org](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) provides the upstream base. This
  branch is rebased on the exact upstream commit stated above.
- [@Patt92](https://github.com/Patt92/llama.cpp) maintains this integration branch and
  supplies the HIP RPC top-k/argsort patch, including the current HIP-only rank-1 MoE
  LoRA MMVF dispatch fix.
- [@Geramy](https://github.com/Geramy/llama.cpp) is the provenance for the original
  hipCUB/CUB-on-HIP top-k and argsort approach. Its useful HIP content was rebased
  into the Patt92 RPC patch; no older branch is required at build time.
- [@Nathanw1014](https://github.com/Nathanw1014/llama.cpp) supplies the selected
  Strix Halo/RDNA3.5 HIP tuning, DeepSeek-V4, Flash-Attention, MMQ/MMVQ and

- [@antirez](https://github.com/antirez/ds4) is the algorithmic source for the
  gfx1151-local Lightning Indexer top-k adaptation. Only the compatible HIP
  specialization is used; ds4 runtime, model and storage code is not included.
- [@stew675](https://github.com/stew675/llama.cpp) supplies the selected
  ROCm-compatible Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 and hybrid-SSM fusions, MMVQ tuning and
  speculative decode/verification consistency fixes.

### Name and Version

    $ llama-server --version
    version: 0.1.0-dev (build 10423, commit a94d563ed)
    built with IntelLLVM 2026.1.1 for Linux x86_64

Also reproduces on build 10289 (f9e832c10) and build 10050 (b15ca938a, 2026-07-16) — see comments below. This is not a new regression in 10423; it predates that build by at least a month and 10423 does not fix it.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

SYCL

### Hardware

Intel Core Ultra 7 258V (Lunar Lake), integrated Arc 140V graphics (Xe2-LPG), UMA (no discrete VRAM, 32 GB shared).

    $ llama-server --list-devices
    Available devices:
      SYCL0: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics (29223 MiB, 22596 MiB free)

oneAPI 2026.1.1, `xe` kernel driver, Ubuntu 24.04.

### Models

Reproduces on multiple, architecturally unrelated models — this does not look specific to any one architecture:

- `gemma4-v2` (gemma4 arch, both Q4_K_M and Q6_K quants)
- `gemma-4-12B-coder-fable5-composer2.5-v1.i1-IQ4_NL` (gemma4 arch)
- `Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-Q6_K` (qwen2 arch — plain dense model, no MoE, no known relation to DeepSeek/Gated-Delta-Net/Lightning-Indexer)

None of these are DeepSeek-V4 or Qwen3-Next/qwen35moe models, yet the crash is immediately preceded by `resolve_fused_ops` reporting several DeepSeek-V4/Gated-Delta-Net/Lightning-Indexer fused ops as **enabled** (not "not supported, set to disabled" as seen on other SYCL hardware in #26549).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` segfaults on the **first graph execution** (the built-in warmup pass, or the first real request if `--no-warmup` is used) whenever any GPU layers are offloaded (`-ngl` > 0), on this Lunar Lake iGPU. Model loading, tokenizer setup, and graph *reservation* (buffer sizing) all complete successfully — the crash is specifically in *executing* the compute graph, not building or sizing it.

`-ngl 0` (CPU-only, same model, same flags otherwise) loads and serves correctly, which rules out a corrupt GGUF or a general metadata-parsing bug and narrows this to the SYCL execution path.

Minimal repro (no server-side overrides, no third-party wrapper):

```shell
llama-server \
  -m gemma4-v2-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  -ngl 999 -c 2048 -t 4 -fa on \
  -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 \
  --port 8080 -lv 5
```

Isolation steps taken, none of which prevented the crash:
- `--fit off` (rules out the new auto-fit-to-device-memory feature)
- `--flash-attn off`
- `--no-warmup` (only moves the crash to the first real `/v1/chat/completions` request instead of the synthetic warmup)
- `GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_FUSION=0` (does not suppress the `resolve_fused_ops` messages below — that env var appears to gate a different, lower-level set of SYCL kernel fusions, not this graph-level pass)
- Reducing `-c` from 65536 down to 2048
- Confirmed with `dmesg`/`journalctl`, not just the process exit code:
  ```
  llama-server[86943]: segfault at 0 ip 0000000000000000 sp 00007ffd6a4b11b8 error 14 likely on CPU 3 (core 12, socket 0)
  ```
  `ip 0000000000000000` — a jump through a null function pointer — on every occurrence, across both builds and all three models above.

Only `-ngl 0` avoids it.

**`5511965b197c131b38d8b5a0beb3ea7606d80b10`** — "sycl: route small f32 matmuls to oneMKL, bypass oneDNN" (#22150), merged 2026-05-18. First bad tag: **b9208**. items.body:
## Disclosure

I used AI assistance (Claude) for the investigation, benchmarking and drafting of this PR, including this description and the commit messages. I have reviewed and validated everything myself; all measurements below were run on my own hardware and are reproducible. Flagging this explicitly per CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Summary

`ggml_vk_should_use_mmvq()` returns early with *"MMVQ is generally good for batches"* for any `n > 1`. A speculative-decode step evaluates `n = 1 + n_draft` tokens, so it takes that path and enables MMVQ — bypassing the per-vendor small-`k` heuristics below it.

Those heuristics predate speculative decoding and were only ever reachable at `n == 1`. This PR raises the cutoff so decode-like `n` reaches them too. **No vendor threshold is changed** — they simply now apply at the small `n` a speculative step actually uses.

Enabling MMVQ there costs twice:

1. The Q8_1 quantization of the activations does not amortize at such small `n`.
2. It **perturbs the logits**, so the draft and the target disagree on tokens they should agree on — lowering **draft acceptance**.

The second effect is the less obvious one: MMVQ was not merely slower in the speculative path, it was degrading speculation quality.

## Commits

- `vulkan: don't use MMVQ for k-quants at small k on AMD` — AMD-specific tuning: for k-quants the Q8_1 quantization does not pay for itself at small `k`; DMMV is faster.
- `vulkan: treat a speculative-decode step as decode, not as a batch` — vendor-agnostic; raises the `n > 1` cutoff to `MMVQ_MAX_DECODE_LIKE_N`.

## Testing

AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 "Strix Halo" (gfx1151, 40 CU, RADV/Mesa), 128 GB unified memory.
Model: 35B-A3B MoE, Q6_K attention + Q4_K FFN. MTP self-speculation (`--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2`), ~33k context, 2 runs each, against master `7f575c39d`.

| | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TG, speculative | 75.2 t/s | **84.9 t/s** (+12.9%) |
| draft acceptance | 72–75% | **83–85%** |
| TG, non-speculative | 72.9 t/s | 73.9 t/s |
| PP (prefill), pp4096 | 679.4 t/s | 677.5 t/s (unchanged) |

Prefill is unaffected because `n` there is far larger — with a 2048 ubatch the per-expert token counts are ~64+, well above the cutoff, so batched MMVQ is retained.

An op-level trace of the MMVQ decisions during a speculative step on master shows the mechanism directly:

```
984x  n=3 k=2048 m=512  q4_K -> MMVQ     (expert up/gate)
492x  n=3 k=512  m=2048 q4_K -> MMVQ     (expert down)
220x  n=1 ...          q4_K -> dmmv      (plain decode, correctly bypassed)
```

## Caveats

- **I could only test gfx1151.** The second commit now applies to all vendors per review feedback, but I have no NVIDIA or Intel hardware to validate against. Numbers from someone with a dGPU would be very welcome — particularly whether MMVQ at `n = 2..8` is a win on those backends, since if so the cutoff may need to stay vendor-conditional.
- The first commit changes AMD behaviour at `n == 1` and therefore also affects **discrete** RDNA cards, which I likewise could not test. It is kept as a separate commit so it can be dropped independently.
- `MMVQ_MAX_DECODE_LIKE_N = 8` is a bound chosen to cover common draft widths. Happy to derive it from the actual draft width instead if you'd prefer something less arbitrary.

items.body:
Verified on current master (tip ece963f) serving Qwen3.8-27B, and reproduced identically on a fork build; posting per the contribution guidelines as an issue with a reproducible red test.

**What happens:** the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` endpoint accepts `echo: true` + `logprobs: N` but returns logprobs **only for generated tokens** — the `logprobs.content` array contains exactly `completion_tokens` entries, never the prompt tokens. No error, no warning.

**Why it matters (measured):** every loglikelihood-based evaluation slices prompt-position logprobs out of the echoed array (lm-eval's `parse_logprobs` does `token_logprobs[ctxlen:-1]`). With generation-only content that slice is empty → every choice scores an identical 0.0 → **exact random-chance scores, silently**. We measured this end-to-end: arc_challenge 0.2433 (chance 0.25), winogrande 0.500, piqa 0.4933 — identical to four decimals across spec-decode on/off, because the scores never read real values. The same model through the chat lane answers the same questions at 0.96/0.835 (arc/wino) — the model is fine; the endpoint contract is the problem.

**Red test (single curl):**
```bash
curl -s http://localhost:PORT/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":1,"echo":true,"logprobs":3}' | jq '{prompt_tokens: .usage.prompt_tokens, logprob_entries: (.choices[0].logprobs.content | length)}'
# EXPECTED for echo semantics: logprob_entries == prompt_tokens + 1
# ACTUAL: logprob_entries == 1 (the generated token only)
```

**Ask:** either implement prompt-token logprobs when `echo: true` (the OpenAI contract), or reject `echo: true` explicitly instead of silently accepting it. The first option makes every loglikelihood eval framework work correctly against llama-server — a meaningful win for the local-eval ecosystem.

Evidence trail: our stack audit is public at https://github.com/KyaniteLabs/qwen38-27b-strix-halo (WAVE4 + VALIDITY-MAP ledgers) and the related tool-salience finding at https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/27165.

items.body:
### Name and Version

Bisected on a ROCm/HIP build for gfx1151 (Strix Halo APU), but the mechanism is backend-agnostic, it's in generic jinja capability-probing code.

### Problem

A long, single-conversation tool-calling session (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, custom jinja template with `enable_thinking`/`preserve_thinking` support) reliably breaks after ~38-41 turns of accumulated context: the model enters a circular reasoning loop second-guessing the tool-call output format, consumes its entire token budget inside `reasoning_content`, and returns `finish_reason: "stop"` with empty `content` and no `tool_calls`, a silent dead end for any agent consuming the API. Independent (non-accumulating) tool-calling requests do not show this; it requires a long-lived, growing conversation to surface.

### Bisect

Range: a known-good production commit through current `origin/master` at time of testing. Test methodology: single growing `messages` array (never reset), `get_weather`-style tool, one new city per turn, generous `max_tokens` to rule out budget-truncation confounds, stop-on-first-failure.

- Confirmed good through the immediate parent of the culprit.
- **First bad commit: `0ef6e55edb306fcbcf73e6f1f41923cccb9cf7f8`** (#26398, "chat: add new template for DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731").

### Update

The root-cause theory below (the `enable_thinking` capability probe) has been refuted by @aldehir, `ctx` in that snippet is ephemeral and isn't the context used to build the final prompt, and `preserve_reasoning` isn't gated by `enable_thinking`, so there's no functional path from that code to the symptom. Reopening with the theory struck, since the actual symptom (long-conversation tool-calling breakdown, described above) is still unexplained and still real, leaving the original write-up below for context on what's already been ruled out.

### Original root-cause theory (ruled out, see Update above)

That PR is scoped to DeepSeek V4 (`common/chat.cpp` changes are all inside `common_chat_params_init_deepseek_v3_2`), but it also touches `common/jinja/caps.cpp`, which is generic template-capability-probing code that runs for every model, not just DeepSeek:

```cpp
ctx.set_val("enable_thinking", mk_val<value_bool>(true));
```

This forces `enable_thinking=true` during the "preserve reasoning" capability probe universally, which changes what `supports_preserve_reasoning` resolves to for unrelated templates (in our case, a Qwen3.5/3.6-family template), which in turn changes how reasoning content is retained/stripped from chat history as a conversation grows. That's consistent with a failure that only appears once context accumulates rather than on the first turn.

**(Ruled out per @aldehir below, the actual mechanism behind the symptom is still open.)**

### Question for maintainers

Was forcing `enable_thinking=true` during capability probing meant to apply globally, or should it be scoped to the DeepSeek-specific code path it was added for? Happy to provide the full bisect log / reproduction script if useful.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 "Strix Halo", integrated Radeon 8060S Graphics (gfx1151), 128GB unified memory, ROCm/HIP backend.

### Models

Qwen 35B-A3B (qwen-35b-a3b), full 99-layer GPU offload.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` started with `--parallel 2`. A request was admitted onto slot 0 but never dispatched into a prefill batch, no log output at all for the entire stall, while slot 1 was concurrently busy and processing normally the whole time. This rules out GPU/VRAM contention; the box had headroom.

Timeline (2026-08-16, ET):

- 10:06:30, request sent, claims slot 0 in `GET /slots`: `id_task=39457`, `n_prompt_tokens=48296`, `is_processing: false`, `n_prompt_tokens_processed: 0`.
- 10:06:30 through 10:16:30 (multiple checks over the full 10 minutes), slot 0 stayed at exactly `n_prompt_tokens_processed: 0`, `is_processing: false`, no change.
- Over the same window, slot 1 was `is_processing: true` on a different task (`id_task=39583`), logging `print_timing` lines every few seconds, decoding steadily at ~33 t/s throughout, the server was actively serving work concurrently.
- `journalctl -u llama-server --since '2026-08-16 10:00:00' --until '2026-08-16 10:20:00'` returned **zero log lines** referencing task 39457, no `launch_slot_`, no batch entry, nothing at all for the entire 10-minute window.
- At 10:16:30 the client (a downstream orchestrator with its own ceiling) gave up waiting and moved on.
- A second, unrelated request on the same session ~1 minute later completed normally in 35.6s, so the server was not globally wedged; this looks like a one-off stuck-task condition rather than a hard deadlock.

### Notes

This may be related to #20906 and #20950 (both report a "slot 0 stuck while slot 1 processes normally" pattern on the same gfx1151/Strix Halo hardware), but the symptom differs: in those reports the stuck slot does reach `prompt processing done` / `init sampler` before stalling before generation, and something is logged. Here, the task appears to never enter a prefill batch at all, there is no log line of any kind for the task during the stall, and `/slots` shows `n_prompt_tokens_processed` pinned at 0 the entire time. Reporting the symptom as observed; not asserting a root cause.

### Relevant log output

```
$ curl -s http://192.168.0.102:8080/slots | jq
# slot 0 (stuck):
{
  "id": 0,
  "id_task": 39457,
  "n_prompt_tokens": 48296,
  "n_prompt_tokens_processed": 0,
  "is_processing": false
}
# slot 1 (working, concurrently):
{
  "id": 1,
  "id_task": 39583,
  "is_processing": true
}

$ journalctl -u llama-server --since '2026-08-16 10:00:00' --until '2026-08-16 10:20:00' | grep 39457
# (no output, zero matching lines for the entire window)
```

items.body:
## Bug Description

GLM-5.2 crashes deterministically when attempting distributed inference across multiple DGX Spark nodes via ggml-rpc. The crash occurs during graph computation with `invalid data ptr` on the worker side and `ggml_backend_rpc_buffer_get_tensor` abort on the orchestrator side. This appears analogous to #26424 (DeepSeek V4, Metal) but affects CUDA (sm_121).

## Environment

- **Hardware:** 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, Grace Blackwell, 128GB unified memory each)
- **OS:** DGX OS (Ubuntu-based, aarch64)
- **CUDA:** sm_121 native build
- **llama.cpp:** master `5788b510a` (ggml 0.18.1), built with `-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON`
- **Network:** 1Gbit Ethernet between nodes
- **Model:** GLM-5.2 UD-IQ4_NL (also reproduced with UD-Q4_K_M), unsloth GGUF split files

## Setup

**Workers (3 nodes):**

```
./build/bin/ggml-rpc-server -c --host 192.168.1.XXX --port 50052
```

**Orchestrator (1 node):**

```
./build/bin/llama-server \
  -m ~/models/gguf/glm-5.2/UD-IQ4_NL/GLM-5.2-UD-IQ4_NL-00001-of-00009.gguf \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \
  -ngl 999 -c 4096 \
  --tensor-split 1,1,1,1 \
  --rpc 192.168.1.121:50052,192.168.1.111:50052,192.168.1.128:50052
```

## Expected Behavior

Model loads across 4 nodes and serves inference (works with Gemma-4-26B, Qwen3.6-35B, Mistral-Small-3.2 on identical setup).

## Actual Behavior

Weights distribute successfully (~113GB cache per worker), but crashes during graph_compute:

**Worker output:**

[create_node] invalid data ptr[graph_compute] failed to create graph node 30 (id=197768091778640)
Client connection closed

**Orchestrator output:**

ggml-rpc.cpp:519: Remote RPC server crashed or returned malformed response
recv failed (bytes_recv=0, size_to_recv=8)

Stack trace: `ggml_backend_rpc_buffer_get_tensor` → `ggml_backend_tensor_copy` → `ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async` → `llama_context::graph_compute` → `llama_context::decode` (during `common_init_from_params`).

## Reproducibility

- 100% deterministic — same worker, same graph node (30)
- Reproduced with UD-IQ4_NL (~348GB) and UD-Q4_K_M (~434GB)
- Reproduced with `-c 4096` and `-c 131072`
- Reproduced with and without `--no-warmup`
- All 4 nodes on identical commit (`5788b510a`, fresh pull)

## What Works

- Single-node llama.cpp on same hardware (Gemma, Qwen, Mistral)
- 2-node llama.cpp RPC with smaller models (Gemma-4-26B, ~51.8 tok/s)
- GLM-5.2 on single-node (4×RTX 6000, Ollama, Note: Different machine! But same model GLM 5.2 UD-IQ4_NL)

## Related

- #26424 — DeepSeek V4 Flash RPC crash (Metal, similar MoE/MLA architecture)
- GLM-5.2 uses IndexShare and MTP/NextN layers — likely unsupported ops in RPC graph distribution

## Logs

Full orchestrator and worker terminal output, dmesg are attached.

[glm-rpc-orch.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708516/glm-rpc-orch.log)

[glm-rpc-worker3.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708521/glm-rpc-worker3.log)

[glm-rpc-dmesg-g3.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708525/glm-rpc-dmesg-g3.log)

### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

Port the CUDA GDN -> recurrent-cache fusion to Vulkan: write GDN state snapshots directly into the hybrid recurrent cache and skip the following `CPY` of the snapshot tail.

CUDA already does this (`ggml_cuda_try_gdn_cache_fusion` in `ggml-cuda.cu`). Vulkan still materializes the snapshot in the GDN dst tail and copies it into cache on every decode step for hybrid models (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 / Qwen3-Next style).

### Motivation

On hybrid GDN models (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B), there are many linear layers. Each GDN step produces a state snapshot that is immediately copied into the recurrent cache via `CPY`. That is extra bandwidth and an extra dispatch for traffic that the GDN kernel already has in registers/LDS when it finishes the recurrence.

Measured on AMD Strix Halo (Vulkan), Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M, before fusion:

- ~96 `CPY` nodes/token related to this path (half are GDN state copies that fusion removes)

After fusion (with companion unary+mul fuse):

- Perf label `GATED_DELTA_NET_CACHE` appears **48**/token (one per linear layer)
- Remaining `CPY` related to GDN state cache path is removed; leftover CPYs are other paths (e.g. conv state)
- Win is small but mechanism is solid and matches CUDA.


### Possible Implementation


## Related prior art

- CUDA: `ggml_cuda_try_gdn_cache_fusion` in `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu` (match GDN + strided CPY of snapshot tail into cache; kernel writes cache; skip CPY)
- Vulkan GDN base: #20334 and follow-ups (chunked PP kernels are separate; this is decode/autoregressive state write)

## Proposed design (Vulkan)

1. **Detect** at graph encode time: `GATED_DELTA_NET` whose snapshot tail is consumed by a later `CPY` into the recurrent cache view.
   - Snapshot tail offset: after attn scores, `tail_off = row_size(F32, S_v * H * n_tokens * n_seqs)`.
   - CPY src is a VIEW of the GDN tensor at that offset (contiguous).
   - CPY dst shape `[D, n_seqs, n_written, 1]` with `D = S_v * S_v * H`, `n_written = min(n_tokens, K)`.

2. **Important Vulkan difference vs CUDA adjacent-only match:** Vulkan `graph_optimize` often inserts nodes (e.g. `MUL_MAT`) between GDN and the cache CPY. Adjacent-only fuse fails. Use a **deferred** scan: from GDN, walk forward skipping views/no-ops and unrelated ops until the matching CPY (or next GDN / fail).

3. **Shader change** (`gated_delta_net.comp`):
   - Add binding 7 `StateOutBuf` for the cache destination.
   - Push constants: `state_out_off`, `state_slot_stride` (floats between snapshot slots; fused cache stride may differ from packed dst tail).
   - Write final/K-slot state to `StateOutBuf` instead of the dst tail when fused.

4. **Host** (`ggml-vulkan.cpp`):
   - Context fields: `fused_gdn_cache_dst`, `fused_gdn_cache_slot_stride`, `fused_gdn_pending_skip_cpy`.
   - On GDN dispatch, bind cache subbuffer; clear fuse state after use.
   - Skip encoding the pending CPY node; clear pending on graph reset / failure paths.
   - Perf fusion string: `GATED_DELTA_NET_CACHE`.

5. Do **not** fuse if GDN is a graph output (snapshot tail must remain visible).

items.body:
## Overview

I was investigating why setting KV cache to BF16 on my Strix Halo seemed to result in slower performance with no  PPL gains.  I discovered that the source of the slowness was BF16 KV cache was silently mapping to F16 behind the scenes, despite the achitecture natively supporting BF16 operations.  Since AMD's RDNA 3/3.5/4 supports native BF16 vector operations,  I thought to try to fix the performance issues I was seeing.

Disclosure:  The follow discussion is a mix of my own words and AI assisted content.

## Key Takeways

- Gated on specifying BF16 for both K/V cache types and native GPU support
- +5-15% prefill speeds over baseline F16 K/V cache prefill performance even at long context
- Generation performance parity vs F16 baseline (was ~20% lower before these changes)
- Near equivalent to baseline F32 PPL parity (PPL was ~5% higher with F16 only at depth)

## Design

A precision pipeline for BF16 K/V (all supported head sizes):

```
KV cache (BF16, 2 bytes/element)
    -> BF16 tile in SRAM (pure memcpy, no BF16->F16 conversion)
    -> Q converted to BF16 once at fill
    -> QK^T via v_dot2_f32_bf16 on RDNA3+ architectures (exact BF16 products, FP32 accumulation)
    -> P computed in FP32, KQ buffer stored as BF16
    -> VKQ via packed BF16 PV: P rounded to BF16, V rows paired across
       consecutive KV rows with v_perm_b32, one v_dot2_f32_bf16 per head
       pair with FP32 accumulation
```

Key decisions:

- **Both-K/V-BF16 gate**: the native-BF16 path is selected only when
  `K->type == GGML_TYPE_BF16 && V->type == GGML_TYPE_BF16` on hardware with
  native BF16 support. No BF16 conversion plumbing in the launcher;
  `fattn-common.cuh` is byte-identical to upstream.
- **v_dot2_f32_bf16**: RDNA3+ has a hardware packed-BF16 dot instruction
  (2 BF16 products + 1 FP32 add per instruction). It gives the KQ phase
  the same 2x FP32 rate as the F16 kernel's v_dot2_f32_f16, so the
  native-BF16 path does not pay an ALU penalty. Guarded by the
  `V_DOT2_F32_BF16_AVAILABLE` macro (gfx110x/gfx115x/gfx120x).
- **BF16 Q_tmp**: Q is converted to BF16 once at fill. This halves the Q
  SRAM footprint vs an FP32 Q tile, so the standard 32-column launch and
  the standard config tables apply unchanged. 
- **Packed BF16 PV (the only VKQ variant)**: the VKQ phase rounds P to
  BF16, pairs V rows across consecutive KV rows with v_perm_b32, and runs
  v_dot2_f32_bf16 with FP32 accumulation. 
- Measured PPL impact vs FP32 VKQ: none. Applies to every head size.  The
  packed design was verified at DV = 512 (no register spills, test-backend-ops clean).
- **BF16 KQ buffer**: the softmax output is stored in SRAM as BF16. P is
  rounded to BF16 exactly once (at the store), which is what the packed PV
  does anyway, so numerics are identical to a float KQ buffer while the
  SRAM footprint and the KQ read/write traffic halve. Measured prefill
  gain vs the float KQ buffer: about +13% at 9k KV rows.
- **Automatic per-arch selection, no user-facing split**: every native-BF16
  code path is gated on `V_DOT2_F32_BF16_AVAILABLE`, defined only for AMD
  RDNA3/RDNA3.5/RDNA4 targets. `bf16/bf16` KV on a supported card
  automatically gets the native kernel; on any other target the same
  instantiation compiles to the original F16 tile path with BF16->F16 conversion at
  tile load. 
- **Config tables**: standard upstream tables for all paths
- **F16 kernel untouched**: the existing F16 path (half2 math, 0.25
  Q-scaling when v_dot2_f32_f16 is unavailable) is unchanged.


## nVidia GPU impllcations (for now)

This PR will need followup work to support nVidia GPUs.  Unfortunately I don't have any to test/develop with.

`v_dot2_f32_bf16` and `v_perm_b32` are AMD RDNA3+ instructions. NVIDIA has
no packed-BF16 dot in its CUDA cores. These are the anticipated consequences
for NVIDIA GPUs:

- The BF16 tile instantiation compiles with `V_DOT2_F32_BF16_AVAILABLE` undefined,
  so it runs the F16 tile path with  in-tile BF16->F16 conversion - the pre-existing F16-speed kernel
- **No native-BF16 precision benefit either**: on NVIDIA the tile kernel
  still converts to F16, so the deep-context half2 accumulation behavior
  is unchanged there. This matches upstream's existing numerics for BF16
  KV; it is not a regression.
- NVIDIA's main BF16 path for head sizes <= 128 is the MMA_F16 tensor-core
  kernel, which is untouched by this change.
- A native-BF16 path for NVIDIA would require a bf16-MMA tile kernel
  (following the existing `mma-f16.cuh` structure); it is separate
  follow-up work, not part of this change.


## Prefill Performance results

Using llama-bench with Qwen3.5-4B and pp1024 on Strix Halo

| Depth | F16 (t/s) | BF16 (t/s) | speed gain |
| ------- | --------: | ---------: | --: |
|  8192  | 1391.3    | 1579.2     | +13.5% |
| 16384  | 1228.5    | 1368.2     | +11.4% |


## Perplexity tests (RDNA3+ only)

Same measurements on a Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, RDNA4, 3x GPU,
ROCm 7.1), Qwen3.5-4B-Q8_0, wiki.test.raw full, c=32768, mlock:

| KV cache / FA | PPL @ 32k |
| ------------- | --------: |
| F32 baseline (FA off) | 8.6368 |
| BF16 (this change) | 8.6403 (+0.04%) |
| F16 | 9.1400 (+5.8%) |


## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure:  YES - Deepseek V4 Flash 0731 was used to create the changes from an implementation plan I had written, under strong supervision.  I've personally review the code, and tested correctness on RDNA3, 3.5, and 4 architectures (7900XTX, Strix Halo, R9700)

## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.

### Name and Version

./bin/llama-cli --version
version: 9586 (76da2450a)
built with GNU 15.2.0 for Linux x86_64

Hardware / software
GPU: AMD Radeon Graphics, gfx1151 (Strix Halo), 111616 MiB VRAM allocation
Memory: LPDDR5X-8000, 256-bit → ~256 GB/s theoretical peak
ROCm: 7.2.1, HSA 8.20.1
Build: llama.cpp 76da2450a (9586)

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-bench

### Command line

```shell
# rocWMMA ON
GGML_HIPBLAS=1 LLAMA_HIP_UMA=1 HIPCXX="$(hipconfig -l)/clang" HIP_PATH="$(hipconfig -R)" \
cmake -S . -B build -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DGGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN=ON \
cd build && make -j
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./bin ./bin/llama-bench -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q8_0 \
  -p 512,2048,8192 -n 128 -fa 0,1 -r 5

# rocWMMA OFF
GGML_HIPBLAS=1 LLAMA_HIP_UMA=1 HIPCXX="$(hipconfig -l)/clang" HIP_PATH="$(hipconfig -R)" \
cmake -S . -B build-no-rocwmma -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DGGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN=OFF \
cd build-no-rocwmma && make -j
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./bin ./bin/llama-bench -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q8_0 \
  -p 512,2048,8192 -n 128 -fa 0,1 -r 5
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I iterated with Claud Opus 4.8 to discover the root configuration for this performance bug.  The analysis was confirmed by myself and the text below summarized and beautified by anthropic.

I looked at a similar open issue #21284 and believe this one is distinct.  I'll also be opening a second issue related to Vulkan compiled llama-bench performing significantly better in token generation than this HIP compiled binary regardless of the rocWMMA compiler option and flash attention options.  I'll link that issue to this one because of the experimental overlap but I believe the next issue is a completely different software code path.

Results
HIP, rocWMMA ON:

test | fa | t/s 
-- | -- | --
pp512 | 0 | 870.55 ± 12.79
pp2048 | 0 | 797.61 ± 4.23
pp8192 | 0 | 708.86 ± 7.23
pp512 | 1 | 704.63 ± 6.41
pp2048 | 1 | 625.27 ± 2.97
pp8192 | 1 | **419.31** ± 1.69

HIP, rocWMMA OFF:

test | fa | t/s
-- | -- | --
pp512 | 0 | 918.17 ± 20.24
pp2048 | 0 | 811.14 ± 3.50
pp8192 | 0 | 723.00 ± 5.57
pp512 | 1 | 823.14 ± 4.75
pp2048 | 1 | 807.58 ± 5.41
pp8192 | 1 | 705.49 ± 3.85

Analysis
FA penalty within each build (fa0 → fa1):

test | rocWMMA ON | rocWMMA OFF
-- | -- | --
pp512 | 870.55 → 704.63 (−19%) | 918.17 → 823.14 (−10%)
pp2048 | 797.61 → 625.27 (−22%) | 811.14 → 807.58 (−0.4%)
pp8192 | 708.86 → 419.31 (**−41%**) | 723.00 → 705.49 (−2.4%)

With rocWMMA off, the FA penalty is negligible and the profile is well-behaved (matching Vulkan, which shows ~flat FA at pp8192: 724.28 → 706.24). With rocWMMA on, the penalty grows super-linearly with context — the opposite of expected FA behavior — strongly implicating the rocWMMA WMMA FA kernels on gfx1151 (RDNA3.5).

Suggested fix directions
Default GGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN to OFF for gfx1151/RDNA3.5, or emit a warning when it's enabled on this ISA, or investigate the rocWMMA FA kernel path for gfx1151. Note that current Strix Halo build guidance frequently recommends enabling this flag as a performance optimization, when it is in fact a pessimization for FA on this hardware.
