### Problem description & steps to reproduce

The `llama-server` fails to reuse the KV cache for subsequent requests in the same chat session. On the second request to the same slot, it forces a full prompt re-processing, logging: `forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data (likely due to SWA or hybrid/recurrent memory)`. As a result, the model "forgets" the conversation history.

This occurs on different models (Qwen 3.5 MoE, Gemma 4 MoE), different llama.cpp versions (b8025, b8769), and even with minimal context (e.g., 45 tokens). The issue is reproducible with direct `curl` requests, ruling out client-side problems.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Start `llama-server` with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B or Gemma-4-26B-A4B.
2. Send first request:
   `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"model\": \"qwen3.5-35b-a3b-128k\", \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"My name is Tester. Remember it.\"}], \"temperature\": 0.6, \"max_tokens\": 50}"`

4. Observe server logs and model response.

**Expected behavior:**
Server restores context from KV cache; model answers "Tester".

**Actual behavior:**
Server logs `forcing full prompt re-processing...`; model responds that it does not know the name.

items.body:
## Overview

ggml_vk_get_cpy_pipeline only routed to the tiled shared-memory transpose shader when dim1 was the innermost dimension, i.e. ggml_transpose (a 0<->1 swap). A 0<->2 swap -- ggml_cont(ggml_permute(x, 2, 1, 0, 3)) -- fell back to the generic per-element strided copy, whose source reads stride by ne0*ne1 elements: one cache line per lane.

DeepSeek-V4's lightning indexer performs exactly that permute on a [n_kv, n_tokens, n_head] tensor. On Vulkan/RADV gfx1151 it ran at ~7-20 GB/s of a ~200 GB/s part and accounted for 43% of total prefill time.

Add copy_transpose_02.comp, mirroring copy_transpose.comp but tiling over dst dims (0, 2) with dims 1 and 3 as the batch, so reads walk src dim2 and writes walk dst dim0 -- both contiguous. The selection condition additionally requires a non-contiguous source and a contiguous destination so it cannot take cases the contiguous-copy shader already handles.

test-backend-ops only exercised ggml_transpose for CONT, so the strided path was untested. Add test_cont_permute covering (2,1,0,3), (1,2,0,3) and (0,2,1,3) over f32/f16 at tile-aligned, tile-unaligned and large shapes. The large shapes are in the eval set rather than only in perf because perf mode does not verify results.

Measured on gfx1151, ne=[n_kv,64,64,1], perm=(2,1,0,3), f32:

| n_kv | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 9.08 GB/s | 579.85 GB/s |
| 1280 | 20.03 GB/s | 153.71 GB/s |
| 2048 | 7.11 GB/s | 91.68 GB/s |
| 2304 | 16.24 GB/s | 86.49 GB/s |

The ~2.2x penalty previously seen at power-of-two n_kv (destination-stride aliasing) is gone. End to end, DeepSeek-V4-Flash IQ3_XXS prefill on a 9k-token prompt goes from 56.33 t/s to 103.74 t/s (+84%).

Note: at n_tokens=512 a single slow-path dispatch takes ~273 ms and looping it in perf mode can trip the GPU watchdog, so the perf cases use n_tokens=64.

## Requirements

### Name and Version

llama-cli --version
version: 10326 (3653e6d6d)
built with GNU 15.2.0 for Linux x86_64

ROCm / TheRock: 7.14.0
GPU architecture: gfx1151

Ubuntu 26.04 Kernel 7.0.0-29

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

RPC, HIP

### Hardware

2x Bosgame M5 Ryzen AI Max+ 395
Radeon 8060S Graphics
architecture: gfx1151
VRAM / unified GPU memory: 120000 MiB
VMM: no

Available devices:
  ROCm0: Radeon 8060S Graphics (120000 MiB, ...)
  RPC0: 10.44.0.2:50053 (120000 MiB, ...)

### Models

https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
GGUF quantization: UD-IQ3_XXS
4 shards
DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00004.gguf

speculative draft model used: dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf

any quantization. Just depends, whether rpc is used

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

### Summary

A ROCm RPC worker on AMD gfx1151 aborts in `GGML_OP_TOP_K` while processing a sufficiently long DeepSeek V4 Flash prompt.

Short requests work correctly.

A long request consistently reaches exactly 4096 processed prompt tokens and then causes the remote ROCm RPC worker to abort with:

```text
ggml_cuda_compute_forward: TOP_K failed
ROCm error: invalid configuration argument
```

The client then reports:

```text
Remote RPC server crashed or returned malformed response
recv failed (bytes_recv=0, size_to_recv=8)
```

This is reproducible on both:

```text
TheRock / ROCm 7.13.0
TheRock / ROCm 7.14.0
```

using the same llama.cpp commit:

```text
3653e6d6d
```

Replacing only the remote ROCm RPC worker with a Vulkan/RADV RPC worker on the exact same Radeon 8060S / gfx1151 hardware makes the same setup stable.

Vulkan is significantly slower, but it does not crash.

### Difference from #24177

This appears related to #24177 because both failures involve the AMD `TOP_K` path and an RPC worker abort.

However, this case is different:

- `--no-spec-draft-backend-sampling` is already enabled.
- The failure occurs during prompt prefill, not draft-token backend sampling.
- Short prompts work.
- Long prompts reproducibly fail after 4096 processed prompt tokens.
- Reducing `--ubatch-size` from 256 to 128 does not change the failure point.
- Switching only the RPC worker backend from ROCm to Vulkan avoids the crash.

Therefore, the `--no-spec-draft-backend-sampling` workaround from #24177 does not avoid this failure.

### Server command

```bash
/usr/local/bin/llama-server \
  --model /opt/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/UD-IQ3_XXS/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00004.gguf \
  --alias deepseek-v4-flash-q3-xxs \
  --gpu-layers all \
  --fit off \
  --load-mode none \
  --ctx-size 1048576 \
  --parallel 4 \
  --jinja \
  --rpc 10.44.0.2:50053 \
  --split-mode layer \
  --tensor-split 1,1 \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 \
  --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --no-spec-draft-backend-sampling \
  --spec-draft-type-v q8_0 \
  --temp 1.0 \
  --top-p 0.95 \
  --min-p 0.0 \
  --top-k 0 \
  --spec-type draft-dspark \
  --model-draft /opt/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/UD-IQ3_XXS/dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf \
  --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
  --batch-size 1024 \
  --ubatch-size 128 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --flash-attn on \
  --port 5800
```

Remote worker:

```bash
ggml-rpc-server \
  --host 10.44.0.2 \
  --port 50053 \
  --device ROCm0
```

### Reproduction

1. Start a ROCm `ggml-rpc-server` on the gfx1151 remote system.
2. Start `llama-server` with the command above.
3. Send a short chat request.
4. The short request completes normally.
5. Send a long chat request containing approximately 18k prompt tokens.
6. Prompt processing proceeds normally:

```text
prompt processing, n_tokens = 1024, progress = 0.06
prompt processing, n_tokens = 2048, progress = 0.11
prompt processing, n_tokens = 3072, progress = 0.17
prompt processing, n_tokens = 4096, progress = 0.22
```

7. Immediately after the 4096-token point, the remote ROCm RPC worker aborts.

Changing:

```text
--ubatch-size 256
```

to:

```text
--ubatch-size 128
```

does not change the behavior.

Both fail after 4096 processed prompt tokens.

## Control tests

### Short prompt, ROCm RPC

Works correctly.

Example successful request:

```text
prompt eval time = 1086.65 ms / 33 tokens
eval time = 23099.77 ms / 388 tokens
total time = 24186.42 ms / 421 tokens
draft acceptance = 0.64118
```

### Long prompt, ROCm RPC

Crashes consistently after:

```text
n_tokens = 4096
```

### Long prompt, Vulkan RPC on the same remote gfx1151 GPU

Does not crash.

Only the remote worker backend was changed:

```text
ROCm/HIP -> crash
Vulkan/RADV -> stable
```

This suggests the problem is specific to the ROCm implementation or dispatch of `GGML_OP_TOP_K` on gfx1151 rather than RPC itself.

## First Bad Commit

Unknown.

Reproduced with:

```text
llama.cpp 10311
commit 217df17ac
```

on both ROCm/TheRock 7.13.0 and 7.14.0.

I have not bisected older llama.cpp revisions.

### First Bad Commit

Reproduced with:

```text
llama.cpp 10311
commit 217df17ac
```

on both ROCm/TheRock 7.13.0 and 7.14.0.

I have not bisected older llama.cpp revisions.


### Relevant log output

### Client

```text

items.body:
### Name and Version

### Description

I'm observing a reproducible VRAM memory leak when running DeepSeek V4 Flash GGUF with DSpark speculative decoding enabled. After each PP+TG (prefill + generate) cycle, VRAM usage increases by approximately **10 MB**, and this accumulation continues until the process eventually runs out of memory (OOM).

This issue does **not** occur with:
- Step 3.7 + DSpark
- Qwen3.8-27B + DSpark

Both of the above maintain stable VRAM usage across multiple cycles.

### Environment
- Model: DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731 version) GGUF + DSpark
- Framework: llama.cpp
- Issue: VRAM leak, ~10 MB per PP+TG cycle

### Suspected Root Cause

I suspect this is a **Draft KV Cache leak** specific to the DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 model when used with DSpark. Specifically:

1. **KV cache positions** are written during every draft step but are **never compacted or properly reclaimed**, leading to continuous VRAM growth[reference:0]. A similar issue has been reported in related forks where "positions are written every tree step but never compacted," causing OOM under sustained traffic[reference:1].

2. **DSpark draft KV-cache group poisoning**: The DSpark draft model's KV cache is flagged as an "eagle group" (same as EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP/DFlash)[reference:2]. The multi-group cache-hit lookup requires **every** KV-cache group to report a nonzero hit for cache reuse to succeed — any single group reporting zero short-circuits the entire request's lookup[reference:3].

3. **Sparse and discontinuous draft KV**: DSpark's draft-layer KV is recomputed from the target model's real hidden state every decode step, meaning it has **no cross-request reuse value**[reference:4]. Its stored blocks are sparse and discontinuous (e.g., `[MISS, MISS, HIT, MISS, MISS]`)[reference:5], never satisfying the consecutive-hit window required for cache lookup[reference:6].

4. **"One-vote veto" effect**: This permanently poisons the AND-combination lookup for the entire request[reference:7], even though the model's real KV-cache groups (SWA, compressed C4A/C128A, indexer) independently have a working hit rate around 89%[reference:8]. As a result, the prefix caching mechanism is effectively disabled — every new request cannot reuse historical caches and must recompute and write new KV cache entries, causing VRAM to grow until exhaustion.

A similar fix has been proposed in vLLM where DSpark draft KV-cache groups are excluded from the cache-hit lookup poisoning mechanism[reference:9]. The same root cause likely applies to llama.cpp.

### Why Step 3.7 and Qwen3.8-27B Are Not Affected

These models likely have different DSpark implementations or KV cache structures that do **not** trigger this cache lookup conflict, allowing normal cache reuse and stable VRAM usage.

### Suggested Fix Direction

- Exclude DSpark draft KV-cache groups from the prefix caching lookup's "all-groups-must-hit" requirement, similar to the approach taken in vLLM PR #47891[reference:10].
- Alternatively, ensure DSpark draft KV cache positions are properly compacted or reclaimed after each generation cycle, as addressed in PR #23461 for draft/MTP resources.

### Additional Context

There have been related reports of DeepSeek V4 KV cache not being reclaimed on slot release, and DSpark-specific KV cache issues with offloading connectors[reference:13]. This may share a root cause with the hybrid-attention KV handling.

Please let me know if additional logs or reproduction steps would be helpful.

Thanks!

### Name and Version

```
$ ./llama-cli --version
version: 0.1.0-dev (build 599, commit ad1de39)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Also observed on `4f31eed` and `6b4344e` (llama-server and llama-cli).

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

AMD Radeon 890M iGPU (gfx1150, RADV 26.1.2, Mesa), Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, 32 GB LPDDR5 unified with 16 GiB firmware VRAM carve-out + 32 GiB GTT aperture. Debian 13, kernel 7.1.3. Kernel params include `ttm.pages_limit=8388608`.

### Models

`Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf` + `mmproj-Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-F16.gguf` (also crashed with GLM-OCR Q8 + mmproj; the specific model does not appear to matter - the crash happens at projector load).

### Command line

```bash
./llama-cli -m Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --mmproj mmproj-Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-F16.gguf \
  --image ui.png -p "What is the dialog title?" \
  -ngl 999 -fa on --temp 0.1 -no-cnv -n 30
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

On this iGPU class, loading ANY mmproj-bearing model balloons GPU-side (GTT/TTM) allocations until the kernel's global OOM killer fires - **at projector load time, before any image is processed**. The process is killed within seconds; with other services resident, the OOM kill cascades (we observed two full-host watchdog resets before isolating it).

Clean single-process repro (no other GPU consumers; process wrapped with `choom -n 1000` so the OOM killer prefers it):

VmSize timeline from `/proc/<pid>/status` sampling:

```
0s VmSize=18184kB    VmRSS=7420kB
2s VmSize=4119524kB  VmRSS=150708kB
4s VmSize=32033928kB VmRSS=28652kB
```

Kernel (verbatim):

```
oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE,nodemask=(null),cpuset=...,global_oom,task_memcg=/system.slice/uit2-repro.scope,task=llama-cli,pid=77433,uid=0
Out of memory: Killed process 77433 (llama-cli) total-vm:33279112kB, anon-rss:4kB, file-rss:52kB, shmem-rss:0kB, UID:0 pgtables:1436kB oom_score_adj:1000
```

Note `total-vm: 33.2 GB` vs `anon-rss: 4 kB` - the memory is almost entirely driver-side, invisible to memory cgroups. We confirmed a `systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=6G` wrapper does **not** contain it (the OOM still fires as `CONSTRAINT_NONE` global; TTM/GTT kernel pages bypass the cgroup). With slower leak progression (CPU projector via `--no-mmproj-offload`) the driver log fills with repeated:

```
radv/amdgpu: Failed to allocate a buffer:
    size      : 1073741824 bytes
    alignment : 262144 bytes
    domains   : 4
```

(1 GiB GTT allocation attempts, `domains: 4`.)

For contrast: the identical artifacts + fixtures run cleanly on a discrete RTX 3090 (Vulkan not involved; CUDA) - this appears iGPU/GTT-specific.

Related prior art: #24626 (absolute per-device memory budget for `--fit` on UMA), #26447 (iGPU Vulkan device-lost at large contexts).

### Suggested fix / ask

Bound or chunk vision-context allocations on UMA/iGPU devices (or document a safe configuration for this class). As-is, every mmproj model is a potential host-crasher on Radeon iGPU systems.

---

*Disclosure: this report was assembled with AI assistance from measurements captured directly on the affected host (VmSize sampling script, kernel journal, RADV logs quoted verbatim above). All data points are from real runs, not generated.*

items.body:
## Overview

**cuda: fuse MoE weighted expert reduction**

Fuses the MoE expert-combine tail on the CUDA backend into one reduction kernel, removing the intermediate tensor traffic between its stages.

After `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID`, the combine is a per-expert scale/weight multiply plus an ordered left-to-right `VIEW`+`ADD` chain that sums the `k = n_expert_used` experts. Those are logical nodes: the backend already fuses consecutive MULs/ADDs, so for the common top-k = 8 case it runs as **two physical `k_bin_bcast` kernels** (fused two-MUL + fused seven-ADD) with the full weighted-expert tensor `[n_embd, k, n_tokens]` written out and read back between them. This PR replaces that with **one kernel** that reads each expert row once and writes the `[n_embd, n_tokens]` result once:

```
dst[t,c] = sum_e ((experts[t,e,c] * expert_scale[t,e]) * weight[t,e])
```

The sum keeps the original left-to-right order. **The primary benefit is reduced global-memory traffic** (the eliminated intermediate tensor)

**Matching** is purely structural (op / shape / stride / view offset / add-chain / closure / aliasing) — never the quant or model. Two shapes: short (`experts * router_weight`) and long (`(experts * expert_scale) * router_weight`). The long form appears whenever a per-expert broadcast scale is applied before the router weight (e.g. the NVFP4 `scale_2` output scale, but the same graph slot can carry other scales); the matcher keys only on that second MUL's presence.

**Kernels:** unrolled templates for `k = 2..8`, one runtime-`k` kernel for `k = 9..15`, a `float4` path when `n_embd % 4 == 0` and aligned (scalar fallback), and an optional per-expert scale via a template flag. The `k <= 15` cap is `ggml_can_fuse_subgraph`'s 31-node limit on the long form (`2*k + 1 <= 31`); larger `n_expert_used` falls back.

**Correctness:** full-model WikiText-2 perplexity is unchanged (**5.8857 ± 0.03661**, on vs off) and `test-backend-ops` passes; the reduction keeps the original left-to-right order. Guards: `weights`/`expert_scale` are copied to scratch when they overlap `dst` (read while writing `dst`); fusion is skipped when `experts` overlaps `dst`; view offsets/strides and the add-chain are validated before fusing.

**Fallback / kill switch:** any unsupported top-k or failed structural/layout/closure/alias check leaves the graph unchanged and runs the per-op path. Enabled by default; `GGML_CUDA_MOE_WEIGHTED_REDUCTION=0` forces the reference path.

## Additional information


**Performance** — prefill `t/s`, default-ON vs `=0`, same binary, mean-vs-mean:

| Hardware | Model | Quant | pp2048 | pp8192 |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| RTX 5090 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | NVFP4 | +3.6% | +3.6% |
| RTX 5090 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | Q4_K_M | +4.1% | +3.9% |
| RTX 5090 | Gemma-4-26B-A4B | NVFP4 | +4.3% | +4.3% |
| DGX Spark (GB10) | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | NVFP4 | +5.4% | +5.4% |
| DGX Spark (GB10) | Gemma-4-26B-A4B | Q4_K_M | +7.1% | +6.2% |

**Testing** (both modes, same binary): `test-backend-ops` **13,178/13,178** pass; CTest **42/42** pass; CPU-vs-CUDA compared; WikiText-2 PPL identical **5.8857 ± 0.03661**; `llama-cli` output unchanged. CUDA backend only; no changes to weights or numerics.

items.body:
## Overview

Fixes a regression after #24233, which restored HIP integrated GPU detection. On my AMD APU, this also made the ROCm host-buffer path available for HIP integrated GPUs. With that path enabled, prompt input appears corrupted: chat templates and system prompts can be ignored, and generated output becomes garbage.

This change keeps integrated GPU detection/reporting intact, but disables direct ROCm_Host compute on HIP integrated GPUs. The fix does not disable host-buffer exposure entirely, pinned buffers remain available to preserve functionality, while only the problematic direct compute path is blocked.

## Additional information

Tested locally on gfx1151 / RDNA3.5 APU with ROCm 7.14. The corrupted input/output issue is fixed with this patch.
The issue appeared in external harnesses like Pi and OpenCode. It can also be reproduced in the built-in web UI with a sufficiently large combined first input. For example, gemma-4-26B-A4B with 4676 tokens of context or more outputs `<unused49>` indefinitely. Other models can be way more resilient and their output starts by saying 'Based on the text provided, which appears to be a corrupted or "hallucinated" version of a Wikipedia article'.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - I used AI assistance to review and patch the relevant code. I tested and reviewed the final change myself.

### Name and Version

Environment

GPU: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B70 Graphics (Battlemage), 32GB VRAM
OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-22-generic (xe driver)
oneAPI / Level Zero: Unified Runtime over Level-Zero V2, 20.2.0 [1.15.38308+1]
llama.cpp commit: 7dad2f1a17d65b5e2034c277125bc9f97573a779 (build b9660, 2026-06-15) for the SYCL repro; current master built locally with -DGGML_VULKAN=ON for the Vulkan comparison run
Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE), Q4_K_M, GGUF

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
SYCL launch command

llama-server \
  --model Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --device SYCL0 \
  --ctx-size 32768 \
  --parallel 1 \
  --n-gpu-layers 99 \
  --jinja \
  --no-mmap \
  --reasoning-budget 0 --reasoning off

Env: UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1, GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_FLASH_ATTN=1, ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

**Summary**

When the underlying GPU resets an engine mid-job (kernel-level xe driver "Timedout job" / "Engine reset" — see companion kernel-level report, link TBD), the SYCL backend never detects it. The server hangs forever, busy-waiting in sched_yield() inside the Level-Zero adapter, with /health still responding but /slots and /v1/chat/completions timing out indefinitely. There is no log output at the point of failure and no way to recover short of SIGKILL.

By contrast, on the same hardware, same model, same kind of underlying GPU reset, the Vulkan backend (ggml-vulkan / Mesa ANV) correctly detects device loss and the driver returns VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST to the application. (llama.cpp itself doesn't catch this exception today and the process aborts — see note at the end — but the detection is correct, which is the point of this report: SYCL has no equivalent detection at all.)

We believe the root cause of the GPU reset itself is upstream of llama.cpp (kernel drm/xe driver / GuC firmware level — filing separately here > https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/xe/kernel/-/work_items/8390), but regardless of that root cause, the SYCL backend hanging forever instead of failing visibly is a real gap worth closing on its own.

**What's been ruled out (from earlier isolated testing against the SYCL server)**

A tools array present without being invoked — no hang
A single forced tool call — no hang, sub-1s
Six simultaneous tool definitions with a genuine call — no hang, sub-1s
Context size from 32768 up to 262144 — hangs occur across the whole range, no clear correlation with size
One hang occurred at only ~2,048 prompt tokens, partway through generation (not during prefill)

These rule out grammar-constrained tool-call generation and large-context prefill as the trigger in isolation. Root cause now appears to be a GPU/kernel-level engine timeout under sustained load (separate report filed against drm/xe), reproducible regardless of which backend is driving the GPU — this report is scoped specifically to SYCL's lack of any detection/recovery path for that event.

Ask

Does the SYCL backend have (or could it have) any equivalent to Vulkan's device-loss detection — checking Level-Zero/SYCL exception state or a result code after a submission/wait, rather than spinning indefinitely?
At minimum, a bounded wait with a clear error/log output on timeout would let an operator's process supervisor recover automatically, instead of requiring an external watchdog to detect a silent hang via a secondary symptom (/slots timing out while /health stays fast).

Happy to test patches — this reproduces reliably under real agentic tool-calling load (multiple times per hour), so turnaround on verification should be fast.

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

SYCL symptom: indefinite hang, no error

GPU power draw stays elevated (~98W) for the duration — confirms the GPU is actively spinning, not idle/crashed/waiting on I/O. gdb backtrace captured live while wedged, all threads idle except one spinning in the Level Zero adapter's USM memcpy path:

Thread 1 (LWP 25923) "llama-server":
#0  __GI_sched_yield ()
#1  ... libze_intel_gpu.so.1
...
#14 ggml_sycl_mul_mat_id(ggml_backend_sycl_context&, ggml_tensor*) () from libggml-sycl.so.0
#15 ggml_backend_sycl_graph_compute_impl(...)
#16 ggml_backend_sycl_graph_compute(...)
#17 ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async()
#18 llama_context::graph_compute(...)
#19 llama_context::process_ubatch(...)
#20 llama_context::decode(...)
#21 llama_decode()
#22 server_context_impl::update_slots()
#23 server_queue::start_loop(...)
#24 llama_server(...)

Notably: at the kernel level (dmesg -T), this exact PID (25923) has a corresponding entry showing the GPU driver itself reset the engine and declared the job timed out, before this backtrace was captured:

xe 0000:03:00.0: [drm] Tile0: GT0: Engine reset: engine_class=ccs, logical_mask: 0x1, guc_id=2, state=0x249
xe 0000:03:00.0: [drm] Tile0: GT0: Timedout job: seqno=4294967200, lrc_seqno=4294967200, guc_id=2, flags=0x20 in llama-server [25923]

i.e., the SYCL/Level-Zero stack is busy-waiting on a GPU job the kernel has already torn down. It never finds out, and never times out on its own.

Vulkan Crash:

items.body: This PR adds a new `--numa mirror` option which mirrors model weights to each Numa node on the system, and uses a thread-local var in the OMP threadpool to select the correct mirror copy local to the thread at runtime, to eliminate cross-socket traffic. Build instructions: ``` apt-get update apt-get install -y libnuma-dev libgomp1 cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-march=native" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-march=native" -DGGML_OPENMP=ON cmake --build build --parallel ``` To test: ```bash # No mirroring: ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ~/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf # Numa mirroring of model weights to every node: ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ~/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --numa mirror ``` Test system is a two-socket Xeon 6238R Cascade Lake, with 768GB of DDR4-2933 (6 channels per socket). Without `--numa mirror`: ``` developer@81ec6c6e6af6:/workspaces/llama-cpp-dbsanfte-dev$ ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ./.devcontainer/Qwen3-32B-Q6_K.gguf | model | size | params | backend | threads | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | ------: | --------------: | -------------------: | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | pp512 | 20.99 ± 0.01 | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | tg128 | 1.91 ± 0.00 | build: c665d3c9 (6468) ``` With `--numa mirror`: ``` developer@81ec6c6e6af6:/workspaces/llama-cpp-dbsanfte-dev$ ./build/bin/llama-bench -m . /.devcontainer/Qwen3-32B-Q6_K.gguf --numa mirror | model | size | params | backend | threads | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | ------: | --------------: | -------------------: | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | pp512 | 21.36 ± 0.11 | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | tg128 | 2.70 ± 0.00 | build: c665d3c9 (6468) ``` Intel PCM tool during mirror inference showing both sockets using local mem: There's still a bit of cross-socket traffic (5%) because only model weights are mirrored, not tensors created at inference time. I'll play with that, maybe mirroring those aggressively will help too, or maybe not. Right now anything created at inference time just gets set to live on Node 0.

items.body:
## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
Adds support for MiniMax-M3, a 60-layer / 128-expert MoE (3 dense + 57 MoE layers) using MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA): a GQA block-sparse attention where a lightweight per-GQA-group indexer scores the visible causal context, max-pools the scores into 128-token key blocks, and selects the top-16 blocks (the query's local block is always force-included). The main attention then runs only over the selected blocks (16*128 = 2048 KV per query), independent of context length, so decode attention cost stops scaling with context.

Implements the architecture from the MSA paper (arXiv:2606.13392v2) and follows the transformers reference (modular_minimax_m3_vl) for the indexer construction, selection semantics, and RoPE. MTP heads are not present in the released weights. Vision support is a separate PR (#25113).

Note that MSA is not an optional speed optimization, as the model is trained with sparse attention, so block selection is part of the model's semantics. Running dense attention is an out-of-distribution approximation that degrades output quality. The dense path exists only as a fallback for configurations that can't run MSA.

## Additional information

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

### Implementation
Batch and decode implement the same block-scoring and selection semantics, block scores bs = maxpool_128(idx_q*idx_k^T + causal mask) plus a host-provided local-force bias (large positive bias on each query's local block), ranked together for top-k. Selection is per GQA group (4 indexer heads, one per group, shared across the group's 16 query heads).

Within each stream, the four GQA groups are mapped onto the FA mask's ne[3] broadcast dimension and executed in one grouped flash-attention call.

- Batch (n_tokens_per_stream > 1, ie. prefill): a small CPU op turns block scores into a block-level 0/-inf mask, then the token-level expansion and combination with the causal mask happens on the GPU, and masked FA runs over the full cache views.

- Decode (1 token per stream): batched top_k on the GPU, index arithmetic expands block ids to flat (token, kv-head) row ids, one ggml_get_rows each gathers the selected K/V/mask, and FA runs over just the 2048 gathered tokens. 

Multi-stream (--parallel N) is supported whenever the KV cache is per-sequence (so kv_unified is false). In that configuration each stream's slots are then position-aligned, which MSA's slot-anchored block selection requires. 

The indexer also needs its own per-layer key cache. It is allocated F32 on the same backend buffer as the main K/V cache. Context-shift is not supported, since shifting would desynchronize the index cache.

### Requirements and fallbacks

- Flash attention required. Both batch and decode call ggml_flash_attn_ext directly and assume the non-transposed V layout that llama.cpp only provides with FA on. FA off uses dense build_attn (no sparsity) with a one-time warning that output quality may be degraded. 

- Unified KV cache with multiple sequences (--kv-unified + -np > 1) would silently break block anchoring so it also falls back to dense with a one-time warning. 

### Limitations

- Block selection is anchored to absolute KV slots. Erasing a prefix or middle of a sequence's history (llama_memory_seq_rm of a partial range) breaks selection silently. Removing whole sequences, trimming the suffix and reusing server slots is fine.
 
- Main KV cache: F16/BF16 are tested. Quantized KV-cache types are not yet validated.

### Quantization

Quants should keep the indexer projections (index_{q,k}_proj) at high precision(F32 ideally) since they drive block selection, so quant error there changes which blocks are read (a discrete retrieval loss), unlike a value projection. The cost is ~1 GB and these are some of the highest-value tensors in the model.

### Conversion

GGUFs must be converted with this branch and must keep the indexer tensors, weights with the indexers stripped will not work. 

### Performance

My tested config is expert-offload  bound.  MSA decode is essentially flat with context (7.7 tok/s at 5k -> 7.67 at 62k), prefill is roughly ~420-480 tok/s at 62k with -b and -ub 2048. Compute buffer at -ub 2048 / 62k ctx is ~4.6 GiB.

### How to test

As mentioned GGUFs converted with this PR are necessary, other's will fail to load. You can either convert one yourself, or you can use [this](https://huggingface.co/Serpen/Minimax-M3-MSA-GGUF/tree/main/Q4_K_M) Q4KM one (graciously provided by @AesSedai). 

CUDA build assumed (`-DGGML_CUDA=ON`), but in theory other backends with flash_attn_ext support for head-dim 128 should work (dense fallback otherwise), ROCm/HIP, Vulkan, Metal untested, reports welcome.

- Feed a ~4k and a ~30k+ prompt and generate. Decode throughput should stay roughly flat with context (fixed 2048-KV budget).

- Multi-stream: llama-server --parallel 2 (or 4) with concurrent requests of different prompt lengths.

### Credits

The initial MiniMax-M3 scaffolding was based on work by @danielhanchen. The sparse-attention indexer, the unified batch/decode MSA graphs, the KV-cache index handling, FA gating, and multi-stream support in this PR are new work.

## Requirements

<!-- IMPORTANT: Please do NOT delete this section, otherwise your PR may be rejected -->

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES, Claude Opus was used to help write the initial test code, was used to help debug a speed related issue concerning the allocation of the indexer cache, helped prototype the architecture of the current unified MSA graph implementation, assisted writing validation code, and further helped debug performance issues (compute-buffer sizing, graph reuse). <!-- mention: YES / NO - if yes, describe how AI was used -->

*Filed by Claude (Anthropic's assistant) on behalf of @elimisteve, who reviewed it before posting. All logs and line references were produced on his machine at commit `11924d4c1`. What I could not verify is stated explicitly below.*

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 547 (11924d4c1)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```
Commit `11924d4c17abc27383376a1ac6a24fa3e36c1c0c` (master, 2026-08-02).

### Operating systems

Linux (Xubuntu, kernel 6.14)

### GGML backends

CUDA (13.1), CPU

### Hardware

Intel Core i9-13950HX · 188 GiB DDR5 · NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada Generation Laptop GPU, 12 GB

### Models

`unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF`, `UD-Q4_K_XL` (native MXFP4 experts), 5 shards.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` fails to start on `deepseek4` with the **default** `-np -1` (auto), and starts
normally with an explicit `--parallel 1`. Nothing else differs.

Auto mode is an unconditional `n_parallel = 4, kv_unified = true`
(`tools/server/server.cpp:151`):

```cpp
if (params.n_parallel < 0) {
    params.n_parallel = 4;
    params.kv_unified = true;
}
```

Under `kv_unified`, `n_ctx_seq` is deliberately **not** divided
(`src/llama-context.cpp:287`):

```cpp
if (cparams.kv_unified) {
    cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx;      // 131072
} else {
    cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx / cparams.n_seq_max;
```

Both values reach the dsv4 cache (`src/llama-model.cpp:2259-2268`) — `cparams.kv_unified`
(true) and `cparams.n_ctx_seq` (undivided).

`llama_kv_cache_dsv4` then **discards the unified flag**
(`src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp:1041-1053`):

```cpp
GGML_UNUSED(unified);

// Keep DSV4 KV/state streams per sequence even when public KV mode is unified.
const bool unified_raw = false;

kv_raw = std::make_unique<llama_kv_cache_iswa>(
        model, hparams_raw, type_k, type_v,
        v_trans, offload, swa_full, unified_raw, kv_size, n_seq_max, n_ubatch, n_pad,
        nullptr, filter_raw, reuse, nullptr);
```

`kv_size` is the constructor parameter received at line 1021 and is forwarded here
unchanged — it is not divided anywhere in between. Downstream, `n_stream` becomes
`n_seq_max` (`src/llama-kv-cache.cpp:82`):

```cpp
n_seq_max(n_seq_max), n_stream(unified ? 1 : n_seq_max), ...
```

So dsv4 combines the **non-unified stream layout** (`n_stream = n_seq_max`) with the
**unified sizing** (`kv_size = n_ctx`, undivided). Each mode is self-consistent on its own —
unified is 1 stream × `n_ctx`; non-unified is `n_seq_max` streams × `n_ctx/n_seq_max` — but
the combination appears to allocate `n_seq_max` streams of the *full* context.

The comment on line 1043 suggests forcing per-sequence streams is intentional for this
architecture. If so, the sizing may need to compensate.

#### Reproduction

Fails (default `-np`):
```
llama-server -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00005.gguf \
  -ngl 999 --n-cpu-moe 43 --no-repack --load-mode mmap \
  --ctx-size 131072 -b 2048 -ub 512 -fa on -ctk f16 -t 8
```
```
E ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating 672.00 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E alloc_tensor_range: failed to allocate CUDA0 buffer of size 704643072
E llama_init_from_model: failed to initialize the context: failed to allocate buffer for kv cache
E srv  llama_server: exiting due to model loading error
```

Succeeds — only `--parallel 1` added:
```
llama-server -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00005.gguf \
  -ngl 999 --n-cpu-moe 43 --no-repack --load-mode mmap --parallel 1 \
  --ctx-size 131072 -b 2048 -ub 512 -fa on -ctk f16 -t 8
```

3/3 reproductions each way.

**Stronger isolation — `-ngl 0`**, which puts no model weights on the GPU at all and still
fails, at a much smaller context:

```
# -ngl 0 --ctx-size 32768, ~4.0 GiB free VRAM reported by nvidia-smi
default -np -1 : E ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer:
                 allocating 1290.30 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
--parallel 1   : I srv load_model: initializing, n_slots = 1, n_ctx_slot = 32768,
                 kv_unified = 'false'      -> starts normally
```

Note the failing 1290 MiB allocation is smaller than the ~4.0 GiB nvidia-smi reported free.
That figure is whole-GPU free memory with other resident processes (a browser compositor and
two small CUDA clients) on the same card, and it precedes the allocations this run had
already made, so it is not directly comparable to the failing request. The meaningful
comparison is the controlled one: same machine, same instant, same command, `--parallel 1`
succeeds and the default does not.

### What I could NOT verify

- **Exact byte counts.** The failing run aborts before printing the KV/compute breakdown, and
  this GPU has other resident consumers, so I have no clean side-by-side `KV self size`
  comparison. I am therefore **not** claiming a specific multiplier — only that the default
  path allocates enough more to fail where `--parallel 1` succeeds.
- **`--parallel 4` with `kv_unified = false`** (i.e. explicit `-np 4` rather than auto). That
  would separate "4 slots" from "unified sizing" as the cause. I could not run it in time;
  the code reading suggests it should succeed, since `n_ctx_seq` would then be divided. If a
  maintainer runs only one extra experiment, this is the one.
- Whether other architectures that similarly override `unified` are affected.
- Which fix is correct.

### Possible directions (untested — no PR proposed)

1. When the caller requested unified but dsv4 forces per-sequence streams, size each stream
   as `kv_size / n_seq_max` rather than `kv_size`.
2. Or mark `deepseek4` as incompatible with `kv_unified`, so `llama-context.cpp` takes the
   dividing branch and the existing non-unified math applies unchanged.

I have not built or benchmarked either, so I am not opening a PR.

### Workaround

Pass `--parallel 1` explicitly. This also leaves `kv_unified` at its `false` default, which
[#19523](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp
items.title: Eval bug: DeepSeek-V4 (deepseek4) fails to start on CUDA with the default -np -1 (auto) — dsv4 KV cache forces per-sequence streams while kv_unified leaves n_ctx undivided

### Name and Version Tested on two prebuilt gfx906 images: mixa3607/llama.cpp-gfx906:b10187-rocm-7.2.4-mxxm-9fa3fef mixa3607/llama.cpp-gfx906:b10207-rocm-7.2.4-9fa3fef ROCm 7.2.4. Note that llama-server --version on these images reports version: 1 (81a8712) — the fork stamps its own build number and commit, so the upstream base is identifiable only from the image tag (b10187 / b10207). Both builds reproduce identically. b10207 is ~20 upstream builds newer than b10187, so this is not a regression introduced in that window and not specific to the gfx906 fork. ### Operating systems Linux ### GGML backends HIP ### Hardware 6 × AMD Instinct MI50, gfx906:sramecc+:xnack- (0x66a1), 32 GiB each Uniform PCIe, 2 hops, all NUMA node 0, no XGMI Host: 8-core AMD CPU, 503 GiB RAM ### Models bartowski DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-MXFP4 — 4 shards, 145.63 GiB, 284.33 B params, arch deepseek4. Fully GPU-resident across all 6 cards. No CPU expert offload. deepseek4 is layer-split only on this backend (--split-mode tensor errors, row fails on gfx906). ### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Command line

llama-bench \
  -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-MXFP4-00001-of-00004.gguf \
  -ngl 999 -sm layer -mg 0 -ts 0.95/1.00/1.00/0.95/1.00/1.10 \
  -fa 1 -b 2048 -ub 2048 -t 8 -ctk f16 -ctv f16 \
  -p 512 -n 64 -d 2048,2560,3072,4096 -r 2

Environment: HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=9.0.6, HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5, ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0 (hipBLASLt ships no gfx906 Tensile kernels).

Problem description

Token generation is flat through depth 3072 and then collapses by 6.4× at depth 4096. Prompt processing degrades smoothly across the same range, with no corresponding discontinuity.

depth | pp512 (t/s) | tg64 (t/s) -- | -- | -- 2048 | 150.28 ± 14.07 | 15.61 ± 0.12 2560 | 150.93 ± 14.04 | 15.76 ± 0.16 3072 | 148.09 ± 12.95 | 15.78 ± 0.05 4096 | 123.67 ± 8.86 | 2.47 ± 0.03

Wider sweep (-p 2048 -n 128 -r 3) shows the post-cliff value is a flat floor rather than continuing decay: tg128 = 16.14 (d0), 16.11 (d1024), 15.68 (d2048), 2.38 (d4096), 2.32 (d8192). pp2048 over the same range: 231.86 → 215.43 → 210.03 → 170.97 → 153.94 → 129.58 (d16384), smooth throughout.

Confirmed on llama-server as well, not just llama-bench:

  • 6-token prompt → tg 16.09 t/s
  • 7001-token prompt → tg 2.37 t/s (pp 196.03 t/s, unaffected)

### Name and Version

Working:  build 8477 (ec2b787eb) with IntelLLVM 2025.2.1 — image built 2026-03-23
Broken:   server-intel latest — image built 2026-06-03 (~b9479)

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

SYCL

### Hardware

2× Intel Arc Pro B60 (24GB each, 46GB combined, PCIe discrete, no XeLink)
AMD Ryzen 7 7700 (host CPU)
64GB DDR5
Level Zero driver 1.15.38308+1
Both GPUs passed via /dev/dri to Docker container

### Models

Qwen3-Coder-Next UD-Q3_K_XL (33.79 GiB, arch=qwen3next) — CRASH on latest, FIXED on b8477
https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF

Qwen3-Coder-Next Q4_K_M (48.18 GiB, arch=qwen3next) — CRASH on latest, FIXED on b8477
https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF

Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M (15.65 GiB, arch=qwen35) — empty/gibberish content on latest, FIXED on b8477
https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-GGUF

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M (arch=qwen35) — empty/gibberish content on latest, FIXED on b8477
https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF

Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B Q4_K_M (arch=qwen3moe, pure attention) — UNAFFECTED on both builds

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Newer qwen models 3.5+ hybrid models were outputing mostly gibberish and crashing.  I've tested most of these models previously and they were working. Honestly thought I did something at first but then realized it was just an update I'm guessing.

Two related symptoms affect all hybrid architecture models (identifiable by 
ssm_d_conv / ssm_d_state / ssm_dt_rank fields in print_info) on Intel Arc Pro B60 
using server-intel latest (built 2026-06-03). Both are fixed by pinning to b8477.

SYMPTOM 1 - CRASH (qwen3next arch, e.g. Qwen3-Coder-Next):
Model loads fully into VRAM then crashes during warmup mul_mat on SSM/GDN weights.
crash at ggml_sycl_op_mul_mat line:3093.

SYMPTOM 2 - EMPTY/GIBBERISH OUTPUT (qwen35 arch, e.g. Qwen3.6-27B/35B):
Model loads and generates tokens but "content" field in API response is empty or 
contains number spam (e.g. 03129816571033482510583...). All output goes to 
"reasoning_content" as corrupted tokens. On b8477 the same models produce clean 
coherent output in "content".

IMPORTANT CONTEXT - why this is hard to diagnose:
server-intel is a rolling latest tag. Not sure when build/image broke but when I tried most recent build or 2026-06-03 get the broken build. Same 
image tag, completely different behavior depending on pull date. At one point I randomly tested Coder-Next about a week ago and although slow it worked. Now I randomly couldn't get any model 3.5 or above to work without gibberish outputs .... Coder-Next had been working in earlier sessions, then 
silently broke when the image updated i'm guessing, I just can't pinpoint when, unless this is known already.

Pure attention MoE models (qwen3moe arch, no SSM layers) are completely unaffected 
on both builds and work correctly throughout.

Steps to reproduce (using Docker):

1. Pull latest server-intel:
   docker pull ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-intel

2. Run with dual Arc Pro B60:

   docker run --rm \
     --device /dev/dri:/dev/dri \
     --group-add 993 --group-add 44 \
     -e ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0;level_zero:1 \
     -e ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=1 \
     -e UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1 \
     -e GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_LEVEL_ZERO=1 \
     -e GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_VMM=1 \
     -e GGML_SYCL_DISABLE_GRAPH=1 \
     -p 8010:8010 \
     ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-intel \
     --model /models/Qwen3-Coder-Next-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf \
     --ctx-size 8192 \
     --host 0.0.0.0 \
     --port 8010 \
     -ngl 999 \
     --split-mode layer \
     --tensor-split 1,1 \
     --flash-attn off \
     --threads 1

3. For qwen3next: crash during warmup at ggml_sycl_op_mul_mat line:3093
   For qwen35: server starts, responds, but content field is empty or number spam

4. Replace image with server-intel-b8477 — identical command — both symptoms fixed

---

Side note for Ollama SYCL users:

This same regression affects users of https://github.com/eleiton/ollama-intel-arc
— an excellent community-maintained project providing native SYCL Ollama builds 
for Intel Arc GPUs. It is not a bug in that project. Ollama 0.30.2 pins 
LLAMA_CPP_VERSION=b9479 (confirmed via 
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/v0.30.2/LLAMA_CPP_VERSION) which 
pulls the broken llama.cpp commit via FetchContent at build time.

Workaround: add this to ollama-sycl/Dockerfile after WORKDIR /ollama, then rebuild:

    RUN echo "ec2b787eb" > LLAMA_CPP_VERSION

Once this regression is fixed in llama.cpp master, Ollama SYCL builds will 
automatically pick up the fix.

### First Bad Commit

Working: server-intel-b8477 (ec2b787eb), image built 2026-03-23
Broken:  server-intel latest (~b9479), image built 2026-06-03

Regression window: somewhere between 2026-03-23 and 2026-06-03.
llama.cpp ships multiple builds per day so this window contains 
hundreds of commits. Have not bisected further.

A git bisect focusing on changes to ggml/src/ggml-sycl/ggml-sycl.cpp 
around the ggml_sycl_op_mul_mat function (line ~3093 in broken build) 
would likely narrow it down quickly.

Related: #21474 (same crash class on iGPU/Meteor Lake — that reporter 
also identified b8477 as working)  I just used this image to see if it would work, and it did!

items.body:
## Bug Description

Gemma 4 models generate an infinite stream of `<unused>` tokens (Token ID 14 = `<unused8>`) on the **Vulkan backend**, both with GPU offloading and CPU-only. No valid text is produced — the model runs until MaxTokens is exhausted.

This happens **despite** having all known Gemma 4 fixes applied:
- Tokenizer fix (#21343)
- Template parser fix (#21326)
- Custom newline split (#21406)
- Byte token handling (#21488)
- Logit softcapping (#21390)
- **Plus** the F32 MoE precision patch from PR #21506 (manually applied)

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26100)
- **GPU:** NVIDIA (24 GB VRAM), Vulkan backend
- **llama.cpp:** Built from `94ca829b6` (master, 2026-04-06) + PR #21506 patch
- **Model:** `gemma-4-E2B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf` from [unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF)
- **Build:** CMake + MSVC + `GGML_VULKAN=ON`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build llama.cpp from current master with Vulkan enabled
2. Load `gemma-4-E2B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf` with `-ngl 99`
3. Send any prompt (e.g., "Hello")
4. Observe: model generates ~18000+ tokens of `<unused8>` (token id=14) without producing any readable text or hitting EOG

## Diagnostic Data

Token sampling output (first 10 tokens):
```
Token[0] id=14
Token[1] id=14
Token[2] id=14
Token[3] id=14
Token[4] id=14
Token[5] id=14
Token[6] id=14
Token[7] id=14
Token[8] id=14
Token[9] id=14
```

Token 14 in Gemma 4 vocab = `<unused8>`.

Generation stats: 183 tok/s, 18432 tokens generated, 44.7 seconds — no EOG token emitted.

## Additional Testing

- **CPU-only (`-ngl 0`):** Same result — generates `[multimodal]` tokens (id=5) in an infinite loop. Also broken.
- **PR #21506 applied (F32 MoE FFN precision):** No improvement on either CPU or Vulkan.
- **Ollama:** Same model works correctly in Ollama (which uses its own llama.cpp fork), producing valid responses.

## Init Logs (successful)

```
Model handle: OK
Vocab size: 262144
Layers: 35
Context size: 32768
Gemma tokens: start_of_turn=105, end_of_turn=106, bos=2
System tokens: 11
Initialization complete!
```

Model loads correctly, context/sampler/batch all initialized — the issue is purely in inference/sampling.

## Related Issues

- #21321 — Gemma 4 generates `<unused24>` tokens (CUDA, partially fixed by #21506)
- #21343 — Gemma 4 tokenizer fix (merged, applied here)
- #21506 — F32 MoE precision (open, manually applied, does not fix this)

The root cause may be Vulkan-specific numerical precision issues beyond what #21506 addresses, or a different code path in the Vulkan compute shaders.

items.body:
There are several issues about abnormal output in multiple GPUs case, like: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/23612. After disable dev2dev memcpy by L0 API, all issues disappear. This PR is used to fix them. This PR use SYCL API to implement dev2dev memcpy directly for dGPU+dGPU case. It should be quicker than host forward mode, and has same performance of L0 API as the test result. For iGPU+dGPU case, still use host forward mode. Add running time environment variable GGML_SYCL_DEV2DEV_MEMCPY to choose the SYCL or L0 API in dev2dev memory copy. Value:
* 0: SYCL API (default)
* 1: L0 API -- L0 API is found to lead to abnormal crash in some case. This debug flag is used to check the issue. ### Name and Version

version: 9607 (6471e3c0)

### Operating systems

Mac

### GGML backends

Metal

### Hardware

Apple M1 Pro, 16 GB unified memory

### Models

Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, Q8_0 (~30 GB GGUF).
Reproduces with any GGUF that stores output.weight near the file start while the
offloaded transformer blocks are near the end.


### Problem description & steps to reproduce

On Metal, partial offload (`-ngl N`) maps a backend's weights as a single mmap region
spanning `[min_offset, max_offset]` over all tensors assigned to that backend
(`get_mapping_range` -> `ggml_backend_dev_buffer_from_host_ptr`). This assumes the
offloaded tensors are contiguous in the file.

`-ngl N` offloads the output layer plus the top N-1 blocks. If a GGUF stores
`output.weight` at the file start while the top block is at the file end, those two land
in the same Metal context, so the mapped span becomes the entire model file.

Concretely, with such a GGUF, `-ngl 2` offloads 2/49 layers (~947 MiB of weights) but maps
`MTL0_Mapped model buffer size = 30973 MiB` — the whole 30 GB file. This over-allocation
is deterministic (printed at every load, independent of free RAM) and overflows
`recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize`. On a machine where RAM < model size it then OOMs at decode.

Steps to reproduce (current master, version 9607 / 6471e3c0):

    llama-completion -m Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-Q8_0.gguf -ngl 2 -fit off -v -p "hi" -n 1

In the load log, compare `offloaded N/49 layers` with `MTL0_Mapped model buffer size`.
(`-fit off` pins `-ngl 2` exactly — the auto-fit estimator accounts for the ~947 MiB of
GPU tensors, not the 31 GB mapped span.)

Controlled check — only variable is tensor order: rewriting the GGUF to move
`output_norm.weight` + `output.weight` to the end (loss-less; tensors are looked up by
name) makes the offload set a contiguous file suffix, and `MTL0_Mapped` drops from
30973 MiB to 947 MiB with no working-set warnings and a clean decode:

| load_tensors, -ngl 2          | output.weight first | output.weight last |
|-------------------------------|---------------------|--------------------|
| offloaded                     | 2/49 layers         | 2/49 layers        |
| MTL0_Mapped model buffer size | 30973 MiB           | 947 MiB            |
| allocated > working set warns | 3                   | 0                  |
| outcome                       | OOM at decode       | decodes cleanly    |

The OOM is pressure-dependent (with the default n_ctx=262144 the CPU KV cache is 24 GB,
which together with the 31 GB Metal span exceeds 16 GB RAM; a small -c sometimes survives),
but the 30973 MiB over-allocation is deterministic.

Root cause:
- `llama_model_loader::get_mapping_range` (src/llama-model-loader.cpp) returns a single
  [first,last] = [min(offs), max(offs+nbytes)] over all tensors in a backend context.
- `llama_model::load_tensors` (src/llama-model.cpp) maps that one span via
  `ggml_backend_dev_buffer_from_host_ptr(dev, addr+first, last-first, max_size)`. The
  comment there says it maps "only the mmap region containing the tensors" but assumes
  contiguity.
- On Metal the buffer is added to an MTLResidencySet and made resident, so the whole span
  is wired.

Suggested fix: in load_tensors, split into one backend buffer per contiguous run of tensor
offsets within the context (instead of a single [first,last] span). `-ngl 2` would then map
~947 MiB instead of ~31 GB.


### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. This is not a recent regression — the single-[min,max]-span mapping in
get_mapping_range is long-standing. Confirmed present on current master (6471e3c0).


### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>

```console
$ llama-completion -m Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-Q8_0.gguf -ngl 2 -fit off -v -p "hi" -n 1
# ---- output.weight FIRST (stock GGUF) ----
load_tensors: offloading 1 repeating layers to GPU
load_tensors: offloaded 2/49 layers to GPU
load_tensors:   CPU_Mapped model buffer size = 29821.95 MiB
load_tensors:  MTL0_Mapped model buffer size = 30973.40 MiB
ggml_metal_log_allocated_size: allocated buffer, size = 9093.12 MiB, ( 9093.50 / 12124.17)
ggml_metal_log_allocated_size: allocated buffer, size = 9093.12 MiB, (18186.62 / 12124.17)
ggml_metal_log_allocated_size: warning: current allocated size is greater than the recommended max working set size
ggml_metal_log_allocated_size: allocated buffer, size = 9093.12 MiB, (27279.75 / 12124.17)
ggml_metal_log_allocated_size: warning: current allocated size is greater than the recommended max working set size
ggml_metal_log_allocated_size: allocated buffer, size = 4639.97 MiB, (31919.72 / 12124.17)

error: Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3

# ---- output.weight LAST (reordered, loss-less) ----
load_tensors: offloaded 2/49 layers to GPU
load_tensors:   CPU_Mapped model buffer size = 29821.95 MiB
load_tensors:  MTL0_Mapped model buffer size =   947.45 MiB
ggml_metal_log_allocated_size: allocated buffer, size =  947.45 MiB, (  947.83 / 12124.17)

### Name and Version

version: 8724 (b54cb2e3d)
built with Clang 19.1.5 for Windows x86_64

### Operating systems

Windows, Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA 12, CUDA 13, Vulkan

### Hardware

1x RTX3090 24GB 
AMD Ryzen 5 3.6Ghz (6 core) + 64GB RAM

Multiple other hardware configurations.

### Models

Gemma4
https://huggingface.co/llmfan46/gemma-4-31B-it-uncensored-heretic-GGUF/

Tried many others.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

**REVISED ISSUE** (see previous edits for history)

With Gemma 4 models (any variant), *and Gemma 4 only*, checkpoints (ctx-checkpoints) on llama-server are consuming enormous (and increasing) amounts of RAM, to a point that on a machine with 64GB of RAM (and 24GB of VRAM), the entirety of the RAM space can be reached in 4 to 5 full prompt processing of about 16K tokens each. Each generation is making llama-server's RAM consumption bump by several gigabytes.

**Workaround:** Setting "--ctx-checkpoints" to 1 or 0 with "-np 1" will prevent the server from going out of RAM.

Something notable beyond the OOM issue, is that the memory usage will be different right from the start.

**Examples of memory usage with the settings below on a Q4_K_M GGUF**
````
-fa on -kvo -ngl 255 -c 16384 --mmap -m "location/model.gguf" --nowebui
````

| ctx-checkpoints | VRAM (start) | RAM (start) | RAM (1st gen) | RAM (2nd gen) |  RAM (after 3rd gen) | 
|-------------------|---------------|--------------|---------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| (defaults) | 23.6 / 24 GB | 0.7GB (+ file) |  10GB  (+ file) | 18GB (+ file) | OOM (>25GB + File) |
| set to 1 + np 1 | 21.6 / 24 GB | 0.7GB (+ file) |   1.5GB (+ file) | 1.5GB (+ file) | 1.5GB (+ file) |
| set to 0 + np 1 | 21.6 / 24 GB | 0.4GB (+ file) |   0.4GB (+ file) | 0.4GB (+ file) | 0.4GB (+ file) |

*(each generation is a different 16K tokens long chatlog sent for text or chat completion processing to the server)*

**Notes:**
- The "-np" setting seems to have a multiplicative value to the consumed VRAM. The higher, the more RAM is used. 
- The "-cram" flag doesn't seem to have any impact either way (set or unset, same values)
- The server behaves normally with other architectures (test Qwen 3.5 and Mistral)

### First Bad Commit

At least since b8660. Bug is consistent since the initial implementation of Gemma 4.

## Overview

**Co-authors:** @jxia4intel, @sliu39

**PR 2/3** of the Intel Xe optimization series — see https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24408 (mega PR, draft) for the full feature set.

**Target platforms:** Xe-LPG Plus, Xe2, Xe3

This PR adds Intel Xe-specific flash attention optimization kernels for both ARLH iGPU (Xe1, UMA, coopmat1) and Xe2/Xe3. Dependency: builds on top of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24404 (Xe-LPG Plus coopmat1 enable). Independent of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24407 (GEMM+CW).

### Flash Attention (Intel Xe)

- New Vulkan shaders: single-phase prefill (`flash_attn_hdim64/96/128`) and two-phase split prefill/decode variants
- Pipelines keyed by `(head_dim, gqa_ratio)` for runtime dispatch across various GQA ratios without combinatorial pipeline proliferation
- Supports non-power-of-two GQA ratios via subgroup splitting (`qk_groups`)
- Intel Xe1 (integrated GPU, UMA, cooperative matrix) and Xe2 paths with separate warptile tuning
- Two-phase decode splits softmax reduction across subgroups; shared QK state copy (`fa_copy_qstate`) between prefill phases

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

### Summary

A ROCm RPC worker on AMD gfx1151 aborts in `GGML_OP_TOP_K` while processing a sufficiently long DeepSeek V4 Flash prompt.

Short requests work correctly.

A long request consistently reaches exactly 4096 processed prompt tokens and then causes the remote ROCm RPC worker to abort with:

```text
ggml_cuda_compute_forward: TOP_K failed
ROCm error: invalid configuration argument
```

The client then reports:

```text
Remote RPC server crashed or returned malformed response
recv failed (bytes_recv=0, size_to_recv=8)
```

This is reproducible on both:

```text
TheRock / ROCm 7.13.0
TheRock / ROCm 7.14.0
```

using the same llama.cpp commit:

```text
3653e6d6d
```

Replacing only the remote ROCm RPC worker with a Vulkan/RADV RPC worker on the exact same Radeon 8060S / gfx1151 hardware makes the same setup stable.

Vulkan is significantly slower, but it does not crash.

### Difference from #24177

This appears related to #24177 because both failures involve the AMD `TOP_K` path and an RPC worker abort.

However, this case is different:

- `--no-spec-draft-backend-sampling` is already enabled.
- The failure occurs during prompt prefill, not draft-token backend sampling.
- Short prompts work.
- Long prompts reproducibly fail after 4096 processed prompt tokens.
- Reducing `--ubatch-size` from 256 to 128 does not change the failure point.
- Switching only the RPC worker backend from ROCm to Vulkan avoids the crash.

Therefore, the `--no-spec-draft-backend-sampling` workaround from #24177 does not avoid this failure.

### Server command

```bash

  --no-spec-draft-backend-sampling \
  --spec-draft-type-v q8_0 \
  --temp 1.0 \
  --top-p 0.95 \
  --min-p 0.0 \
  --top-k 0 \
  --spec-type draft-dspark \
  --model-draft /opt/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/UD-IQ3_XXS/dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf \
  --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
  --batch-size 1024 \
  --ubatch-size 128 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --flash-attn on \
  --port 5800
```

Remote worker:

```bash
ggml-rpc-server \
  --host 10.44.0.2 \
  --port 50053 \
  --device ROCm0
```

### Reproduction

1. Start a ROCm `ggml-rpc-server` on the gfx1151 remote system.
2. Start `llama-server` with the command above.
3. Send a short chat request.
4. The short request completes normally.
5. Send a long chat request containing approximately 18k prompt tokens.
6. Prompt processing proceeds normally:

```text
prompt processing, n_tokens = 1024, progress = 0.06
prompt processing, n_tokens = 2048, progress = 0.11
prompt processing, n_tokens = 3072, progress = 0.17
prompt processing, n_tokens = 4096, progress = 0.22
```

7. Immediately after the 4096-token point, the remote ROCm RPC worker aborts.

Changing:

```text
--ubatch-size 256
```

to:

```text
--ubatch-size 128
```

does not change the behavior.

Both fail after 4096 processed prompt tokens.

## Control tests

### Short prompt, ROCm RPC

Works correctly.

Example successful request:

```text

Does not crash.

Only the remote worker backend was changed:

items.body:
## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

this adds several fixes for rpc and rocm related GPU paths additional tuning and fixes crashes, prefill issues and general compatibility. Fixes #26746

### Included changes relative to upstream

#### HIP, RPC and long-context routing

- Enables hipCUB for HIP top-k and argsort, including the distributed RPC execution
  path, so these operations remain GPU-capable on ROCm.
- Adds a gfx1151-local Lightning Indexer top-k specialization for 512, 1024 and 2048
  candidates up to 8192 score entries, avoiding the expensive generic device-wide sort
  during DeepSeek-V4 long-context prefill.
- Keeps the Lightning Indexer key cache in F16 when a quantized KV cache is selected,
  where required by the DeepSeek path.
- Resolves fused operations per layer and device instead of disabling an entire graph
  on a single ROCm/RPC backend mismatch; the default fallback remains unfused GPU work,
  not CPU work.
- Fixes the HIP MMVF dispatch for MoE LoRA `MUL_MAT_ID` tensors. Rank-1 LoRA-B
  expert matrices now use the existing general GPU fallback instead of entering an
  MMVF kernel which requires an even K dimension; this prevents RPC worker crashes
  with valid DeepSeek-V4 expert LoRA adapters.

#### Strix Halo compute tuning

- Adds RDNA3.5/gfx1151 kernel and launch tuning for MMQ, MMVQ, Q8 MoE and expert MMQ.
- Caches MMVQ Q8_1 activations and partitions MMQ waves across rows and columns.
- Adds AMD WMMA Lightning Indexer support and tuned tiled Flash Attention, including a
  fix for NaNs in the compacted-tile mask path.
- Tunes Gated Delta Net and adds quantized-KV Flash Attention support for Strix Halo.
- Extends the gfx1151 MMVQ selection to the relevant Q4/Q5/Q6/Q8 and MXFP4 decode
  types, including the Q6_K VDR=2 decode kernel.
- Keeps HIP integrated-GPU host-buffer handling safe.

#### DeepSeek-V4 and speculative decoding

- Makes the grouped output-projection input contiguous for small multi-token
  DeepSeek-V4 speculative batches.
- Uses matching MMVQ and Flash-Attention kernel configurations for decode and small
  speculative/MTP verification batches, preventing numerical divergence between the
  logits used for acceptance checks.
- Keeps fused DeepSeek-V4 HC and Gated Delta Net operations on devices that support
  them while safely falling back only for mismatching layers.

#### Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 and hybrid SSM models

- Fuses SSM gate/beta projections, the SSM convolution-output L2 norm, and the SSM
  pre-scan chain (convolution, L2 norm, gate/beta).
- Folds SSM convolution-input concatenation into QKV MMVQ and fuses paired MMVQ
  matmuls that share an activation.
- Caches graph-local Q8_1 matmul inputs, folds Q8_1 quantization into RMS norm and
  gating-MUL, and fuses a matmul-plus-add-through-view sequence.
- Folds MoE top-k weights into the down projection and fuses the shared-expert output
  chain.
- Fuses IMRoPE and set-rows for BF16 KV cache use, and aligns the attention-gate
  tensor-parallel split with attention-Q.

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

tested on a halo strix cluster setup (RPC, rocm 7.14).

## Requirements

rocm 7.14, hipcub-dev (build requirements)
ROCm/HIP with hipCUB, HIP/ROCm >= 6.1.
Build for gfx1151 (-DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151).

- AI usage disclosure: <!-- mention: YES / NO - if yes, describe how AI was used --> YES

OpenAI Codex GPT 5.6 Terra for tracing affected crash paths. Adding GPU fallback, instead of adding CPU fallback.

### Sources and provenance

- [@ggml-org](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) provides the upstream base. This
  branch is rebased on the exact upstream commit stated above.
- [@Patt92](https://github.com/Patt92/llama.cpp) maintains this integration branch and
  supplies the HIP RPC top-k/argsort patch, including the current HIP-only rank-1 MoE
  LoRA MMVF dispatch fix.
- [@Geramy](https://github.com/Geramy/llama.cpp) is the provenance for the original
  hipCUB/CUB-on-HIP top-k and argsort approach. Its useful HIP content was rebased
  into the Patt92 RPC patch; no older branch is required at build time.
- [@Nathanw1014](https://github.com/Nathanw1014/llama.cpp) supplies the selected
  Strix Halo/RDNA3.5 HIP tuning, DeepSeek-V4, Flash-Attention, MMQ/MMVQ and
  backend-neutral fused-op work. Vulkan-only implementation code is excluded.
- [@antirez](https://github.com/antirez/ds4) is the algorithmic source for the
  gfx1151-local Lightning Indexer top-k adaptation. Only the compatible HIP
  specialization is used; ds4 runtime, model and storage code is not included.
- [@stew675](https://github.com/stew675/llama.cpp) supplies the selected
  ROCm-compatible Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 and hybrid-SSM fusions, MMVQ tuning and
  speculative decode/verification consistency fixes.

### Name and Version

    $ llama-server --version
    version: 0.1.0-dev (build 10423, commit a94d563ed)
    built with IntelLLVM 2026.1.1 for Linux x86_64

Also reproduces on build 10289 (f9e832c10) and build 10050 (b15ca938a, 2026-07-16) — see comments below. This is not a new regression in 10423; it predates that build by at least a month and 10423 does not fix it.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

SYCL

### Hardware

Intel Core Ultra 7 258V (Lunar Lake), integrated Arc 140V graphics (Xe2-LPG), UMA (no discrete VRAM, 32 GB shared).

    $ llama-server --list-devices
    Available devices:
      SYCL0: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics (29223 MiB, 22596 MiB free)

oneAPI 2026.1.1, `xe` kernel driver, Ubuntu 24.04.

### Models

Reproduces on multiple, architecturally unrelated models — this does not look specific to any one architecture:

- `gemma4-v2` (gemma4 arch, both Q4_K_M and Q6_K quants)
- `gemma-4-12B-coder-fable5-composer2.5-v1.i1-IQ4_NL` (gemma4 arch)
- `Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-Q6_K` (qwen2 arch — plain dense model, no MoE, no known relation to DeepSeek/Gated-Delta-Net/Lightning-Indexer)

None of these are DeepSeek-V4 or Qwen3-Next/qwen35moe models, yet the crash is immediately preceded by `resolve_fused_ops` reporting several DeepSeek-V4/Gated-Delta-Net/Lightning-Indexer fused ops as **enabled** (not "not supported, set to disabled" as seen on other SYCL hardware in #26549).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` segfaults on the **first graph execution** (the built-in warmup pass, or the first real request if `--no-warmup` is used) whenever any GPU layers are offloaded (`-ngl` > 0), on this Lunar Lake iGPU. Model loading, tokenizer setup, and graph *reservation* (buffer sizing) all complete successfully — the crash is specifically in *executing* the compute graph, not building or sizing it.

`-ngl 0` (CPU-only, same model, same flags otherwise) loads and serves correctly, which rules out a corrupt GGUF or a general metadata-parsing bug and narrows this to the SYCL execution path.

Minimal repro (no server-side overrides, no third-party wrapper):

```shell
llama-server \
  -m gemma4-v2-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  -ngl 999 -c 2048 -t 4 -fa on \
  -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 \
  --port 8080 -lv 5
```

Isolation steps taken, none of which prevented the crash:
- `--fit off` (rules out the new auto-fit-to-device-memory feature)
- `--flash-attn off`
- `--no-warmup` (only moves the crash to the first real `/v1/chat/completions` request instead of the synthetic warmup)
- `GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_FUSION=0` (does not suppress the `resolve_fused_ops` messages below — that env var appears to gate a different, lower-level set of SYCL kernel fusions, not this graph-level pass)
- Reducing `-c` from 65536 down to 2048
- Confirmed with `dmesg`/`journalctl`, not just the process exit code:
  ```
  llama-server[86943]: segfault at 0 ip 0000000000000000 sp 00007ffd6a4b11b8 error 14 likely on CPU 3 (core 12, socket 0)
  ```
  `ip 0000000000000000` — a jump through a null function pointer — on every occurrence, across both builds and all three models above.

Only `-ngl 0` avoids it.

### First Bad Commit

**`5511965b197c131b38d8b5a0beb3ea7606d80b10`** — "sycl: route small f32 matmuls to oneMKL, bypass oneDNN" (#22150), merged 2026-05-18. First bad tag: **b9208**. Confirmed by tag-level then commit-level binary search down to a single-commit range (`e98bcfec2..5511965b1`) — see comments for the full trail and an explanation of why the diff produces exactly this symptom. items.body:
## Summary
On the Vulkan backend, Qwen3.5-27B (architecture qwen35, hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full-attention layers) generates garbage / truncated output when the batch size is set to 512. The same model and configuration generate correct, coherent text at batch sizes 1024 and 4096.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11 (build 26200)
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (24 GB), AMD proprietary driver
- Backend: Vulkan
- Software: koboldcpp 1.119 (nocuda build, Vulkan backend) which bundles the llama.cpp Vulkan backend. The underlying kernel issue appears to be in ggml-vulkan.

## Model
- Architecture: qwen35 (Gated DeltaNet / linear-attention hybrid, full_attention_interval = 4, 3x DeltaNet + 1x full-attention per group, ssm state_size 128)
- GGUFs tested: Q4_K_M and Q6_K_M quantizations of Qwen3.5-27B, including a variant carrying the built-in MTP/NextN head
- Context: reproduced at both 32768 and 262144

## Repro steps
1. Load the model with the Vulkan backend.
2. Set batch size to 512 (llama.cpp: -b 512; koboldcpp: batchsize=512), ubatch 512.
3. Send a simple generation request (e.g. 'Write a short poem about the ocean.').
4. Observe output: random token fragments / garbage, or generation stops after 1-2 tokens (e.g. 'The.') with an early EOS.

With batch size 1024 or 4096 the same request produces normal coherent output.

## Notes
- MMQ disabled; Flash Attention on/off both reproduce the issue.
- KV cache f16 and q8_0 both reproduce the issue.
- MTP drafting on/off both reproduce the issue.
- The symptom pattern points at the Gated Delta Net kernel path selection: at small batch the autoregressive (non-chunked) path corrupts the logits, while at larger batch the chunked/fused path works correctly.
- Related: #20610 (Qwen3.5-27B garbage on Vulkan), #21888, #24812, #20515.

## Expected behavior
Output quality should be independent of batch size.
items.title: [Vulkan] Qwen3.5-27B (qwen35 hybrid DeltaNet) garbage output at batch size 512; OK at 1024/4096

items.body:
## Summary

On a Radeon Vega 8 iGPU (`gfx90c`, GCN), updating the AMD driver from 2023 to Adrenalin 26.5.2 changes the reported `VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::maxComputeSharedMemorySize` from **65536 to 32768**, with no other reported device capability changing. This costs ~17% throughput in Vulkan diffusion workloads.

Rolling the driver back restores performance exactly, and generated outputs are **byte-identical** across driver states — so this is purely a shader-selection/tuning effect, not a numerical one.

I'm filing here because `ggml-vulkan.cpp` contains an **exact-equality** gate on `65536` that looks like it may be unintentionally fragile.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | AMD Radeon Vega 8 iGPU, `gfx90c`, GCN, integrated/UMA |
| CPU | Ryzen 7 5800H, 8C/16T |
| RAM | 29 GB (3 GB UMA carve-out) |
| OS | Windows 11 Pro 26200 |
| Frontend | `stable-diffusion.cpp` master-796-2d0385b, prebuilt `win-vulkan-x64` |

`stable-diffusion.cpp` vendors ggml via the `leejet/ggml` fork at commit `eced84c86f8b012c752c016f7fe789adea168e1e`. I diffed the relevant block against `ggml-org/llama.cpp` master and it is **character-identical**, so this is not a fork divergence.

ggml device line on the **old** driver:

```
ggml_vulkan: 0 = AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics (AMD proprietary driver) | uma: 1 | fp16: 1 | bf16: 0 | warp size: 64 | shared memory: 65536 | int dot: 0 | matrix cores: none
```

On the **new** driver — only `shared memory` differs:

```
ggml_vulkan: 0 = AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics (AMD proprietary driver) | uma: 1 | fp16: 1 | bf16: 0 | warp size: 64 | shared memory: 32768 | int dot: 0 | matrix cores: none
```

| | old (OEM) | new |
|---|---|---|
| Driver | 31.0.12027.9001 (2023-03-29) | 31.0.21925.1001 (2026-05-19) |
| Adrenalin | 22.20.27.09 | 26.5.2 (Vega/Polaris legacy branch) |
| Vulkan API | 1.3.217 | 1.3.260 |

Vega hardware has 64 KB LDS per CU, so the 65536 report appears to be the physically correct one. 26.5.2 is the package AMD's own Ryzen 7 5800H support page serves, so this is not a mismatched driver.

## Measurements

Both runs were the first job after a reboot, preceded only by the SD1.5 job, so pipeline-cache and thermal state are matched. Same seed (42), prompts, steps, resolution and flags throughout.

**SD1.5, 512x512, 20 steps** (no flash attention)

| | shmem 32768 | shmem 65536 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| sampling | 80.12 s | 68.48 s | **−14.5%** |
| VAE decode | 6.84 s | 5.99 s | −12.4% |
| total | 88.42 s | 75.17 s | **−15.0%** |

**SDXL 1024x1024, 30 steps** (`--diffusion-fa --auto-fit --vae-tiling --offload-to-cpu`)

| | shmem 32768 | shmem 65536 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| text encode | 2.79 s | 2.68 s | −3.9% |
| sampling | 834.78 s | 696.14 s | **−16.6%** |
| VAE decode | 79.50 s | 65.63 s | **−17.4%** |
| total | 917.14 s | 764.53 s | **−16.6%** |

Output PNGs are byte-identical between driver states (SHA256 `BBEA8144...`, 1,907,961 bytes) — identical math, just slower.

The regression magnitude tracks how LDS-dependent each stage is: **VAE decode > sampling > text encode.**

## Suspected code paths

Line numbers below are from the vendored copy (`leejet/ggml@eced84c`, `src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp`); llama.cpp master has the same code at a different offset.

### 1. Exact-equality gate — the reason I'm filing (L3322)

```cpp
// On AMD RDNA, for small head sizes and big batch size the shader uses few registers, so too many subgroups get scheduled
// at once and end up thrashing the cache. Fix this by setting a large (unused) shmem buffer that reduces occupancy.
// This targets an occupancy of 4 subgroups per SIMD.
if (device->vendor_id == VK_VENDOR_ID_AMD && device->properties.limits.maxComputeSharedMemorySize == 65536) {
    if (device->architecture != AMD_GCN && n_rows >= 64 && hsk <= 128) {
        // 30kb target for hsk > 64, 26kb for <= 64 due to smaller workgroup size
        // Values are guessed, tested on RDNA2
        result.limit_occupancy_shmem = (hsk <= 64 ? 26 : 30) * 1024 / 4 / 4;
    } else if (device->architecture == AMD_GCN && n_rows <= 8 && hsk >= 256) {
        // Same thing for GCN, with an occupancy target of 2 subgroups per SIMD.
        // Here low-batch FA with large head size is affected.
        // n_rows < 4 switch because workgroup size switches from 128 to 256 there.
        result.limit_occupancy_shmem = (n_rows < 4 ? 14 : 26) * 1024 / 4 / 4;
    }
}
```

`== 65536`, not `>=`. The block has an explicit `AMD_GCN` branch, so Vega is clearly in scope — but any AMD device whose driver reports something other than exactly 65536 silently loses the occupancy tuning.

### 2. Shader-variant support checks (L3535, L3599, L10029, L10074)

```cpp
const bool supported = total_size <= device->properties.limits.maxComputeSharedMemorySize;
```

### 3. Division-derived batch sizing (L5265, L17468)

```cpp
const uint32_t batch_N = device->properties.limits.maxComputeSharedMemorySize / ((N + K) * sizeof(float));
```

### 4. conv2d path selection (L5450, L5483)

The cm1 and padded-shmem variants are disabled when the budget is too small. This is the best candidate for the outsized VAE-decode regression.

Items 2–4 are legitimate correctness checks — if the driver genuinely only permits 32 KB, they must hold. The open questions are whether the driver's report is accurate for Vega, and separately whether item 1 should tolerate values other than exactly 65536.

## Questions

1. Is the `== 65536` in the AMD FA tuning path intentional, or should it be a threshold comparison (`>= 65536`)?
2. Is there an existing escape hatch (env var / build flag) to override the shared-memory limit ggml-vulkan uses, for testing? I could not find one.
3. Has anyone reproduced a similar regression in **llama.cpp** proper on Polaris/Vega with Adrenalin 26.5.2? I only tested diffusion workloads; if LLM inference is affected too, the blast radius is much wider.

## Caveats

- Single machine, one sample per configuration.
- I have not built a patched binary to confirm caus
